path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws›Western State Psychiatric Institute and Clinic›Establishment›PA ST 50 P.S. § 569. Acquisition of site; preliminary survey and plans
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws › Western State Psychiatric Institute and Clinic › Establishment › PA ST 50 P.S. § 569. Acquisition of site; preliminary survey and plans
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 569. Acquisition of site; preliminary survey and plans (2023)
content:
The Department of Property and Supplies1is hereby authorized to acquire in the name of the Commonwealth, by gift from the
   University of Pittsburgh, a suitable site for a Western State Psychiatric Institute
   and Clinic on the campus of or in the neighborhood of the University of Pittsburgh.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws›Western State Psychiatric Institute and Clinic›Purpose and Management›PA ST 50 P.S. § 575.3. Medical Advisory Board
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws › Western State Psychiatric Institute and Clinic › Purpose and Management › PA ST 50 P.S. § 575.3. Medical Advisory Board
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 575.3. Medical Advisory Board (2023)
content:
In addition to the Board of Trustees hereinbefore provided for, such institution shall
   have a medical advisory board, the duty of which shall be to submit policy recommendations
   relative to the treatment and cure of persons admitted to the same for treatment,
   and recommend anything necessary to carry out the purposes of the institute, as hereinbefore

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws›Establishment›PA ST 50 P.S. § 571. Conveyance of site to General State Authority; lease of property; management and operation by Department of Welfare
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws › Establishment › PA ST 50 P.S. § 571. Conveyance of site to General State Authority; lease of property; management and operation by Department of Welfare
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 571. Conveyance of site to General State Authority; lease of property; management and operation by Department of Welfare (2023)
content:
In lieu of procedure by the Department of Property and Supplies1for obtaining and paying for preliminary surveys, plans, and estimates for the construction
   of the said hospital, and the improvement of the grounds connected therewith, and
   for the erection and financing of the erection of the same, the Secretary of Property
   and Supplies may convey the tract, so acquired, in fee to the General State Authority,
   and in such case, the Department of Property and Supplies, upon the undertaking by
   the General State Authority of the construction of a building or buildings for the
   said hospital, may enter into a contract to lease, as lessee, and, upon completion
   by the Authority of such construction, shall enter into a lease, as lessee, of the
   same for a period of not exceeding thirty (30) years, at an annual rental to be fixed
   and determined by the Authority, and, upon the commencement of the term of the said
   lease, the Department of Property and Supplies shall turn over the said hospital to
   the Department of Welfare for management, and for the care, maintenance, and treatment
   of psychiatric patients, pursuant to the intent of the act hereby amended.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws›Western State Psychiatric Institute and Clinic›Purpose and Management›PA ST 50 P.S. § 575.5. Lease of property to University of Pittsburgh
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws › Western State Psychiatric Institute and Clinic › Purpose and Management › PA ST 50 P.S. § 575.5. Lease of property to University of Pittsburgh
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 575.5. Lease of property to University of Pittsburgh (2023)
content:
The Department of Property and Supplies,1with the approval of the Governor, is hereby authorized and directed to lease for
   the rental of one dollar ($1.00) per annum, to the Board of Trustees of the University
   of Pittsburgh, all the lands, buildings and equipment in the City of Pittsburgh, County
   of Allegheny, Pennsylvania, which comprise the Western State Psychiatric Institute
   and Clinic, or such term as shall be agreed upon.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 575.7. Relinquishment of control by Department of Welfare (2023)
content:
The Department of Welfare of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania is hereby authorized

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws›Purpose and Management›PA ST 50 P.S. § 575.4. Reference and consideration of recommendations of advisory board
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws › Purpose and Management › PA ST 50 P.S. § 575.4. Reference and consideration of recommendations of advisory board
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 575.4. Reference and consideration of recommendations of advisory board (2023)
content:
All recommendations concerning the policies of the institute and clinic which come
   from the Medical Advisory Board shall be referred to the Board of Trustees through
   the trustee committee of the Medical Center of the University of Pittsburgh.  When such recommendations are considered by the trustee committee on the Medical
   Center of the University of Pittsburgh, the Secretary of Welfare shall be invited
   to be present and to participate in the discussion of the same.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws › Establishment › PA ST 50 P.S. § 572. Cost of maintenance of private or full-pay patients
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 572. Cost of maintenance of private or full-pay patients (2023)
content:
All patients who are classified as private or full-pay patients, transferred from
   the State-owned mental hospitals to the Western State Psychiatric Institute and Clinic,
   shall pay only the per capita cost of maintenance which they paid at the hospital
   from which transferred or which applies to the hospital serving the district in which
   such patients have a legal residence.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 570. Department of Property and Supplies to erect and equip; qualifications of superintendent (2023)
content:
The Department of Property and Supplies1shall proceed, as soon as funds are made available therefor by appropriation, with
   the erection, construction and equipment of said Western State Psychiatric Institute
   and Clinic, which shall be sufficient to accommodate at least one hundred and fifty
   psychiatric patients and at least two hundred daily visits of psychiatric out-patients.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws›Purpose and Management›PA ST 50 P.S. § 575.2. Management; director

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 575.2. Management; director (2023)
content:
The Western State Psychiatric Institute and Clinic shall be under the management of
   the Board of Trustees of the University of Pittsburgh, which board shall select and
   appoint a director of the institute who shall be a physician of qualifications and
   experience in the care and treatment of mental diseases and mental defectives.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws›Western State Psychiatric Institute and Clinic›Purpose and Management›PA ST 50 P.S. § 575.1. Purposes of institution
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws › Western State Psychiatric Institute and Clinic › Purpose and Management › PA ST 50 P.S. § 575.1. Purposes of institution
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 575.1. Purposes of institution (2023)
content:
The Western State Psychiatric Institute and Clinic, located in Allegheny County, shall
   be used for study and research into the causes, treatment, prevention and cure of
   the various types of nervous disorders and mental diseases.  This institute shall also provide training and teaching both at the undergraduate
   and at the graduate level of students who, upon graduation, will enter the practice
   of general medicine, with a technical background of training in mental illness, as
   well as for the purpose of taking up the great gap between the number of qualified
   psychiatrists and the number who are needed as a result of the constantly mounting
   number of persons needing attention for mental disorders.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws›Harrisburg State Hospital›PA ST 50 P.S. § 325. Sale of parkway rights to City of Harrisburg
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws › Harrisburg State Hospital › PA ST 50 P.S. § 325. Sale of parkway rights to City of Harrisburg
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 325. Sale of parkway rights to City of Harrisburg (2023)
content:
The board of trustees of the Harrisburg State Hospital, acting through its president
   and secretary, be and the same is hereby authorized and empowered to negotiate with
   the City of Harrisburg for the opening of the parkway proposed by the said city from
   Reservoir Park to Wildwood Park, in the same city, and to agree upon the terms, conditions,
   limitations, and damages for so doing, and, an agreement being reached, to grant and
   convey the rights required for so doing, taking in exchange therefor such sum of money
   as damages, or such other lands, or such other consideration, as the said board of
   trustees may determine.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws›Eastern Pennsylvania Psychiatric Institute›PA ST 50 P.S. § 582. Site; construction and equipment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws › Eastern Pennsylvania Psychiatric Institute › PA ST 50 P.S. § 582. Site; construction and equipment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 582. Site; construction and equipment (2023)
content:
The Department of Property and Supplies1shall proceed with surveys, plans and estimates for an available site selected by
   the Department of Welfare and approved by the Governor, for the construction and equipment
   of such institution thereon, and for the improvement of the grounds connected therewith,
   in the manner provided by The Administrative Code of one thousand nine hundred twenty-nine,
   as amended,2and shall proceed, as soon as said site is selected and the plans for such institution
   are approved, with the erection, construction and equipping of the same.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws›Eastern Pennsylvania Psychiatric Institute›PA ST 50 P.S. § 581. Establishment; functions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws › Eastern Pennsylvania Psychiatric Institute › PA ST 50 P.S. § 581. Establishment; functions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 581. Establishment; functions (2023)
content:
There is hereby directed to be established and erected, at a site within the limits
   of the City of Philadelphia to be designated by the Department of Public Welfare1with the approval of the Governor, the Eastern Pennsylvania Psychiatric Institute.  It shall provide training and teaching to graduate and undergraduate students in
   the mental health field and shall conduct research into the causes, prevention, treatment
   and cure of mental, neurological and related disorders.  Through the department, the institute may enter into agreements specifying the terms
   and conditions under which one or more medical schools selected by the Secretary of
   Public Welfare may be associated with the institute in providing diagnosis, treatment,
   training, teaching and research.  Such agreements may provide for the transfer of responsibility by the department
   for the management and operation of the institute in whole or in part.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws›Eastern Pennsylvania Psychiatric Institute›PA ST 50 P.S. § 583.1. Lease of land and buildings

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 583.1. Lease of land and buildings (2023)
content:
The Department of General Services, with the approval of the Governor, is authorized
   to lease or sublease, all or part of the land and buildings known as the Eastern Pennsylvania
   Psychiatric Institute, and equipment therein, as appropriate to medical schools selected
   by the Secretary of Public Welfare1upon such terms and conditions as the Secretary of the Department of General Services
   may prescribe.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws›Pennsylvania School for Mental Defectives›PA ST 50 P.S. § 589.1. Selection of site
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws › Pennsylvania School for Mental Defectives › PA ST 50 P.S. § 589.1. Selection of site
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 589.1. Selection of site (2023)
content:
The Department of Welfare, with the approval of the Governor, shall select for acquisition
   by the Department of Property and Supplies1in the name of the Commonwealth, land for the erection and construction thereon of
   a new institution for mental defectives, with a capacity of not less than six hundred
   inmates.  Such land shall provide ample water supply and be capable of adequate sewerage and
   drainage, and the acreage obtained shall be sufficient for the most productive agricultural
   employment of the inmates.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws›Pennsylvania School for Mental Defectives›PA ST 50 P.S. § 589.4. Management and operation; personnel
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws › Pennsylvania School for Mental Defectives › PA ST 50 P.S. § 589.4. Management and operation; personnel
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 589.4. Management and operation; personnel (2023)
content:
The management and operation of the school and the care, maintenance and employment
   of the inmates, shall be the function of the Department of Welfare.  Subject to and in the manner provided in The Administrative Code of 1929 and its
   amendments,1the Department of Welfare shall have power to employ and fix the compensation of
   a superintendent, deputy superintendent, chaplain, guards, physicians, mechanics,
   clerks, stenographers, and other employes, as may be deemed necessary for the proper
   maintenance and management of the school and the safekeeping therein of its inmates.  The compensation of all persons so appointed and all other expenses in connection
   with the care and maintenance of inmates of the institution shall be paid from the
   appropriation made to the Department of Welfare for such purposes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws›Habitual Drunkard--Sale, Mortgage or Lease of Real Estate›PA ST 50 P.S. § 798. Procedure
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws › Habitual Drunkard--Sale, Mortgage or Lease of Real Estate › PA ST 50 P.S. § 798. Procedure
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 798. Procedure (2023)
content:
All jurisdiction conferred by this act on the court of common pleas shall be exercised
   on the petition of the spouse holding legal title to said real estate, supported by
   oath or affirmation.  Upon the presentation of such petition, the court shall fix a day for the hearing
   of which notice shall be given to the committee or next of kin of said habitual drunkard.  If, upon such hearing, the court is satisfied that the facts set forth in said petition
   are true, the prayer of the petition shall be granted, and the welfare of said habitual
   drunkard may be provided for in the discretion of the court as set forth in section
   one of this act, and the petitioning spouse shall be authorized and empowered to make,
   execute, and deliver a good and sufficient deed, mortgage, lease for years, or conveyance
   upon ground rent, as the case may be, for said real estate, to have the same force
   and effect as though the said petitioning spouse were unmarried:  the lien of all
   debts of record against said land to be preserved.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws›Habitual Drunkard--Sale, Mortgage or Lease of Real Estate›PA ST 50 P.S. § 797. Sale, mortgage, or lease of real estate of habitual drunkard; when authorized
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws › Habitual Drunkard--Sale, Mortgage or Lease of Real Estate › PA ST 50 P.S. § 797. Sale, mortgage, or lease of real estate of habitual drunkard; when authorized
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 797. Sale, mortgage, or lease of real estate of habitual drunkard; when authorized (2023)
content:
The courts of common pleas of the several counties of this Commonwealth, in all cases
   where the legal title to real estate is held by a married woman or a married man whose
   spouse is an habitual drunkard duly so found by inquisition, shall have power to direct
   and authorize said married woman or married man to sell, mortgage, lease for years,
   and convey upon ground rent, the same or any part thereof, under the direction of
   said court of the proper county, whenever it shall appear to said court that said
   spouse is an habitual drunkard and that it is the interest of the owner of said real
   estate that the same should be sold, mortgaged, leased for years, or conveyed on ground
   rent, as the case may be:  Provided, however, Where said spouse has no estate in his
   or her own right or one inadequate to his or her support, it shall be in the discretion
   of said court, by their order and decree, to make a reasonable provision for his or
   her support and maintenance out of said rents or proceeds of sale or mortgage so long
   as said spouse shall continue and habitual drunkard:  Provided, further, That such
   sale shall divest said real estate from any estate or claim of dower and estate as
   tenants by the curtesy or any claim in the nature thereof.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws › Pennsylvania School for Mental Defectives › PA ST 50 P.S. § 589.5. Powers of Department of Welfare
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 589.5. Powers of Department of Welfare (2023)
content:
In the management of the Pennsylvania School for Mental Defectives, the Department
   of Welfare shall have all the power conferred and perform all the duties imposed by
   the laws of the Commonwealth on the boards of trustees of the mental hospitals and
   institutions for mental defectives and epilepsy in Pennsylvania.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws›Pennsylvania School for Mental Defectives›PA ST 50 P.S. § 589.3. Receipt of mental defectives
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws › Pennsylvania School for Mental Defectives › PA ST 50 P.S. § 589.3. Receipt of mental defectives
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 589.3. Receipt of mental defectives (2023)
content:
The Department of Welfare shall receive into the custody of such institution, for
   care, guidance and control, mental defectives, in the manner provided by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article I. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4101. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article I. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4101. Short title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4101. Short title (2023)
content:
This act shall be known and may be cited as the “Mental Health and Intellectual Disability
   Act of 1966.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws›Pennsylvania School for Mental Defectives›PA ST 50 P.S. § 589.2. Construction of school
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws › Pennsylvania School for Mental Defectives › PA ST 50 P.S. § 589.2. Construction of school
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 589.2. Construction of school (2023)
content:
Upon the acquisition of any land in the name of the Commonwealth, the Department of
   Property and Supplies1shall construct thereon a new institution which shall be known as the “Pennsylvania
   School for Mental Defectives”.  The plans and specifications of the institution shall be subject to the approval
   of the Department of Welfare, and shall provide for suitable buildings and an adequate
   water supply system, sewage treatment works, heat and electric power plant or plants,
   service lines, and other necessary equipment, structures and improvements.  The buildings shall be of modern design, plan and substantial, and capable of extension
   as the needs of the institution may require.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 10. Alcoholism›PA ST 50 P.S. § 2104. Hospital and clinical facilities; State institutions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 10. Alcoholism › PA ST 50 P.S. § 2104. Hospital and clinical facilities; State institutions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 2104. Hospital and clinical facilities; State institutions (2023)
content:
The Secretary of Health shall contract for or establish such hospital and clinical
   facilities as are necessary to care properly for persons addicted to the excessive
   use of alcoholic beverages, and shall establish standards for the administration and
   organization of these facilities.  The Secretary of Health may also contract for the use of any State institution having
   adequate facilities therefor and admissions and commitments may be made thereto.

content: As used in this act:

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4201. General powers and duties of the department (2023)
content: The department shall have power, and its duty shall be:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 10. Alcoholism›PA ST 50 P.S. § 2101. Duty of the Department of Health
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 10. Alcoholism › PA ST 50 P.S. § 2101. Duty of the Department of Health
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 2101. Duty of the Department of Health (2023)
content:
The Department of Health is hereby authorized and required to establish a Program
   of Alcoholic Studies and Rehabilitation, hereinafter referred to as the “Program”
   to (1) study the problems of alcoholism, (2) treat and rehabilitate persons addicted
   to excessive use of alcoholic beverages, and (3) promote preventive and educational
   programs designed to eliminate alcoholism.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws›Guardianship of Weak-Minded Persons›PA ST 50 P.S. § 944. Trial by jury to be granted on demand
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 1. Miscellaneous Laws › Guardianship of Weak-Minded Persons › PA ST 50 P.S. § 944. Trial by jury to be granted on demand
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 944. Trial by jury to be granted on demand (2023)
content:
If the person against whom the proceedings are taken shall demand in writing, prior
   to the decision of the court on such application, a trial by jury, it shall thereupon
   be the duty of the said court to award an issue, framed to determine the question
   of fact involved, and such trial shall be granted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article II. Responsibilities of the State›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4202. State facilities
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article II. Responsibilities of the State › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4202. State facilities
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4202. State facilities (2023)
content:
(a) The department shall operate all State facilities and shall assign such functions
      to each as the secretary shall prescribe.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article III. Responsibilities of Counties›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4301. General powers and duties of local authorities; mental health and intellectual disability program and services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article III. Responsibilities of Counties › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4301. General powers and duties of local authorities; mental health and intellectual disability program and services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4301. General powers and duties of local authorities; mental health and intellectual disability program and services (2023)
content:
(a) The local authorities of each county separately or in concert with another county
      or counties, as the secretary may approve, shall establish a county mental health
      and intellectual disability program for the prevention of mental disability, and for
      the diagnosis, care, treatment, rehabilitation and detention of the mentally disabled
      and shall have power to make appropriations for such purposes.  Such program shall conform with regulations of the department promulgated under
      section 202(2).1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article III. Responsibilities of Counties›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4302. Establishment of County Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Board
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article III. Responsibilities of Counties › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4302. Establishment of County Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Board
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4302. Establishment of County Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Board (2023)
content:
(a) Except in cities of the first class, the local authorities of a county or of two
      or more counties participating in concert in a county mental health and intellectual
      disability program shall appoint a Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Board,
      hereinafter called the board, which shall consist of thirteen residents including,
      from each county, a representative of the board of county commissioners.  At least two members thereof shall be physicians, and where possible one shall be
      a psychiatrist and the other a pediatrician.  There shall also be appropriate representation drawn from:

content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article III. Responsibilities of Counties›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4304. County mental health and intellectual disability administrator; appointment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article III. Responsibilities of Counties › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4304. County mental health and intellectual disability administrator; appointment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4304. County mental health and intellectual disability administrator; appointment (2023)
content:
Except in cities of the first class, where the administrator shall be appointed under
   the merit system, the local authorities shall appoint a county mental health and intellectual
   disability administrator from a list of not less than two names submitted by the County
   Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Board.  If, thirty days after the county board has submitted a list to the local authorities,
   an appointment has not been made because of a tie vote or other failure of the local
   authorities to make such appointment, the same shall be made by the secretary after
   consultation with the local authorities.  The appointment of the administrator, by whomever made, may be terminated by the
   local authorities, provided, that no appointment made by the secretary under this
   section shall be terminated without the approval of a majority of the County Mental
   Health and Intellectual Disability Board.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4402. Voluntary admission; application, examination and acceptance; duration of admission (2023)
content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4406. Civil court commitment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4406. Civil court commitment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4406. Civil court commitment (2023)
content:
(a) Whenever a person is believed to be mentally disabled, and in need of care or
      treatment by reason of such mental disability, and examination of such person has
      been made by a physician or physicians, or for any reason the examination of such
      person cannot be made, a petition may be presented to the court of common pleas of
      the county in which a person resides or is, for his immediate examination or commitment
      to an appropriate facility for examination, observation and diagnosis.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4405. Commitment for emergency detention
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4405. Commitment for emergency detention
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4405. Commitment for emergency detention (2023)
content:
(a) Whenever a person appears, by reason of his acts or threatened acts, to be so
      mentally disabled as to be dangerous to himself or others and in need of immediate
      care, he may be taken into custody for the purpose of examination, provided that:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4404. Commitment on application by relative, etc.; physicians' certificates; review
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4404. Commitment on application by relative, etc.; physicians' certificates; review
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4404. Commitment on application by relative, etc.; physicians' certificates; review (2023)
content:
(a) A written application for commitment to a facility may be made in the interest
      of any person who appears to be mentally disabled and in need of care.  It may be made by a relative, guardian, friend, individual standing in loco parentis
      to the person to be committed, or by the executive officer or an authorized agent
      of a governmental or recognized nonprofit health or welfare organization or agency
      or any responsible person.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4401. Applications for admission or commitment; to whom made
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4401. Applications for admission or commitment; to whom made
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4401. Applications for admission or commitment; to whom made (2023)
content:
(a) Any mentally disabled person who desires care in a facility may make appropriate
      application directly to any facility willing and able to receive him, or to the administrator
      of the county where the person is or resides, for placement in a facility.

content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4409. Effect of commitment on pending criminal proceedings; duration of commitment; authority of attorney for the Commonwealth
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4409. Effect of commitment on pending criminal proceedings; duration of commitment; authority of attorney for the Commonwealth
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4409. Effect of commitment on pending criminal proceedings; duration of commitment; authority of attorney for the Commonwealth (2023)
content:
(a) Whenever a person who has been charged with crime is committed in accordance with
      either section 407 or section 408 of this act,1the criminal proceedings against him shall be stayed for the duration of commitment,
      provided however, that the Attorney for the Commonwealth may submit indictments to
      the grand jury involving such charge.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4408. Commitment of person charged with crime and detained in a penal or correctional institution
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4408. Commitment of person charged with crime and detained in a penal or correctional institution
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4408. Commitment of person charged with crime and detained in a penal or correctional institution (2023)
content:
(a) Whenever a person who has been charged with crime is detained in a penal or correctional
      institution and he is believed to be mentally disabled so that his commitment to a
      facility is necessary, a petition for such commitment may be presented to the court
      of the county where he stands charged with crime.  The petition may be made by the warden or other officer in charge of the detailing
      institution, a relative of the detained person, the detained person or his counsel
      or the attorney for the Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4407. Commitment of person charged with crime and released on bail
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4407. Commitment of person charged with crime and released on bail
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4407. Commitment of person charged with crime and released on bail (2023)
content:
(a) Whenever a person who has been charged with crime and released on bail is or becomes
      mentally disabled so that his admission or commitment to a facility is necessary,
      proceedings may be instituted under the appropriate provisions of this act, in the
      same manner as if he had not been so charged with crime.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4410. Commitment in lieu of sentence of person adjudged guilty of crime
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4410. Commitment in lieu of sentence of person adjudged guilty of crime
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4410. Commitment in lieu of sentence of person adjudged guilty of crime (2023)
content:
(a) Whenever any person is adjudged guilty of a crime punishable by sentence to a
      penal or correctional institution, the trial court may defer sentence and order an
      examination of the defendant for mental disability to guide it in determining his
      disposition.  Such action may be taken on the court's initiative, or on the application of the
      district attorney, the defendant, or his counsel or other person acting in his interest.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4411. Commitment of person undergoing sentence and detained in a penal or correctional institution
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4411. Commitment of person undergoing sentence and detained in a penal or correctional institution
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4411. Commitment of person undergoing sentence and detained in a penal or correctional institution (2023)
content:
(a) Whenever a person undergoing sentence and detained in a penal or correctional
      institution, is believed to be mentally disabled so that his commitment to a facility
      is necessary, a petition for such commitment may be presented to the court which imposed
      sentence.  The petition may be made by the warden or other officer in charge of the detaining
      institution or counsel for the person so sentenced.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4414. Deportation of persons charged with or sentenced for crime
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4414. Deportation of persons charged with or sentenced for crime
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4414. Deportation of persons charged with or sentenced for crime (2023)
content:
Whenever any person is detained in a facility after having been charged with or convicted
   of crime, and is subject to deportation from the Commonwealth under the laws of the
   United States, the court committing such person, upon the petition of the director
   of such facility, may enter an order releasing such person from detention into the
   custody of an agent of the United States for the purposes of deportation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4413. Commitment of persons acquitted of crime because of insanity
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4413. Commitment of persons acquitted of crime because of insanity
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4413. Commitment of persons acquitted of crime because of insanity (2023)
content:
(a) Whenever any person charged with any crime is acquitted on the ground of insanity
      or having been insane at the time he committed the crime, the jury or the court as
      the case may be, shall state such reason for acquittal in its verdict.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4412. Transfer of State prisoners without court approval; retransfers; further commitments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4412. Transfer of State prisoners without court approval; retransfers; further commitments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4412. Transfer of State prisoners without court approval; retransfers; further commitments (2023)
content:
(a) Whenever any person who is detained in a State penal or correctional institution
      is believed to be mentally disabled so that his commitment to a facility is necessary
      or desirable, he may, without court approval, be transferred to any facility operated
      by the department in accordance with the following procedures:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4417. Powers and duties of directors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4417. Powers and duties of directors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4417. Powers and duties of directors (2023)
content:
(a) The director of any facility shall be in charge of all services afforded to any
      person admitted or committed to such facility including all maintenance services,
      custody, and employment of such persons, and shall also be in charge of the diagnosis,
      treatment and care to be given such person by reason of mental or physical disability.  If the director is not a physician, a physician shall be in charge of all medical
      diagnosis, treatment and care to be rendered such persons.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4415. Commitment or transfers to facilities of the United States Government or of another State; reciprocal agreements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4415. Commitment or transfers to facilities of the United States Government or of another State; reciprocal agreements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4415. Commitment or transfers to facilities of the United States Government or of another State; reciprocal agreements (2023)
content:
(a) Except when a person has been charged with or sentenced for crime, if proceedings
      for his admission or commitment have been effected he may be committed or transferred
      to the Veterans Administration or any other agency of the United States government
      or to another state for care therein.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4416. Transfers between facilities
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4416. Transfers between facilities
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4416. Transfers between facilities (2023)
content:
(a) The department may, upon application by the director of any state operated facility,
      transfer a mentally disabled person to any other state operated facility under its
      jurisdiction.  The administrator may, upon application by the director of any local facility, transfer
      a mentally disabled person to any other local facility under his jurisdiction.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4422. Mechanical restraints prohibited; exceptions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4422. Mechanical restraints prohibited; exceptions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4422. Mechanical restraints prohibited; exceptions (2023)
content:
Mechanical restraints shall not be used or applied to a mentally disabled person,
   except:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4419. Leaves of absence
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4419. Leaves of absence
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4419. Leaves of absence (2023)
content:
(a) The director of any facility, in his discretion, may allow a leave of absence
      to any person admitted or committed whose condition is such as to warrant the action,
      for a period not exceeding one year, and upon such terms and conditions as he may
      prescribe consistent with regulations of the department and the director may renew
      or extend a leave of absence for an additional period or periods not exceeding one
      year for each such renewal or extension.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4425. Escapes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4425. Escapes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4425. Escapes (2023)
content:
(a) Whenever any committed person who may be dangerous to the safety of the public
      or himself escapes from a facility, it shall be the duty of the director to promptly
      notify the local, county and State law enforcement officers.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4420. Discharge by department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4420. Discharge by department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4420. Discharge by department (2023)
content:
The department may review any commitment made under this act other than a criminal
   commitment and the secretary may order the discharge of any person so committed whenever
   he finds that such committed person is no longer in need of care and treatment in
   a facility.  The department may also review criminal commitments and the secretary may make recommendation
   to the court which committed such person that he be discharged or returned to a penal
   or correctional institution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4423. Rights of persons admitted or committed
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4423. Rights of persons admitted or committed
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4423. Rights of persons admitted or committed (2023)
content: Every person admitted, committed or detained in any facility shall have the right:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4426. Habeas corpus; discharge by order of court
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4426. Habeas corpus; discharge by order of court
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4426. Habeas corpus; discharge by order of court (2023)
content:
(a) Every person committed or detained in a facility by reason of the provisions of
      this act or anyone acting on his behalf, may at any time, petition for a writ of Habeas
      Corpus and, except as hereinafter provided, said petition shall be filed in accordance
      with the provisions of the act of May 25, 1951 (P.L. 415).1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4418. Duration of admission or commitment; in general
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4418. Duration of admission or commitment; in general
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4418. Duration of admission or commitment; in general (2023)
content:
Any admission or commitment of a person under this act, shall be valid and authorize
   the detention of such person only for the period specified in the section under which
   he was admitted or committed, or, where authorized, for such period as a court may
   specify in its order of commitment.  If no period is specified in a commitment, the person may be detained until care
   or treatment is no longer necessary, whereupon he shall be discharged, or otherwise
   dealt with in accordance with the provisions of this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4421. Transportation of mentally disabled persons
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4421. Transportation of mentally disabled persons
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4421. Transportation of mentally disabled persons (2023)
content:
Whenever the transportation of a mentally disabled person from one place to another
   is necessary to effect admission to, commitment in, or transfer between facilities
   and circumstances permit, such person shall be accompanied by a relative or other
   suitable person of the same sex.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4424. Funds of persons admitted or committed to State operated facilities
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article IV. General Provisions Relating to Facilities; Admissions and Commitments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4424. Funds of persons admitted or committed to State operated facilities
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4424. Funds of persons admitted or committed to State operated facilities (2023)
content:
Where no guardian has been appointed for a mentally disabled person admitted or committed
   to a State operated facility all money and other personal property of such person
   shall be handled in the following manner, unless the director determines that such
   person's recovery or wellbeing will be promoted by his own handling of such money
   or personal property:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4502. Liability of persons owing a legal duty to support
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4502. Liability of persons owing a legal duty to support
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4502. Liability of persons owing a legal duty to support (2023)
content:
Except as provided in this section and in section 504,1whenever any person under eighteen years of age admitted, committed or otherwise
   receiving any service or benefit under this act shall be unable to discharge the obligation
   imposed upon him by section 501,2such liability is hereby imposed upon any person owing a legal duty to support the
   person admitted, committed or otherwise receiving services or benefits under this
   act.  Upon the mentally disabled person attaining the age of eighteen, or any mentally
   disabled person over eighteen years of age on the effective date of this act, the
   liability under the act of the persons owing a legal duty to support him shall cease:
   Provided, however, That spouses shall remain liable for each other regardless of age
   except for periods of continuous inpatient care in excess of one hundred and twenty
   days.  Continuous inpatient care for the purposes of this section shall be any in-hospital
   stay not interrupted by more than one hundred and twenty days.  Nothing in this section 502 shall relieve any private, nonprofit or governmental
   health insurer for liability to pay for such care under any contract of insurance
   or group insurance plan.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4503. Contingent liability of State and local government; intention of act
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4503. Contingent liability of State and local government; intention of act
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4503. Contingent liability of State and local government; intention of act (2023)
content:
(a) Neither the State nor a county shall be required to expend public funds under
      this act on behalf of a mentally disabled person until such person, who has been admitted
      or committed or is receiving services or benefits under this act, shall have exhausted
      his eligibility and receipt of benefits under all other existing or future, private,
      public, local, State or Federal programs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4504. Powers of secretary to determine liability and establish criteria
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4504. Powers of secretary to determine liability and establish criteria
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4504. Powers of secretary to determine liability and establish criteria (2023)
content:
(a) Whenever any person receives a service or benefit at any facility under this act
      wholly or in part at public expense, the secretary is hereby authorized and shall
      have the power, subject to the approval of the Attorney General, to determine the
      extent of liability imposed under sections 501 or 502,1and to abate, modify, compromise or discharge the liability so imposed provided:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4501. Liability of mentally disabled persons
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4501. Liability of mentally disabled persons
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4501. Liability of mentally disabled persons (2023)
content:
Whenever public funds are expended under any provision of this act on behalf of a
   mentally disabled person, the governmental body expending such funds may recover the
   same from such person subject to the regulations of the department and for this purpose
   liability is hereby imposed upon such person admitted, committed or otherwise receiving
   any service or benefit under this act for all costs, payments or expenditures with
   reference thereto, including but not being limited to the costs of admission or commitment,
   transportation, treatment, training, maintenance, complete care, partial care or aftercare
   and discharge.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4509. State and county grants and payments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4509. State and county grants and payments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4509. State and county grants and payments (2023)
content: The department, subject to the provisions of section 503,1shall have the power, and its duty shall be:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4505. Liability of county
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4505. Liability of county
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4505. Liability of county (2023)
content: (a) Repealed by1997, June 18, P.L. 179, No. 18, § 6, imd. effective.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4507. Liability of the Commonwealth
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4507. Liability of the Commonwealth
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4507. Liability of the Commonwealth (2023)
content: (a) Except as provided in sections 501, 502, and 505,1the Commonwealth shall pay for the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4508. Relief of county from obligation to insure service; State's obligation; liability in such cases
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4508. Relief of county from obligation to insure service; State's obligation; liability in such cases
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4508. Relief of county from obligation to insure service; State's obligation; liability in such cases (2023)
content:
(a) If local authorities cannot insure the availability of any of the services required
      by section 301,1or if they assert that it would be economically unsound to do so, such authorities
      may make application to the department to be relieved for the period of one year from
      the duty to insure their availability.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4506. Collection of costs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4506. Collection of costs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4506. Collection of costs (2023)
content:
(a) The primary responsibility for collecting the cost of care and treatment provided
      at a facility not operated by the State, or by an individual, because of any liability
      imposed by this act, shall rest with the facility or such individual, as the case
      may be, providing such care and treatment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4511. Interim grants for mental health and intellectual disability services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4511. Interim grants for mental health and intellectual disability services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4511. Interim grants for mental health and intellectual disability services (2023)
content:
(a) From State and Federal funds, the department may make grants to any county, or
      combination of counties, or to any facility for all or part of the cost of services
      designed to carry out the provisions of article III of this act.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4510. Supplemental grants
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4510. Supplemental grants
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4510. Supplemental grants (2023)
content:
The department may make additional grants to any county participating in an approved
   mental health and intellectual disability plan to assist in establishing the services
   provided for in such plan, for the first three years of operation of such plan.  Said grant shall be supplemental to grants authorized by section 5091but shall not exceed in any one year, ten percent of the grant made under that section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4602. Record of persons admitted or committed
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4602. Record of persons admitted or committed
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4602. Record of persons admitted or committed (2023)
content:
(a) Whenever a person is admitted or committed to any facility or receives services
      or benefits at a facility under any provision of this act, a complete record pertaining
      to such person shall be maintained by the facility.  Such record shall include, if available, but need not be limited to, applications,
      petitions, affidavits, orders of court, reports of physicians, psychiatrists, psychologists,
      nurses, social workers, police records, financial records, and all clinical records
      or a full abstract thereof containing all essential particulars, including results
      of physical examinations, examinations for mental disability, laboratory tests, and
      any other material with reference to such person.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4603. Immunities
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4603. Immunities
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4603. Immunities (2023)
content:
No person and no governmental or recognized nonprofit health or welfare organization
   or agency shall be held civilly or criminally liable for any diagnosis, opinion, report
   or any thing done pursuant to the provisions of this act if he acted in good faith
   and not falsely, corruptly, maliciously or without reasonable cause;  provided, however,
   that causes of action based upon gross negligence or incompetence shall not be affected
   by the immunities granted by this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4601. Forms to be used under this act
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4601. Forms to be used under this act
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4601. Forms to be used under this act (2023)
content:
The secretary may develop suggested forms to be used in carrying out the provisions
   of this act.  By regulation, he may require the use of any form so developed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4512. Deadline for establishment of county mental health and intellectual disability program; failure to comply with minimum standards; penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article V. Financial Obligations; Liabilities and Payments › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4512. Deadline for establishment of county mental health and intellectual disability program; failure to comply with minimum standards; penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4512. Deadline for establishment of county mental health and intellectual disability program; failure to comply with minimum standards; penalties (2023)
content:
(a) Each county acting alone or in participation with other counties as provided in
      section 3011shall, by January 1, 1969, submit to the department for approval a plan for a county
      mental health and intellectual disability program.  The information and material upon which such plan shall be formulated for submission
      to the department shall be published and distributed to the counties by the Advisory
      Committee for Mental Health and Intellectual Disability on or before August 1, 1968.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4604. Report of psychological examination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4604. Report of psychological examination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4604. Report of psychological examination (2023)
content:
Whenever a preliminary examination required by this act indicates that the person
   examined is mentally retarded, the report of a psychologist shall accompany the physician's
   report or certificate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4605. Penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4605. Penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4605. Penalties (2023)
content:
The following acts are hereby declared to be crimes and any person found guilty thereof
   shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction thereof shall be sentenced to
   pay a fine not exceeding one thousand dollars ($1,000), or to undergo imprisonment
   not exceeding one year, or both, except that if such acts shall be committed by corporation,
   partnership or association, the officers and directors of such corporation or the
   members of such partnership or association, its agents and employes who knowingly
   participated in such acts shall also be guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction
   thereof, shall be punished as hereinbefore provided:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article VI. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4606. Administrative Agency Law to apply
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article VI. Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4606. Administrative Agency Law to apply
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4606. Administrative Agency Law to apply (2023)
content:
The provisions of this act shall be subject to the provisions of the Administrative
   Agency Law of 1945, P.L. 1388, as amended.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article VII. Repeals; Interim Powers; Appropriations; Effective Date›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4701. Repeals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article VII. Repeals; Interim Powers; Appropriations; Effective Date › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4701. Repeals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4701. Repeals (2023)
content: (a) The act of June 12, 1951 (P.L. 533), known as “The Mental Health Act of 1951,”1is repealed absolutely, effective July 1, 1969.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article VII. Repeals; Interim Powers; Appropriations; Effective Date›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4702. Interim powers of the department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article VII. Repeals; Interim Powers; Appropriations; Effective Date › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4702. Interim powers of the department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4702. Interim powers of the department (2023)
content:
(a) Between the effective date of this act and July 1, 1969, or until such time between
      said dates as the local authorities shall carry out the responsibilities imposed upon
      them by Article III,1the department shall have the general power to do all things necessary to act for
      the state or in place of local authorities or their appointees in the designation
      of facilities and the furnishing of mental health and mental retardation services
      to the mentally disabled.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article VII. Repeals; Interim Powers; Appropriations; Effective Date›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4703. Appropriation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article VII. Repeals; Interim Powers; Appropriations; Effective Date › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4703. Appropriation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4703. Appropriation (2023)
content:
The sum of six million dollars ($6,000,000), or as much thereof as may be necessary,
   is hereby appropriated to the Department of Public Welfare for the fiscal year 1966-67
   for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 14. Parklands Payback Pilot Project›PA ST 50 P.S. § 6002. Applicability of act
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 14. Parklands Payback Pilot Project › PA ST 50 P.S. § 6002. Applicability of act
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 6002. Applicability of act (2023)
content:
The provisions of this act shall apply only to the site as designated herein on Commonwealth-owned
   land at the Otocsin Interchange No. 18 of I-80.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966›Article VII. Repeals; Interim Powers; Appropriations; Effective Date›PA ST 50 P.S. § 4704. Effective date
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 12. Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Act of 1966 › Article VII. Repeals; Interim Powers; Appropriations; Effective Date › PA ST 50 P.S. § 4704. Effective date
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 4704. Effective date (2023)
content: This act shall take effect January 1, 1967.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 14. Parklands Payback Pilot Project›PA ST 50 P.S. § 6003. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 14. Parklands Payback Pilot Project › PA ST 50 P.S. § 6003. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 6003. Definitions (2023)
content:
As used in this act the following words and terms shall be construed as defined in
   this section, except where a different intent is plainly apparent from the context
   thereof:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 14. Parklands Payback Pilot Project›PA ST 50 P.S. § 6001. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 14. Parklands Payback Pilot Project › PA ST 50 P.S. § 6001. Short title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 6001. Short title (2023)
content:
This act shall be known as and may be cited as the “Parklands Payback Pilot Project
   Act.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 15. Mental Health Procedures›Article I. General Provisions›PA ST 50 P.S. § 7103. Scope of act
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 15. Mental Health Procedures › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 50 P.S. § 7103. Scope of act
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 7103. Scope of act (2023)
content:
This act establishes rights and procedures for all involuntary treatment of mentally
   ill persons, whether inpatient or outpatient, and for all voluntary inpatient treatment
   of mentally ill persons.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 14. Parklands Payback Pilot Project›PA ST 50 P.S. § 6004. Purpose of this act
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 14. Parklands Payback Pilot Project › PA ST 50 P.S. § 6004. Purpose of this act
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 6004. Purpose of this act (2023)
content:
The purpose of this act is to aid certain mentally retarded and otherwise developmentally
   disabled persons to become self-sustaining citizens, in conjunction with development
   of tourist and recreational accommodations on lands owned by the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 50 P.S. Mental Health›Chapter 14. Parklands Payback Pilot Project›PA ST 50 P.S. § 6005. Developer guarantee
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 50 P.S. Mental Health › Chapter 14. Parklands Payback Pilot Project › PA ST 50 P.S. § 6005. Developer guarantee
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 50 P.S. § 6005. Developer guarantee (2023)
content:
The developer shall guarantee the Commonwealth that he will employ workers who are
   available for all jobs for which they are qualified, acting on referrals of workers
   through established agencies and institutions of the Commonwealth.  The specific jobs to be filled shall be established by the habilitator in conjunction
