citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 1721. Veterans' Trust Fund (2023)
content:
(a) Source of revenue.--In addition to transfers under section 1719-G of the act of April 9, 1929 (P.L. 343,
      No. 176),1known as The Fiscal Code, the Veterans' Trust Fund shall include funds from the following
      sources:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 501. Powers of Governor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 501. Powers of Governor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 501. Powers of Governor (2023)
content:
The Governor of this Commonwealth as Commander-in-Chief shall have the powers enumerated
   hereafter in this title over the Pennsylvania military forces which includes the Pennsylvania
   National Guard when not absent from this Commonwealth on the call or order of the
   United States and the Pennsylvania Guard when formed, organized and equipped under
   order from the Governor in conformity with this title.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 502. Acceptance of Federal allotment for Pennsylvania National Guard
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 502. Acceptance of Federal allotment for Pennsylvania National Guard
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 502. Acceptance of Federal allotment for Pennsylvania National Guard (2023)
content:
The Governor shall accept for the Commonwealth allotments of military personnel and
   equipment and their apportionment to the various arms and services proposed by the
   Department of Defense for the Pennsylvania National Guard as he may, in his discretion,
   deem proper for the Commonwealth to accept.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 503. Training and Federal property of Pennsylvania National Guard
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 503. Training and Federal property of Pennsylvania National Guard
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 503. Training and Federal property of Pennsylvania National Guard (2023)
content:
The Governor shall assume the obligation of carrying out the training requirement
   set forth under the applicable Federal statutes and regulations for the Pennsylvania
   National Guard.  This training function is hereby delegated and becomes the responsibility of the
   normal channels of command in the Pennsylvania National Guard.  The Governor shall furnish suitable shelter for personnel and suitable storage facilities
   for Federal property, issued for use of the Pennsylvania National Guard.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 504. Permanent location of Pennsylvania National Guard units
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 504. Permanent location of Pennsylvania National Guard units
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 504. Permanent location of Pennsylvania National Guard units (2023)
content:
The Governor shall establish the permanent location, within the boundaries of this
   Commonwealth, of any assigned, authorized organizations or units of the Pennsylvania
   National Guard allotted to this Commonwealth by the Department of Defense.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 505. Change in organization of Pennsylvania National Guard
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 505. Change in organization of Pennsylvania National Guard
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 505. Change in organization of Pennsylvania National Guard (2023)
content:
The Governor shall organize or reorganize any organization or unit of the Pennsylvania
   National Guard so as to conform, so far as practicable, to the structure of the armed
   forces of the United States.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 506.1. Use of Pennsylvania National Guard for special State duty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 506.1. Use of Pennsylvania National Guard for special State duty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 506.1. Use of Pennsylvania National Guard for special State duty (2023)
content:
(a) Authorization.--The Governor may place, or delegate authority to the Adjutant General to order, any
      volunteer member of the Pennsylvania National Guard or, if unavailable due to call
      or order into the service of the United States, any member of the Pennsylvania Guard
      on special State duty to respond to community needs, support Commonwealth functions
      and ceremonies, participate in courts-martial and board functions, support State and
      local governments and designated critical infrastructure with cybersecurity functional
      support and nongovernmental and educational institutions with cyber training or exercises
      and perform other necessary military duties to the extent that money is appropriated
      and available for special State duty.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 506. Organization of Pennsylvania Guard for emergency
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 506. Organization of Pennsylvania Guard for emergency
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 506. Organization of Pennsylvania Guard for emergency (2023)
content:
Whenever the Pennsylvania National Guard, or any part thereof, shall be called or
   ordered into the service of the United States, the Governor may organize units of
   the Pennsylvania Guard for the internal security of this Commonwealth.  The Governor shall comply with the laws of the United States for the organization,
   maintenance and functioning of this force.  The Governor is further empowered to organize at any time a nucleus of Pennsylvania
   Guard personnel for the purpose of planning.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 507. Draft from militia for emergency
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 507. Draft from militia for emergency
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 507. Draft from militia for emergency (2023)
content:
The Governor shall have the power to order out for actual service with the Pennsylvania
   Guard by draft as many persons from the militia as necessity demands during a war
   or other emergency.  The Governor is hereby authorized to form, adopt and prescribe such rules and regulations,
   and appoint such officers and civilian boards and fix their compensation, for the
   purpose of drafting the militia, when such process may be required, as deemed best
   and most expedient.  Any such rules or regulations shall not conflict with any Federal Selective Service
   Act or National Draft Act in effect at the time.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 509. Coordination with adjacent states
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 509. Coordination with adjacent states
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 509. Coordination with adjacent states (2023)
content:
The Governor shall confer with the Governors or proper authorities of adjacent states
   for the purpose of coordinating and providing for the mutual defense and the internal
   security and for the exchange of authority to employ the Pennsylvania military forces
   in other states, and the employment of their armed forces within the boundaries of
   this Commonwealth.  This power may be delegated to the Adjutant General.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 508. Active duty for emergency
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 508. Active duty for emergency
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 508. Active duty for emergency (2023)
content:
(a) State duty.--The Governor may place the Pennsylvania National Guard, or any part thereof, or when
      unavailable due to call or order into the service of the United States, the Pennsylvania
      Guard, or any part thereof, on active duty when an emergency in this Commonwealth
      occurs or is threatened, or when tumult, riot or disaster shall exist or is imminent.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 510. Promulgation of regulations and rules
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 510. Promulgation of regulations and rules
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 510. Promulgation of regulations and rules (2023)
content:
The Governor shall promulgate such rules and regulations as he may deem expedient
   for the government of the Pennsylvania military forces.  The regulations shall conform to this title and other laws of this Commonwealth
   applicable to said forces and, as nearly as practicable, to those governing similar
   Federal armed military forces.  They shall have the same force and effect as the provisions of this title and other
   laws affecting these forces.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Subpart A. Organization›Chapter 15. State Armory Board›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 1511. State Treasury Armory Fund
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Subpart A. Organization › Chapter 15. State Armory Board › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 1511. State Treasury Armory Fund
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 1511. State Treasury Armory Fund (2023)
content:
(a) Establishment.--There is hereby established in the State Treasury a special revenue fund to be known
      as the State Treasury Armory Fund.  The proceeds from the sale of any armory, the proceeds from the sale or lease of
      timber or other mineral rights at Fort Indiantown Gap or at any armory, the proceeds
      from any rental or lease of any facility at Fort Indiantown Gap and the proceeds from
      the rental or lease of any armory shall be deposited in the fund.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 512. Display of POW/MIA flag
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 512. Display of POW/MIA flag
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 512. Display of POW/MIA flag (2023)
content:
The POW/MIA flag may be displayed at the western entrance to the Fort Pitt Tunnel
   in Allegheny County.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 511. Issuing flags, standards and guidons
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 5. The Governor as Commander-In-Chief › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 511. Issuing flags, standards and guidons
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 511. Issuing flags, standards and guidons (2023)
content:
The Governor as Commander-in-Chief is hereby authorized to procure and issue from
   time to time to the Pennsylvania National Guard and Pennsylvania Guard such flags,
   standards and guidons as may be necessary, in conformance with applicable Federal
   and State statutes and regulations.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 701. Overall powers of department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 701. Overall powers of department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 701. Overall powers of department (2023)
content:
(a) Powers and duties.--The department shall continue to exercise the powers and perform the duties by law
      vested in and imposed upon the Adjutant General and the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 704. Advisory councils for veterans' homes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 704. Advisory councils for veterans' homes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 704. Advisory councils for veterans' homes (2023)
content:
(a) Establishment of advisory council.--There is hereby established an advisory council for each veterans' home operated by
      the Commonwealth.  Each advisory council shall consist of 15 members and the Adjutant General, who
      shall serve ex officio.  Twelve of the members shall be appointed by the Governor from a list of nominations
      submitted to the Adjutant General by the Pennsylvania War Veterans' Council.  The Speaker of the House of Representatives and the President pro tempore of the
      Senate shall each appoint one member from their respective bodies to serve on each
      council.  The remaining member on the advisory council shall be selected by the residents
      of the veterans' homes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Subpart A. Organization›Chapter 15. State Armory Board›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 1512. Maintenance, construction and repairs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Subpart A. Organization › Chapter 15. State Armory Board › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 1512. Maintenance, construction and repairs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 1512. Maintenance, construction and repairs (2023)
content:
Notwithstanding the provisions of any other law, the board may carry out all maintenance
   activities with respect to an armory if the cost does not exceed $100,000 and may
   carry out contracts for repair or construction of armories up to an amount of $100,000.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 702. Duties of department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 702. Duties of department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 702. Duties of department (2023)
content: The department shall have the power and its duty shall be:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 703. Administration, supply and supervision of military forces
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 703. Administration, supply and supervision of military forces
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 703. Administration, supply and supervision of military forces (2023)
content:
The department shall be specifically responsible for the administration and supply
   of the Pennsylvania military forces and shall have general supervisory function of
   all matters pertaining thereto.  The department shall make periodic reports, as required by law or requested by the
   Governor or the Department of Defense, concerning the condition and state of the readiness
   of the Pennsylvania military forces.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 705. Burial details for veterans
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 705. Burial details for veterans
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 705. Burial details for veterans (2023)
content:
(a) Authority.--The department shall have the power to arrange for burial details for veteran soldiers
      who are to be interred at any of the following national cemeteries:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 707. Training areas
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 707. Training areas
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 707. Training areas (2023)
content:
(a) Acquisition.--Upon the request of the Adjutant General and with the approval of the Governor, the
      Secretary of General Services is authorized to purchase, lease or obtain the right
      to use any real estate or building necessary for military training or preparedness
      of the Pennsylvania National Guard.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 708. Fort Indiantown Gap
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 708. Fort Indiantown Gap
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 708. Fort Indiantown Gap (2023)
content:
(a) Operation.--The Adjutant General is authorized to promulgate rules, regulations and policies for
      the continuing operation of Fort Indiantown Gap.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 709. Operation of State-owned vehicles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 709. Operation of State-owned vehicles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 709. Operation of State-owned vehicles (2023)
content: (a) Authority.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 710. Pennsylvania Veterans' Monuments and Memorial Trust Fund
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 710. Pennsylvania Veterans' Monuments and Memorial Trust Fund
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 710. Pennsylvania Veterans' Monuments and Memorial Trust Fund (2023)
content:
(a) Establishment and administration.--There is established a separate fund in the State Treasury to be known as the Pennsylvania
      Veterans' Monuments and Memorial Trust Fund.  The fund shall be administered by the department, and all moneys in the fund are
      appropriated to the department on a continuing basis for the purposes provided for
      under subsection (b).  The State Veterans' Commission shall assist the department in accordance with section
      1704(1) (relating to specific powers and duties).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 706. Cooperative agreements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 706. Cooperative agreements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 706. Cooperative agreements (2023)
content:
The department may enter into cooperative agreements with the Federal Government to
   perform certain military or training functions.  A cooperative agreement shall contain any appendixes and supplements necessary to
   allow for the performance of those functions and reimbursement by the Federal Government.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 711. Installation of police officers for Fort Indiantown Gap and other designated Commonwealth military installations and facilities
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 711. Installation of police officers for Fort Indiantown Gap and other designated Commonwealth military installations and facilities
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 711. Installation of police officers for Fort Indiantown Gap and other designated Commonwealth military installations and facilities (2023)
content:
(a) Appointment.--The Adjutant General may issue commissions to Commonwealth employees of the Department
      of Military and Veterans Affairs to act as installation police officers at Fort Indiantown
      Gap and other Commonwealth military installations and facilities designated by the
      Adjutant General.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 712. Veterans registry
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia › Chapter 7. Department of Military and Veterans Affairs › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 712. Veterans registry
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 712. Veterans registry (2023)
content:
(a) Establishment of veterans registry.--The department shall establish a registry of veterans residing in this Commonwealth
      in order to provide information on Federal, State and local government benefits, programs
      and services available to veterans and to link veterans with resources that can provide
      assistance.  Upon registration, if permission is granted by the registrant, the registrant's
      information shall be shared with county directors of veterans affairs and other State
      agencies.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part II. Pennsylvania National Guard, Pennsylvania Guard and Militia›Subpart A. Organization›Chapter 17.       have completed honorable, active duty military service and who reside or resided in
      the geographic region served by the veterans' home.  The area or space in the veterans' home dedicated to the hall of fame may be used

      accused is subject to this part and subject matter jurisdiction is established under
      section 5104 (relating to subject matter jurisdiction).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part IV. Military Justice›Chapter 52. Apprehension and Restraint›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5202. Apprehension of persons absent without leave
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part IV. Military Justice › Chapter 52. Apprehension and Restraint › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5202. Apprehension of persons absent without leave
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5202. Apprehension of persons absent without leave (2023)
content:
Any civil officer having authority to apprehend offenders under the laws of the United
   States or of this Commonwealth, or any military officer subject to this part who has
   been authorized by the Governor by regulation, may summarily apprehend any person
   subject to this part absent without leave from the State military forces and deliver
   him into the custody of the State military forces.

content:
Persons subject to this part confined before, during or after trial by a military
   court shall be confined in a civilian or military confinement facility.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part IV. Military Justice›Chapter 51. General Provisions›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5105. Jurisdiction to try certain personnel
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part IV. Military Justice › Chapter 51. General Provisions › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5105. Jurisdiction to try certain personnel
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5105. Jurisdiction to try certain personnel (2023)
content:
(a) Discharge obtained fraudulently.--Each person subject to this part discharged from the State military forces who is
      later charged with having fraudulently obtained a discharge shall be, subject to section
      5708 (relating to statute of limitations), subject to trial by court-martial on said
      charge and shall after apprehension be subject to this part while in custody under
      the direction of the State military forces for that trial.  Upon conviction of said charge, the person shall be subject to trial by court-martial
      for all offenses under this part committed before the fraudulent discharge.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part IV. Military Justice›Chapter 52. Apprehension and Restraint›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5206. Reports and receiving of prisoners
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part IV. Military Justice › Chapter 52. Apprehension and Restraint › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5206. Reports and receiving of prisoners
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5206. Reports and receiving of prisoners (2023)
content:
(a) Duty to receive prisoner.--Unless otherwise authorized by law, no facility authorized to receive prisoners under
      section 5205 (relating to place of confinement) may refuse to receive or keep any
      prisoner subject to this part and committed to the facility's charge by a commissioned
      officer of the State military forces when the officer furnishes a statement, signed
      by the officer, of the offense charged against the prisoner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part IV. Military Justice›Chapter 51. General Provisions›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5104. Subject matter jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part IV. Military Justice › Chapter 51. General Provisions › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5104. Subject matter jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5104. Subject matter jurisdiction (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Subject matter jurisdiction is established if a nexus exists between an offense and
      the State military forces.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part III. Interstate Relations›Chapter 47. Fresh Pursuit by Military Forces›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 4702. Fresh pursuit by forces of other states
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part III. Interstate Relations › Chapter 47. Fresh Pursuit by Military Forces › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 4702. Fresh pursuit by forces of other states
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 4702. Fresh pursuit by forces of other states (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Any military forces, or organization, unit or detachment thereof, of another state,
      who are in fresh pursuit of insurrectionists, saboteurs, enemies or enemy forces,
      may continue such pursuit into this Commonwealth until the military or police forces
      of this Commonwealth or the forces of the United States have had a reasonable opportunity
      to take up the pursuit or to apprehend or capture such persons, and are hereby authorized
      to arrest or capture such persons within this Commonwealth while in fresh pursuit.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part IV. Military Justice›Chapter 52. Apprehension and Restraint›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5207. Punishment prohibited before trial
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part IV. Military Justice › Chapter 52. Apprehension and Restraint › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5207. Punishment prohibited before trial
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5207. Punishment prohibited before trial (2023)
content:
Subject to section 5804 (relating to effective date of sentence), no person subject
   to this part while being held for trial or the result of trial may be subjected to
   punishment or penalty other than arrest or confinement upon the charges pending against
   the person, nor shall the arrest or confinement imposed upon the person be any more
   rigorous than the circumstances required to insure the person's presence.  The person may be subjected to minor punishment during that period for infractions
   of discipline.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part III. Interstate Relations›Chapter 47. Fresh Pursuit by Military Forces›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 4701. Fresh pursuit by Commonwealth forces
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part III. Interstate Relations › Chapter 47. Fresh Pursuit by Military Forces › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 4701. Fresh pursuit by Commonwealth forces
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 4701. Fresh pursuit by Commonwealth forces (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--No military forces of this Commonwealth, other than the Pennsylvania National Guard,
      shall be required to serve outside the boundaries of this Commonwealth, except that
      any organization, unit or detachment of such forces, upon order of the officer in
      immediate command thereof, may continue in fresh pursuit of insurrectionists, saboteurs,
      enemies or enemy forces beyond the borders of this Commonwealth into another state
      until they are apprehended or captured by such organization, unit or detachment, or
      until the military or police forces of the other state or the forces of the United
      States have had a reasonable opportunity to take up the pursuit or to apprehend or
      capture such persons, provided such other state shall have given authority by law
      for such pursuit by such forces of the Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part IV. Military Justice›Chapter 51. General Provisions›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5106. Dismissal of commissioned officer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part IV. Military Justice › Chapter 51. General Provisions › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5106. Dismissal of commissioned officer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5106. Dismissal of commissioned officer (2023)
content:
(a) Court-martial proceedings.--Any commissioned officer subject to this part dismissed by order of the Governor may
      make a written application for trial by court-martial, setting forth, under oath,
      that the officer has been wrongfully dismissed.  In such event, the Governor, as soon as practicable, shall convene a general court-martial
      to try such officer on the charges on which the officer was dismissed.  A court-martial so convened shall have jurisdiction to try the dismissed officer
      on such charge, and the officer shall be considered to have waived the right to plead
      any statute of limitations applicable to any offense with which the officer is charged.  The court-martial may, as part of its sentence, adjudge the affirmance of the dismissal,
      but, if the court-martial acquits the accused or if the sentence adjudged, as finally
      approved or affirmed, does not include dismissal, the Adjutant General shall substitute
      for the dismissal ordered by the Governor a form of discharge authorized for administrative
      issue.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part IV. Military Justice›Chapter 52. Apprehension and Restraint›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5208. Delivery of offenders to civil authorities
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part IV. Military Justice › Chapter 52. Apprehension and Restraint › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5208. Delivery of offenders to civil authorities
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5208. Delivery of offenders to civil authorities (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Under such regulations as may be prescribed under this part, a person subject to this
      part accused of an offense against civil authority may be delivered, upon request,
      to the civil authority for trial or confinement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part IV. Military Justice›Chapter 51. General Provisions›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5103. Persons subject to part
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part IV. Military Justice › Chapter 51. General Provisions › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5103. Persons subject to part
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5103. Persons subject to part (2023)
content:
This part applies to all members of the State military forces who are not in a Federal
   status under which they are subject to the Uniform Code of Military Justice (64 Stat.
   109,10 U.S.C. § 801 et seq.).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part IV. Military Justice›Chapter 51. General Provisions›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5108. Judge advocates and legal officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part IV. Military Justice › Chapter 51. General Provisions › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5108. Judge advocates and legal officers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5108. Judge advocates and legal officers (2023)
content:
(a) Appointment of State Judge Advocate.--The Governor, on the recommendation of the Adjutant General, shall appoint a judge
      advocate officer of the State military forces as the State Judge Advocate.  To be eligible for appointment, such officer shall have been a member of the bar
      of the Supreme Court for at least five years.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part IV. Military Justice›Chapter 52. Apprehension and Restraint›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5201. Apprehension

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5201. Apprehension (2023)
content: (a) Persons authorized to apprehend.--Any person authorized by this part, by10 U.S.C. Ch. 47(relating to Uniform Code of Military Justice) or by regulations issued under:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part IV. Military Justice›Chapter 52. Apprehension and Restraint›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5203. Imposition of restraint
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part IV. Military Justice › Chapter 52. Apprehension and Restraint › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5203. Imposition of restraint
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5203. Imposition of restraint (2023)
content:
(a) Enlisted personnel.--An enlisted person subject to this part may be ordered into arrest or confinement
      by any commissioned officer by an order, oral or written, delivered in person or through
      other persons subject to this part or through any person authorized by this part to
      apprehend persons.  A commanding officer may authorize warrant officers, petty officers or noncommissioned
      officers to order enlisted members of his command or subject to his authority into
      arrest or confinement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part IV. Military Justice›Chapter 52. Apprehension and Restraint›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5204. Restraint of persons charged with offenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part IV. Military Justice › Chapter 52. Apprehension and Restraint › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5204. Restraint of persons charged with offenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5204. Restraint of persons charged with offenses (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Any person subject to this part charged with an offense under this part may be ordered
      into arrest or confinement.  When any person subject to this part is placed in arrest or confinement prior to
      trial, immediate steps shall be taken to inform the person of the specific wrong of
      which the person is accused, and diligent steps shall be taken to try the person or
      to dismiss the charges and release the person.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part IV. Military Justice›Chapter 52. Apprehension and Restraint›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5209. Confinement with enemy prisoners prohibited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part IV. Military Justice › Chapter 52. Apprehension and Restraint › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5209. Confinement with enemy prisoners prohibited
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5209. Confinement with enemy prisoners prohibited (2023)
content:
No member of the State military forces may be placed in confinement in immediate association
   with enemy prisoners or other foreign nationals who are not members of the armed forces.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part IV. Military Justice›Chapter 54. Courts-Martial Jurisdiction›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5402. Jurisdiction of courts-martial in general
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part IV. Military Justice › Chapter 54. Courts-Martial Jurisdiction › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5402. Jurisdiction of courts-martial in general
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5402. Jurisdiction of courts-martial in general (2023)
content:
Each force of the State military forces has court-martial jurisdiction over all members
   of the force who are subject to this part.  The Pennsylvania National Guard has court-martial jurisdiction over all members
   subject to this part.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part IV. Military Justice›Chapter 54. Courts-Martial Jurisdiction›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5403. Jurisdiction of general courts-martial

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5403. Jurisdiction of general courts-martial (2023)
content:
Subject to section 5402 (relating to jurisdiction of courts-martial in general), general
   courts-martial have jurisdiction to try persons subject to this part for any offense
   made punishable by this part and may, under such limitations as the Governor may prescribe,
   adjudge any punishment not prohibited by this part including any of the following
   punishments:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part IV. Military Justice›Chapter 53. Nonjudicial Punishment›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5301. Commanding officer's nonjudicial punishment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part IV. Military Justice › Chapter 53. Nonjudicial Punishment › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5301. Commanding officer's nonjudicial punishment

content:
(a) General rule.--Under such regulations as the Governor may prescribe, any commanding officer or officer-in-charge
      may impose disciplinary punishments for minor offenses without the intervention of
      a court-martial.  The Governor, the Adjutant General or a general officer or colonel in command may
      delegate the powers under this section to a principal assistant who is a member of
      the State military forces.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part IV. Military Justice›Chapter 54. Courts-Martial Jurisdiction›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5405. Jurisdiction of summary courts-martial
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part IV. Military Justice › Chapter 54. Courts-Martial Jurisdiction › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5405. Jurisdiction of summary courts-martial
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5405. Jurisdiction of summary courts-martial (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Subject to section 5402 (relating to jurisdiction of courts-martial in general), summary
      courts-martial shall have jurisdiction to try all persons subject to this part, except
      officers, cadets, candidates and midshipmen, for any offense made punishable by this
      part and may, under such limitations as the Governor may prescribe, adjudge any of
      the following punishments:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs›Part IV. Military Justice›Chapter 54. Courts-Martial Jurisdiction›PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5401. Courts-martial classified
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part IV. Military Justice › Chapter 54. Courts-Martial Jurisdiction › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5401. Courts-martial classified
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5401. Courts-martial classified (2023)
content: The three kinds of courts-martial in the State military forces are:

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 51 Pa.C.S.A. Military Affairs › Part IV. Military Justice › Chapter 54. Courts-Martial Jurisdiction › PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5404. Jurisdiction of special courts-martial
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5404. Jurisdiction of special courts-martial (2023)
content:
Subject to section 5402 (relating to jurisdiction of courts-martial in general), special
   courts-martial shall have jurisdiction to try persons subject to this part for any
   offense made punishable by this part and may, under such limitations as the Governor
   may prescribe, adjudge any of the following punishments:

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 51 Pa.C.S.A. § 5501. Who may convene general courts-martial (2023)
content: (a) General rule.--General courts-martial may be convened by any of the following:
