title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › B. Miners' Examining Boards and Certification of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-219. Power to administer oaths
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-219. Power to administer oaths (2023)
content:
For the purposes of this act the members of the said miners' examining boards shall
   have power to administer oaths.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›C. Mine Foreman and Assistant Mine Foreman›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-221. Mine foreman, assistant mine foreman and mine examiner, agent of Commonwealth
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › C. Mine Foreman and Assistant Mine Foreman › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-221. Mine foreman, assistant mine foreman and mine examiner, agent of Commonwealth
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-221. Mine foreman, assistant mine foreman and mine examiner, agent of Commonwealth (2023)
content:
Every mine foreman, assistant mine foreman and mine examiner under the provisions
   of the anthracite mining laws, shall represent the Commonwealth in the coal mine or
   colliery in which he is employed and be deemed to be an officer of the Commonwealth
   in enforcing the provisions of said mining laws and performing his duties thereunder.  He shall perform said duties during such times as the mine or colliery in which
   he is employed is in operation, and at such other times as, in the judgment of the
   operator or Secretary of Mines and Mineral Industries,1shall be necessary or desirable to make the mine or colliery safe for operations
   or to protect the health and safety of the employes of the operator or the protection
   and preservation of the property connected therewith.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›Article II. Boards of Examiners; Certification of Mine Foremen, Assistant Mine Foremen, Miners, Superintendents; General Mining Requirements›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-276. Safety lamps or electric lamps property of operator; competent person to examine
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › Article II. Boards of Examiners; Certification of Mine Foremen, Assistant Mine Foremen, Miners, Superintendents; General Mining Requirements › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-276. Safety lamps or electric lamps property of operator; competent person to examine
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-276. Safety lamps or electric lamps property of operator; competent person to examine (2023)
content:
Whenever safety lamps or electric lamps are required in any mine or part thereof,
   they shall be the property of the operator of said mine;  and a competent person,
   who shall be appointed for the purpose, shall examine every safety lamp and electric
   lamp immediately before it is taken into the workings for use and he shall ascertain
   that all safety lamps are clean, safe, and securely locked;  and safety lamps and
   electric lamps shall not be used until they have been so examined and found safe,
   and, in the case of safety lamps, clean and securely locked.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›Article II. Boards of Examiners; Certification of Mine Foremen, Assistant Mine Foremen, Miners, Superintendents; General Mining Requirements›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-275. Gassy mines--Unlawful to employ persons unable to understand regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › Article II. Boards of Examiners; Certification of Mine Foremen, Assistant Mine Foremen, Miners, Superintendents; General Mining Requirements › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-275. Gassy mines--Unlawful to employ persons unable to understand regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-275. Gassy mines--Unlawful to employ persons unable to understand regulations (2023)
content:
It shall not be lawful for any mine foreman or superintendent of any mine or colliery
   to employ any person who is not competent to understand the regulations of any mine
   evolving explosive gases:  Provided, That this rule shall not apply to a mine free
   from the said explosive gases.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›B. Miners' Examining Boards and Certification of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-214. Monthly meetings of miners' examining boards
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › B. Miners' Examining Boards and Certification of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-214. Monthly meetings of miners' examining boards
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-214. Monthly meetings of miners' examining boards (2023)
content:
It shall be the duty of each of the said boards to meet once every month and not oftener,
   and said meeting shall be public, and examine under oath all persons who shall desire
   to be employed as miners in their respective districts;  and said board shall grant
   such persons as may be qualified, certificates of competency or qualification which
   shall entitle the holders thereof to be employed as and to do the work of miners as
   may be expressed in said certificate, and such certificate shall be good and sufficient
   evidence of registration and competency under this act;  and the holder thereof shall
   be entitled to be registered without an examination in any other of the anthracite
   districts upon the payment of the fee herein provided.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›C. Mine Foreman and Assistant Mine Foreman›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-220. Mine foreman, assistant mine foreman, agent of operators
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › C. Mine Foreman and Assistant Mine Foreman › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-220. Mine foreman, assistant mine foreman, agent of operators
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-220. Mine foreman, assistant mine foreman, agent of operators (2023)
content:
The mine foreman and assistant mine foreman, shall be the agent of the operators,
   and such operators shall employ them and discharge them at will.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›Article II. Boards of Examiners; Certification of Mine Foremen, Assistant Mine Foremen, Miners, Superintendents; General Mining Requirements›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-281. Notices to mine inspector from operators or superintendents
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › Article II. Boards of Examiners; Certification of Mine Foremen, Assistant Mine Foremen, Miners, Superintendents; General Mining Requirements › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-281. Notices to mine inspector from operators or superintendents
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-281. Notices to mine inspector from operators or superintendents (2023)
content:
The operator or superintendent of a mine, bank, preparation plant or colliery shall
   without delay give notice in writing to the inspector of the district in which said
   mine or colliery is situated in any or all of the following cases:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›Article II. Boards of Examiners; Certification of Mine Foremen, Assistant Mine Foremen, Miners, Superintendents; General Mining Requirements›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-282. Monthly report of tonnage, man hours, source and quantity of coal
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › Article II. Boards of Examiners; Certification of Mine Foremen, Assistant Mine Foremen, Miners, Superintendents; General Mining Requirements › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-282. Monthly report of tonnage, man hours, source and quantity of coal
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-282. Monthly report of tonnage, man hours, source and quantity of coal (2023)
content:
On or before the fifteenth day of every month, the operator or superintendent of every
   mine, bank or colliery shall, with respect to the previous month, send by mail to
   the inspector of the district, on a form to be prescribed and furnished by the Department
   of Mines and Mineral Industries,1a report of the quantity of coal mined or produced and the man hours worked.  Operators of preparation plants shall furnish the mine inspector with a monthly
   and annual report showing the source and quantity of coal purchased for preparation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-224. Mine foreman; examine working places while men are or should be at work
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-224. Mine foreman; examine working places while men are or should be at work
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-224. Mine foreman; examine working places while men are or should be at work (2023)
content:
The mine foreman or his assistant shall visit and examine every working place in the
   mine each working shift while the men of such place are or should be at work, and
   shall direct and see that each and every working place is properly secured by props,
   timber, roof bolts or such other practical devices as may serve to secure the safety
   of the workmen, and that safety in all respects is assured by having all loose coal
   or rock pulled down or secured, and that no person shall be permitted to work in an
   unsafe place, unless it be for the purpose of making it secure, and a report of said
   examination shall be recorded in a book kept at the colliery for that purpose, and
   signed by the person making the same.  All such reports shall be made and signed at the end of each shift and countersigned
   within a period of one week by the mine foreman;  providing, however, if the mine
   is idle forty-eight hours or more, the mine foreman, assistant mine foreman or mine
   examiner shall examine every working place and the adjoining places the day before
   operations are resumed;  and all such entries shall be made and signed in ink in a
   manner similar to that heretofore described.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-223. Mine examiner; examine all mines prior to entrance of workmen; report of examination recorded in book
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-223. Mine examiner; examine all mines prior to entrance of workmen; report of examination recorded in book
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-223. Mine examiner; examine all mines prior to entrance of workmen; report of examination recorded in book (2023)
content:
In all mines the mine examiner shall make a careful examination every morning of all
   working places and traveling roads and all other places which might endanger the safety
   of the workmen, before the workmen shall enter the mine, and such examination shall
   be made with a safety lamp within three hours at most, before time for commencing
   work, and a workman shall not enter the mine or his working place until the said mine
   or part thereof and working place are reported to be safe.  Every report shall be recorded without delay in a book which shall be kept at the
   colliery for the purpose and shall be signed by the person making the examination.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-227. Proof of examination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-227. Proof of examination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-227. Proof of examination (2023)
content:
The person who makes said examinations as listed under sections 223, 224, 225 and
   2261shall establish proof of the same by marking plainly his initials and the date thereof
   at the face of each working place and all other places examined.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-229. Withdrawal of workmen, noxious gases
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-229. Withdrawal of workmen, noxious gases
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-229. Withdrawal of workmen, noxious gases (2023)
content:
If, at any time, it is found by the person in charge of a mine or any part thereof,
   that by reason of noxious gases prevailing in such mine or such part thereof, or of
   any cause whatever the mine or the said part is dangerous, every precaution shall
   be used to ensure the safety of the workmen;  and every workman, except such persons
   as may be required to remove the danger, shall be withdrawn from the mine, or such
   part thereof as is so found dangerous, until the said mine or said part thereof is
   examined by the mine foreman, assistant mine foreman or mine examiner and reported
   by him to be safe.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-225. Mine foreman; examine slopes, shafts, main roads, etc.
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-225. Mine foreman; examine slopes, shafts, main roads, etc.
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-225. Mine foreman; examine slopes, shafts, main roads, etc. (2023)
content:
The mine foreman, or some other competent person or persons to be designated by him,
   shall examine at least once every day all slopes, shafts, main roads, traveling ways,
   signal apparatus, pulleys and timbering and see that they are in safe and efficient
   working condition and a report of said examinations shall be recorded in a book, without
   delay, kept at the colliery for that purpose, and signed by the person making the
   same and countersigned by the mine foreman within a period of one week.  The book in which this and all other such reports are required to be made and recorded
   by the mine foreman, assistant foreman and mine examiner and others shall be securely
   bound and the manner and form in which the results of each examination shall be recorded
   shall be in accordance with a form furnished by the Department of Mines and Mineral
   Industries.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›Article II. Boards of Examiners; Certification of Mine Foremen, Assistant Mine Foremen, Miners, Superintendents; General Mining Requirements›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-280. Scene of accident; preservation of evidence
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › Article II. Boards of Examiners; Certification of Mine Foremen, Assistant Mine Foremen, Miners, Superintendents; General Mining Requirements › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-280. Scene of accident; preservation of evidence
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-280. Scene of accident; preservation of evidence (2023)
content:
After the occurrence of a mine accident which resulted in the death or serious injury
   to one or more persons and after the occurrence of any accident due to a fall of roof,
   the evidence surrounding such occurrence shall not be disturbed after recovery of
   bodies or removal of injured persons until an investigation of the accident has been
   completed by the mine inspector or inspectors:  Provided, however, That sufficient
   wreckage or debris may be moved to allow recovery work after disasters or continued
   general operation of the mine following fatalities not caused by mine fires or explosions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-230. Operator, superintendent, mine foreman to furnish supplies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-230. Operator, superintendent, mine foreman to furnish supplies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-230. Operator, superintendent, mine foreman to furnish supplies (2023)
content:
It shall be the duty of the operator, superintendent and mine foreman of every mine
   to furnish to the miners all props, ties, rails, timbers and materials necessary for
   the safe mining of coal and for the protection of the lives of the workmen.  Such props, ties, rails, timbers and materials shall be suitably prepared and shall
   be delivered to the workmen as near to their working places as they can be conveyed
   in ordinary mine cars free of charge.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-226. Mine foreman, assistant; weekly inspection; accessible abandoned portions of mine
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-226. Mine foreman, assistant; weekly inspection; accessible abandoned portions of mine
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-226. Mine foreman, assistant; weekly inspection; accessible abandoned portions of mine (2023)
content:
All accessible parts of an abandoned portion of a mine shall be carefully examined
   by the mine foreman, assistant mine foreman or mine examiner at least once a week,
   and all danger found existing therein shall be immediately removed.  A report of said examination shall be recorded in a book kept at the colliery for
   that purpose on the day the examination is made and shall be signed by the person
   making the same and countersigned by the mine foreman within a period of one week.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›Article II. Boards of Examiners; Certification of Mine Foremen, Assistant Mine Foremen, Miners, Superintendents; General Mining Requirements›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-283. Annual report February first for previous year
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › Article II. Boards of Examiners; Certification of Mine Foremen, Assistant Mine Foremen, Miners, Superintendents; General Mining Requirements › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-283. Annual report February first for previous year
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-283. Annual report February first for previous year (2023)
content:
On or before the first day of February, in each year, the operator or superintendent
   of every mine, bank or colliery, shall send to the inspector of the district, a correct
   report specifying with respect to the year ending December 31, previously, the name
   of the operator and officials of the mine with their post office addresses;  the quantity
   of coal mined;  the amount of powder or other explosives consumed;  the number of
   persons employed above and below ground in or about such colliery or bank, classifying
   the persons so employed.  The report shall be in such form as may be from time to time prescribed by the Department
   of Mines and Mineral Industries.1Blank forms for said report shall be furnished by the Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-231. Failure to furnish supplies, negligence
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-231. Failure to furnish supplies, negligence
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-231. Failure to furnish supplies, negligence (2023)
content:
A failure to furnish timbers and materials as required shall be deemed an offense
   against this act, and shall be taken to be negligence per se on the part of the operator,
   superintendent and mine foreman of such mine, in an1action for the recovery of damages for accidents resulting from the insufficient
   propping of such mine, through failure to furnish the necessary props or timbers.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›C. Mine Foreman and Assistant Mine Foreman›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-222. Mine foreman; ventilation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › C. Mine Foreman and Assistant Mine Foreman › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-222. Mine foreman; ventilation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-222. Mine foreman; ventilation (2023)
content:
The mine foreman shall have charge of all matters pertaining to ventilation, and the
   speed of the ventilators shall be particularly under his charge and direction;  and
   any operator or superintendent who shall cause the mine foreman to disregard the provisions
   of this act shall be amenable in the same manner as the mine foreman.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-232. Unlawful to employ person not competent to understand regulations concerning explosive gases
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-232. Unlawful to employ person not competent to understand regulations concerning explosive gases
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-232. Unlawful to employ person not competent to understand regulations concerning explosive gases (2023)
content:
It shall not be lawful for any mine foreman or superintendent of any mine or colliery
   to employ any person who is not competent to understand the regulations of any mine
   evolving explosive gases;  provided that this rule shall not apply to a mine free
   from the said explosive gases.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›E. Mine Foreman; Blasting›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-234. Certified miners only to blast coal or rock
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › E. Mine Foreman; Blasting › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-234. Certified miners only to blast coal or rock
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-234. Certified miners only to blast coal or rock (2023)
content:
No person shall be permitted to blast coal or rock unless he is a certified miner
   and in the opinion of the mine foreman is qualified by experience and judgment to
   perform the work with ordinary safety.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›F. Mine Foreman; Drainage›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-237. Passageways, well drained
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › F. Mine Foreman; Drainage › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-237. Passageways, well drained
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-237. Passageways, well drained (2023)
content:
Passageways used by persons and roads used for transportation in any mine shall be
   well drained.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-228. Stations at entrance to mine or parts of mine
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › D. Mine Foreman and Mine Examiner; Examination and Safety of Working Places › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-228. Stations at entrance to mine or parts of mine
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-228. Stations at entrance to mine or parts of mine (2023)
content:
A station or stations shall be established at the entrance to each mine or different
   parts of each mine, as the case may require, and a workman shall not pass beyond any
   such station until the mine or part of the mine beyond the same has been inspected
   by the mine foreman, assistant mine foreman or mine examiner and reported to be safe.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-240. Tight cartridge not to be rammed into blast hole
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-240. Tight cartridge not to be rammed into blast hole
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-240. Tight cartridge not to be rammed into blast hole (2023)
content:
In charging holes for blasting in coal, slate or rock in any mine, a tight cartridge
   shall not be rammed into the hole by any means.  Only nonmetallic tamping bars shall be used for charging and tamping blast holes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-244. Shall not detonate blast in presence of methane
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-244. Shall not detonate blast in presence of methane
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-244. Shall not detonate blast in presence of methane (2023)
content:
Blasts shall not be detonated in any place where methane can be detected with a flame
   safety lamp.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›E. Mine Foreman; Blasting›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-235. Firing lines, supervision of mine foreman
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › E. Mine Foreman; Blasting › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-235. Firing lines, supervision of mine foreman
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-235. Firing lines, supervision of mine foreman (2023)
content:
The location of the firing lines and safety breaks shall be under the supervision
   of the mine foreman or his assistant.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›E. Mine Foreman; Blasting›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-233. Mine foreman, permission for blasts in mine where locked safety lamps are in use
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › E. Mine Foreman; Blasting › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-233. Mine foreman, permission for blasts in mine where locked safety lamps are in use
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-233. Mine foreman, permission for blasts in mine where locked safety lamps are in use (2023)
content:
No blast shall be fired in any mine where locked safety lamps are used except by permission
   of the mine foreman or his assistants.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-242. Leg wires of electric detonators to be kept shunted
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-242. Leg wires of electric detonators to be kept shunted
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-242. Leg wires of electric detonators to be kept shunted (2023)
content:
The leg wires of electric detonators shall be kept shunted until ready to connect
   to the firing cable.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›F. Mine Foreman; Drainage›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-238. Regulations, places approaching inaccessible workings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › F. Mine Foreman; Drainage › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-238. Regulations, places approaching inaccessible workings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-238. Regulations, places approaching inaccessible workings (2023)
content:
Whenever a place is approaching inaccessible workings, the operator shall establish
   and clearly show on the map furnished the mine foreman a stopping distance not less
   than one hundred feet from the said inaccessible workings and such stopping point
   shall not be passed until after the coal company officials, the mining engineer and
   the mine inspector have agreed on the width of any such approaching place or places,
   the point at which test holes shall be started and the location of the test holes.  The test holes shall not be less than twenty feet in advance of the working face
   with sufficient flank holes on each side of said place.  No such stopping distance shall be less than one hundred feet from the said inaccessible
   abandoned workings, nor need it be greater than the distance calculated in accordance
   with the rule commonly used in the establishing of barrier pillars, namely, one per
   cent of the depth below drainage times the thickness of the coal seam plus thickness
   of seam times five, excepting in such cases where calculation in accordance with said
   rule establishes a stopping distance of less than one hundred feet.  This act does not permit the driving of gangways, chambers or other excavations
   into barriers which are subjected to their maximum water pressure, as calculated in
   accordance with the rule here established, unless the said waterhead is reduced by
   pumping or other means.  The term“mining engineer,”as used in this act, shall mean the person who shall, in behalf of the operator,
   have charge or general supervision of the work of compiling the mine map.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-245. Extinguish gas ignited by blast, notify mine foreman
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-245. Extinguish gas ignited by blast, notify mine foreman
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-245. Extinguish gas ignited by blast, notify mine foreman (2023)
content:
When gas is ignited by blast or otherwise, the person igniting the same shall immediately
   extinguish it, if possible, and notify the mine foreman or his assistant of the fact,
   and workmen must see that no gas blowers are left burning upon leaving their working
   places.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-243. Examine for gas before and after firing blast
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-243. Examine for gas before and after firing blast
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-243. Examine for gas before and after firing blast (2023)
content:
Examinations for gas shall be made immediately before firing each blast or group of
   blasts.  Before work is commenced an examination of the face shall be made.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›E. Mine Foreman; Blasting›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-236. Mine foreman to supervise misfires
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › E. Mine Foreman; Blasting › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-236. Mine foreman to supervise misfires
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-236. Mine foreman to supervise misfires (2023)
content:
The handling of a misfired blast shall be under the supervision of the mine foreman
   or his assistant.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-239. Secure roof and sides
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-239. Secure roof and sides
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-239. Secure roof and sides (2023)
content:
Any person having charge of a working place in any mine shall keep the roof and sides
   thereof properly secured by timber or otherwise so as to prevent such roof and sides
   from falling, and he shall not do any work or permit any work to be done under loose
   or dangerous material except for the purpose of securing the same.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-247. Thirty minute waiting period before returning to misfire
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-247. Thirty minute waiting period before returning to misfire
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-247. Thirty minute waiting period before returning to misfire (2023)
content:
Where misfires occur with electric detonators, a waiting period of at least thirty
   minutes shall elapse before anyone returns to the misfired hole or holes.  The blasting wires shall be disconnected from the blasting battery and the ends
   of the blasting wires short-circuited before returning to the misfire hole or holes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-246. Misfired explosives not to be withdrawn
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-246. Misfired explosives not to be withdrawn
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-246. Misfired explosives not to be withdrawn (2023)
content:
A charge of explosives in coal, slate or rock, which has misfired shall not be withdrawn
   or the hole reopened.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-241. Issue warning to all persons in proximity before firing blast
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-241. Issue warning to all persons in proximity before firing blast
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-241. Issue warning to all persons in proximity before firing blast (2023)
content:
When a miner is about to fire a blast he shall notify the persons in the adjoining
   places and shall have received a reply therefrom and shall give sufficient alarm so
   that any person or persons who may be approaching shall be warned of the danger before
   firing the blast.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-249. Order props, ties, rails, timber, materials at least one day in advance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-249. Order props, ties, rails, timber, materials at least one day in advance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-249. Order props, ties, rails, timber, materials at least one day in advance (2023)
content:
Every workman in want of props, ties, rails, timbers or materials shall notify the
   mine foreman or his assistant of the fact at least one day in advance, giving the
   length of the props or timber required;  and in case of danger from loose roof or
   sides, he shall not continue to cut or load coal or do any other work within the danger
   area until the said props and timber have been properly furnished and the place made
   secure.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-252. Accumulation of gas not to be removed by brushing
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-252. Accumulation of gas not to be removed by brushing
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-252. Accumulation of gas not to be removed by brushing (2023)
content: An accumulation of gas in mines shall not be removed by brushing.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-250. Notify mine foreman of any dangerous condition
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-250. Notify mine foreman of any dangerous condition
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-250. Notify mine foreman of any dangerous condition (2023)
content:
Any miner or other workman who shall discover anything wrong with the ventilating
   current or with the condition of the roof, side, timber, or roadway or with any other
   part of the mine in general, such as would lead him to suspect danger to himself or
   his fellow workmen or to the property of his employer, shall immediately report the
   same to the mine foreman or other certified person for the time being in charge of
   that portion of the mine.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-255. Examine place for gas prior to start of work and other times
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-255. Examine place for gas prior to start of work and other times
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-255. Examine place for gas prior to start of work and other times (2023)
content:
Before the commencement of work the miner in charge shall examine his working place
   for gas and oxygen deficiency with an approved safety lamp and thoroughly test the
   roof, face and ribs with a suitable testing bar.  A similar test shall also be made before starting any machine, before and after
   each blast fired during the working shift.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-254. System of roof support
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-254. System of roof support
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-254. System of roof support (2023)
content:
The roof in all underground areas shall be supported as outlined in sections 269 and
   270 of this article.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-251. Penalty endangering lives, health of workmen, security of property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-251. Penalty endangering lives, health of workmen, security of property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-251. Penalty endangering lives, health of workmen, security of property (2023)
content:
Any person or persons who shall knowingly or wilfully damage, or without proper authority
   remove or render useless any fencing, means of signaling, apparatus, instrument or
   machine, or shall throw open or obstruct any airway, or open a ventilating door and
   not have the same closed, or enter a place in or about a mine against caution, or
   carry fire, open lights, matches or any device for making lights or fire not authorized
   or approved in places where safety lamps are used, or handle without proper authority,
   or disturb any machinery or cars, or do any other act or thing whereby the lives or
   health of persons or the security of the property in or about a mine or colliery are
   endangered, shall be guilty of an offense against this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-256. Correct unsafe roof, face or rib conditions before other work started
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-256. Correct unsafe roof, face or rib conditions before other work started
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-256. Correct unsafe roof, face or rib conditions before other work started (2023)
content:
If roof, face or rib conditions are found to be unsafe, they shall be corrected by
   taking down loose material, or shall be securely supported, before other work is started.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-257. Roof support to be placed promptly as soon as room available
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-257. Roof support to be placed promptly as soon as room available
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-257. Roof support to be placed promptly as soon as room available (2023)
content:
All props and timbers shall be placed promptly, as soon as the room to do so is made
   available, and shall be adequate and proper for the needs of the place.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-248. Method of removing misfired explosives
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-248. Method of removing misfired explosives
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-248. Method of removing misfired explosives (2023)
content:
Explosives in misfired blast holes shall be removed by drilling a separate blast hole
   two feet distant from and parallel to the hole containing the misfired charge and
   then charging and detonating the explosives in this new hole.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-263. Superintendent to provide supplies and materials to mine foreman
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-263. Superintendent to provide supplies and materials to mine foreman
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-263. Superintendent to provide supplies and materials to mine foreman (2023)
content:
It shall be the duty of every superintendent, on behalf and at the expense of the
   operator, to keep on hand at each mine at all times a sufficient quantity of all materials
   and supplies required to preserve the health and safety of the employes, as ordered
   by the mine foreman, and required by this act.  If, for any reason, the superintendent cannot procure the necessary materials or
   supplies as aforesaid, he shall at once notify the mine foreman, whose duty it shall
   be to withdraw the men from the mine, or portion of mine, until such materials or
   supplies are received.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-262. Safety committee; superintendent; monthly report of safety meeting
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-262. Safety committee; superintendent; monthly report of safety meeting
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-262. Safety committee; superintendent; monthly report of safety meeting (2023)
content:
If a safety committee has not been selected by the employes, a safety committee consisting
   of the mine superintendent, mine foreman, at least one assistant mine foreman, or,
   in the absence of such officials, a designated qualified agent or agents of the operator
   and at least two persons selected by the employes working in the mine shall be formed
   to acquaint the workers with the shortcomings of the mine as indicated by the State
   mine inspector and prescribing appropriate precautions and remedial action.  The mine superintendent shall execute, on behalf of the safety committee a monthly
   report on the last work day of each calendar month with the Department of Mines and
   Mineral Industries1containing a statement that the committee met and a summary of the information that
   was furnished to the employes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-261. Superintendent or operator, supervision, direction and control of all employes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-261. Superintendent or operator, supervision, direction and control of all employes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-261. Superintendent or operator, supervision, direction and control of all employes (2023)
content:
The operator or superintendent of a mine or colliery shall use every precaution to
   insure the safety of the workmen in all cases, whether provided for in this act or
   not, and shall have supervision, direction, and control of the mine foreman and all
   other mine employes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-265. Superintendent or operator to provide and maintain constant and adequate supply of pure air for mine or colliery
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-265. Superintendent or operator to provide and maintain constant and adequate supply of pure air for mine or colliery
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-265. Superintendent or operator to provide and maintain constant and adequate supply of pure air for mine or colliery (2023)
content:
The operator or superintendent of every mine or colliery shall provide and maintain
   a constant and adequate supply of pure air for the same, as hereinafter provided for
   in article V.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-258. Props, timbers, properly hitched, spragged, blocked, lined and lagged
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-258. Props, timbers, properly hitched, spragged, blocked, lined and lagged
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-258. Props, timbers, properly hitched, spragged, blocked, lined and lagged (2023)
content: All props and timbers shall be properly hitched.  It necessary they shall be spragged or braced, blocked, lined and lagged and cribbed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-264. Authorize mine foreman to employ assistants
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-264. Authorize mine foreman to employ assistants
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-264. Authorize mine foreman to employ assistants (2023)
content:
Whenever a mine foreman cannot personally carry out the provisions of this act so
   far as they pertain to him, the operator or superintendent shall authorize him to
   employ a sufficient number of competent persons to act as his assistants, who shall
   be subject to his orders.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›G. Duties of Miners›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-253. Props or timbers supporting roof not to be removed by cutting, removed by blasting or prop puller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › G. Duties of Miners › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-253. Props or timbers supporting roof not to be removed by cutting, removed by blasting or prop puller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-253. Props or timbers supporting roof not to be removed by cutting, removed by blasting or prop puller (2023)
content:
No person or persons working in any coal mine or colliery shall cut any props or timbers
   while the same are in position to support the roof or sides.  When it becomes necessary to remove any of the said props or timbers they shall
   be removed by blasting or by means of a prop puller.  Such prop puller, however, shall be designed and constructed with ropes or chains
   of sufficient length that the person operating the device will not be exposed to the
   danger of a falling roof or falling coal resulting from the removal of such props
   and timbers.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-260. Superintendent shall direct and provide means for law compliance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-260. Superintendent shall direct and provide means for law compliance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-260. Superintendent shall direct and provide means for law compliance (2023)
content:
The superintendent shall not obstruct the mine foreman or other officials in the fulfillment
   of any of their duties as required by this act, but he shall direct, provide the means,
   and see to it that the mine foreman and all other employes under him comply with the
   law in all its provisions.  He shall give immediate attention to any violation of the law called to his attention
   by the mine inspector.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-259. Mine not to be operated without supervision of mine foreman
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-259. Mine not to be operated without supervision of mine foreman
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-259. Mine not to be operated without supervision of mine foreman (2023)
content:
No mine shall be operated without the supervision of a mine foreman.  In case any mine is worked without a mine foreman, the operator or superintendent
   thereof shall be subjected to a penalty of fifty dollars ($50) per day for each day
   during which the said mine is operated.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-269. Minimum timbering or other roof support methods adopted
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-269. Minimum timbering or other roof support methods adopted
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-269. Minimum timbering or other roof support methods adopted (2023)
content:
Where roof support is required, minimum timbering, or other roof support methods,
   suitable to the roof conditions of each mine or part of a mine shall be adopted by
   the operator and complied with.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-266. Superintendent or operator to employ outside foreman
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-266. Superintendent or operator to employ outside foreman
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-266. Superintendent or operator to employ outside foreman (2023)
content:
The operator or superintendent of a colliery shall place a competent person to be
   called “outside foreman,” in charge of the breaker and the outside work of such colliery,
   who shall direct and as far as practicable see that the provisions of this act are
   complied with in respect to the breaker, outside machinery, ropes, cages and all other
   things pertaining to the outside work, unless otherwise provided for in this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-268. Superintendent or operator to furnish reports to mine inspectors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-268. Superintendent or operator to furnish reports to mine inspectors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-268. Superintendent or operator to furnish reports to mine inspectors (2023)
content:
The operator or superintendent of each mine or colliery shall furnish the district
   mine inspector with all reports and notices hereinbefore or hereinafter cited in this
   act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-275. Gassy mines--Unlawful to employ persons unable to understand regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-275. Gassy mines--Unlawful to employ persons unable to understand regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-275. Gassy mines--Unlawful to employ persons unable to understand regulations (2023)
content:
It shall not be lawful for any mine foreman or superintendent of any mine or colliery
   to employ any person who is not competent to understand the regulations of any mine
   evolving explosive gases:  Provided, That this rule shall not apply to a mine free
   from the said explosive gases.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-267. Superintendent or operator to have right to hire and discharge employes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-267. Superintendent or operator to have right to hire and discharge employes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-267. Superintendent or operator to have right to hire and discharge employes (2023)
content:
The right to hire and discharge employes, the management of the mine, and the direction
   of the working forces, are vested exclusively in the operator or superintendent and
   no person or persons, association or associations, organization or organizations,
   or corporation or corporations, shall interfere with or attempt to interfere with,
   abridge or attempt to abridge, in any manner whatsoever, such right, provided that
   this does not invalidate any existing or future contract.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-274. Gassy mines--No light or fire except approved safety lamps and electric lamps
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-274. Gassy mines--No light or fire except approved safety lamps and electric lamps
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-274. Gassy mines--No light or fire except approved safety lamps and electric lamps (2023)
content:
In each part of all gassy mines no light or fire, other than a locked safety lamp,
   or a locked safety lamp and electric lamp, both of a type which shall be first approved
   by the Department of Mines and Mineral Industries,1shall be allowed or used in such part.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-276. Safety lamps or electric lamps property of operator; competent person to examine
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-276. Safety lamps or electric lamps property of operator; competent person to examine
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-276. Safety lamps or electric lamps property of operator; competent person to examine (2023)
content:
Whenever safety lamps or electric lamps are required in any mine or part thereof,
   they shall be the property of the operator of said mine;  and a competent person,
   who shall be appointed for the purpose, shall examine every safety lamp and electric
   lamp immediately before it is taken into the workings for use and he shall ascertain
   that all safety lamps are clean, safe, and securely locked;  and safety lamps and
   electric lamps shall not be used until they have been so examined and found safe,
   and, in the case of safety lamps, clean and securely locked.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-273. Posting of copy of mining law in pamphlet form
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-273. Posting of copy of mining law in pamphlet form
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-273. Posting of copy of mining law in pamphlet form (2023)
content:
For the purpose of making known the provisions of this act to all persons employed
   in or about such mine or colliery to which this act applies, a copy of the law in
   pamphlet form shall be posted in some conspicuous place or places at the mine or colliery,
   where it may be conveniently read by the persons employed, and so often as the same
   become obliterated or destroyed the operator or superintendent shall cause it to be
   renewed with all reasonable dispatch.  Any person who pulls down, injures or defaces such copy of the law when posted up
   in pursuance of the provisions of this act, shall be guilty of an offense against
   this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-278. Acetylene burners or blow torches
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-278. Acetylene burners or blow torches
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-278. Acetylene burners or blow torches (2023)
content:
Welding, cutting or soldering with arc or flame, use of blow torch in underground
   face regions shall be done under the direct supervision of the mine foreman or assistant
   mine foreman who shall test for methane before and during such operations in gassy
   mines and shall make a diligent search for fire after such operations in all mines.  Suitable fire extinguishers shall be immediately available during such welding,
   cutting, soldering or use of blow torch.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-272. Employment of boys under eighteen years of age
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-272. Employment of boys under eighteen years of age
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-272. Employment of boys under eighteen years of age (2023)
content:
No boy under eighteen years of age and no woman or girl of any age, shall be employed
   or permitted to be in any mine for the purpose of employment therein.  Nor shall a woman or girl of any age, be employed or permitted to be in or about
   the outside structures or workings of a colliery for the purpose of employment, but
   it is provided, however, that this prohibition shall not affect the employment of
   a female of at least eighteen years of age in an office or in the performance of clerical
   work at a colliery.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-271. Roof-bolt support requirements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-271. Roof-bolt support requirements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-271. Roof-bolt support requirements (2023)
content:
Should an operator desire to use roof bolts in lieu of props or timber as conventionally
   used, he shall not be permitted to do so unless permission in writing is first obtained
   from the Secretary of Mines and Mineral Industries.1The Secretary of Mines and Mineral Industries shall grant such permission after
   he has received the approval of a commission of three mine inspectors, one of whom
   shall be the inspector in whose district the mine for which permission is sought to
   use roof bolts is located.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-277. Matches, smokers' articles in gassy mine unlawful; mine foreman to cause search
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-277. Matches, smokers' articles in gassy mine unlawful; mine foreman to cause search
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-277. Matches, smokers' articles in gassy mine unlawful; mine foreman to cause search (2023)
content:
It shall be unlawful for any person or persons, working in a mine or portion of a
   mine, which is worked by locked safety lamps or locked safety lamps and electric lamps,
   to carry into the mine matches, smokers' articles, or any other material or article
   which may cause fire.  To prevent such articles being carried into a dangerous mine or section thereof,
   the mine foreman, when he sees fit, shall cause a search of the men for such articles.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-280. Scene of accident; preservation of evidence
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-280. Scene of accident; preservation of evidence
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-280. Scene of accident; preservation of evidence (2023)
content:
After the occurrence of a mine accident which resulted in the death or serious injury
   to one or more persons and after the occurrence of any accident due to a fall of roof,
   the evidence surrounding such occurrence shall not be disturbed after recovery of
   bodies or removal of injured persons until an investigation of the accident has been
   completed by the mine inspector or inspectors:  Provided, however, That sufficient
   wreckage or debris may be moved to allow recovery work after disasters or continued
   general operation of the mine following fatalities not caused by mine fires or explosions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-270. Roof support plan not to exceed six feet centers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-270. Roof support plan not to exceed six feet centers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-270. Roof support plan not to exceed six feet centers (2023)
content:
Such plan shall specify the maximum center line distance between props, timbers, roof
   bolts or such other practical devices which shall, in no instance exceed six feet.  However, if conditions of the seam or seam roof warrant, additional roof support
   shall be placed without delay.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-281. Notices to mine inspector from operators or superintendents
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-281. Notices to mine inspector from operators or superintendents
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-281. Notices to mine inspector from operators or superintendents (2023)
content:
The operator or superintendent of a mine, bank, preparation plant or colliery shall
   without delay give notice in writing to the inspector of the district in which said
   mine or colliery is situated in any or all of the following cases:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-279. Notices of accidents to mine inspectors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-279. Notices of accidents to mine inspectors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-279. Notices of accidents to mine inspectors (2023)
content:
Notices of death or serious injuries resulting from accidents and any injury resulting
   from a roof-fall accident in or about mines or collieries, shall be made to the inspector
   of mines immediately and shall specify the name, age and occupation of the person
   killed or injured, and also the nature and character of the accident and of the injury
   caused thereby.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-283. Annual report February first for previous year
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-283. Annual report February first for previous year
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-283. Annual report February first for previous year (2023)
content:
On or before the first day of February, in each year, the operator or superintendent
   of every mine, bank or colliery, shall send to the inspector of the district, a correct
   report specifying with respect to the year ending December 31, previously, the name
   of the operator and officials of the mine with their post office addresses;  the quantity
   of coal mined;  the amount of powder or other explosives consumed;  the number of
   persons employed above and below ground in or about such colliery or bank, classifying
   the persons so employed.  The report shall be in such form as may be from time to time prescribed by the Department
   of Mines and Mineral Industries.1Blank forms for said report shall be furnished by the Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-282. Monthly report of tonnage, man hours, source and quantity of coal
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › H. General Responsibility of the Superintendent › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-282. Monthly report of tonnage, man hours, source and quantity of coal
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-282. Monthly report of tonnage, man hours, source and quantity of coal (2023)
content:
On or before the fifteenth day of every month, the operator or superintendent of every
   mine, bank or colliery shall, with respect to the previous month, send by mail to
   the inspector of the district, on a form to be prescribed and furnished by the Department
   of Mines and Mineral Industries,1a report of the quantity of coal mined or produced and the man hours worked.  Operators of preparation plants shall furnish the mine inspector with a monthly
   and annual report showing the source and quantity of coal purchased for preparation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›Article III. Maps and Plans›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-301. Operator or superintendent--Map scale 1″=100'
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › Article III. Maps and Plans › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-301. Operator or superintendent--Map scale 1″=100'
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-301. Operator or superintendent--Map scale 1″=100' (2023)
content:
The operator or superintendent of every coal mine or colliery shall make, or cause
   to be made, an accurate map or plan of the workings or excavations of such coal mine
   or colliery, on a scale of one hundred feet to the inch, which map or plan shall exhibit
   the workings or excavations in each and every seam of coal and the tunnels and passages
   connecting with such workings or excavations.  It shall state in degrees the general inclination of the strata with any material
   deflection therein in said workings or excavations, the seam thickness and shall also
   state the tidal elevations of the bottom of each and every shaft, slope, tunnel, and
   gangway, and of any other point in the mine or on the surface where such elevation
   shall be deemed necessary by the inspector.  The map or plan shall show the number of the last survey station and date of each
   survey on the gangways or the most advanced workings and the location and identity
   of each working face advanced and the location of each area of pillar removed since
   the last inspection.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›Article III. Maps and Plans›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-306. Operator fails to furnish map to inspector, stop order issued
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › Article III. Maps and Plans › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-306. Operator fails to furnish map to inspector, stop order issued
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-306. Operator fails to furnish map to inspector, stop order issued (2023)
content:
Whenever the operator or superintendent of any coal mine or colliery shall neglect
   or refuse, or from any cause not satisfactory to the inspector, shall fail, for a
   period of one month, to furnish to the inspector the map or plan of said colliery
   or of the extensions thereto, as provided for in this act, the inspector is hereby
   authorized to issue a stop order until an accurate map or plan of the said coal mine
   or colliery is furnished to him.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›Article III. Maps and Plans›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-303. Copy of map or plan furnished mine inspector
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › Article III. Maps and Plans › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-303. Copy of map or plan furnished mine inspector
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-303. Copy of map or plan furnished mine inspector (2023)
content:
A true copy of which map or plan, the said operator or superintendent shall deposit
   with the inspector of mines for the district in which the said coal mine or colliery
   is situated, showing the workings of each seam.  If so desired by the inspector, a copy may be made on a separate sheet of tracing
   muslin.  One copy of the said map or plan shall be kept at the colliery and a copy shall
   be furnished by the superintendent or mine foreman to the inspector upon his arrival
   at the mine for the purpose of making a periodic inspection.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining›Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965›Article III. Maps and Plans›PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-302. Map to show boundary lines, pipe lines, streams, roads, etc.
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 52 P.S. Mines and Mining › Chapter 6. Pennsylvania Anthracite Coal Mine Act of 1965 › Article III. Maps and Plans › PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-302. Map to show boundary lines, pipe lines, streams, roads, etc.
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 52 P.S. § 70-302. Map to show boundary lines, pipe lines, streams, roads, etc. (2023)
content:
The map shall also accurately show the boundary lines of the lands of the said coal
   mine or colliery and the proximity of the workings thereto, all pipelines, streams
