title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.204. Delinquent actuarial valuation reports and experience investigations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.204. Delinquent actuarial valuation reports and experience investigations (2023)
content:
If a complete actuarial valuation report or experience investigation is not filed
   in a timely fashion, any and all financing which is provided to the municipality by
   the Commonwealth and is dedicated for pension plan purposes shall be withheld until
   the report or investigation is filed.  If a municipality fails to file an actuarial valuation report or experience investigation,
   the commission shall have the report or investigation prepared and the municipality
   shall reimburse the commission for the actual cost of the preparation of the report
   or investigation.  The commission shall issue rules and regulations specifying the procedures which
   the commission shall follow in obtaining delinquent actuarial valuation reports or
   experience investigations.

   to or elimination of requirements for the contents of actuarial valuation reports

   governing the issuance of rules and regulations by Commonwealth agencies.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.203. Contents of experience investigation (2023)
content:
(a) Generally.--The experience investigation shall contain sufficient information to substantiate
      the actuarial assumptions upon which the actuarial exhibits of the most recent actuarial
      report shall be based.  The experience investigation shall be prepared only by an approved actuary.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.206. Requirement for additional information in certain instances (2023)
content:
The commission may request any additional information, data or calculations in connection
   with any required actuarial valuation report or experience investigation which it
   deems necessary or desirable.  The requested information, data or calculations shall be transmitted to the commission
   as soon as is practicable following receipt of the request.

Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.209. Authorization for alternate amortization schedules to accommodate extraordinary events
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.209. Authorization for alternate amortization schedules to accommodate extraordinary events
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.209. Authorization for alternate amortization schedules to accommodate extraordinary events (2023)
content:
In the preparation of an actuarial valuation report as of the beginning of the plan
   year occurring in 2005 or thereafter, a municipality may adopt an alternate amortization
   schedule rather than the amortization schedule specified in section 202(b)(4)1for any increment of unfunded actuarial accrued liability that exceeds $9,000,000,
   causes at least a 30% increase in the aggregate actuarial accrued liability of the
   pension plan and is attributable to a single benefit enhancement granted prior to
   January 1, 2004, and being newly recognized in the actuarial valuation report.  The alternate amortization schedule shall be formally adopted by the governing body
   of the municipality and shall provide for an amortization target date that results
   in an amortization period of 30 years, level percentage amortization payments increasing
   by no more than 5% annually if adopted in an actuarial valuation report with a valuation
   date in 2005 and level dollar amortization payments if adopted in an actuarial valuation
   report with a valuation date occurring after December 31, 2005.  The initial and all subsequent actuarial valuation reports filed with the commission
   during the operation of the alternate amortization schedule shall separately disclose
   the initial amount of the increment of unfunded actuarial accrued liability, the date
   that the alternate amortization schedule was established, the amortization target
   date, the original amortization period, the remaining balance of the increment of
   unfunded actuarial accrued liability and the amortization payment for the year following
   the valuation date of the actuarial valuation report.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.202. Contents of actuarial valuation report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.202. Contents of actuarial valuation report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.202. Contents of actuarial valuation report (2023)
content:
(a) Generally.--The actuarial valuation report shall contain actuarial exhibits, financial exhibits
      and demographic exhibits.  The actuarial exhibits shall be prepared and certified by an approved actuary.  The remaining exhibits may be prepared by a qualified person other than an approved
      actuary.  The financial and demographic exhibits shall be prepared as of the end of the prior
      year.  The submission by a municipality of a single report setting forth the various required
      contents items in total for the various pension plans associated with the Pennsylvania
      Municipal Retirement System shall be deemed to be compliance by that municipality
      with the requirements of this chapter only if the report also separately sets forth
      the various required contents items for the municipality.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.207. Actuarial valuation and experience investigation expenses allowable
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.207. Actuarial valuation and experience investigation expenses allowable
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.207. Actuarial valuation and experience investigation expenses allowable (2023)
content:
Notwithstanding any provision of law, municipal ordinance, municipal resolution, municipal
   charter, pension plan agreement or pension plan contract to the contrary, the expenses
   attributable to the preparation of any actuarial valuation report or experience investigation
   required pursuant to this chapter shall be an allowable administrative expense payable
   from the assets of the pension plan.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.201. Requirement to file actuarial valuation report or experience investigation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.201. Requirement to file actuarial valuation report or experience investigation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.201. Requirement to file actuarial valuation report or experience investigation (2023)
content:
(a) Actuarial valuation report required.--Each municipality which has established or maintains a pension plan for its employees,
      including any municipality which participates in the Pennsylvania Municipal Retirement
      System, shall cause to be made actuarial valuation reports.  Actuarial valuation reports shall be made biennially, unless the applicable municipality
      is applying or has previously applied for supplemental State assistance pursuant to
      section 603,1whereupon actuarial valuation reports shall be made annually.  Each municipality which has established or maintains a pension plan for its employees
      and has an active, vested inactive and benefit recipient membership equal to or greater
      than 1,000 shall also cause experience investigations to be made.  Experience investigations shall be made quadrennially.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.304. Certification of pension plan financial requirements and minimum municipal obligations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.304. Certification of pension plan financial requirements and minimum municipal obligations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.304. Certification of pension plan financial requirements and minimum municipal obligations (2023)
content:
The chief administrative officer of each pension plan shall submit the financial requirements
   of the pension plan and the minimum obligation of the municipality with respect to
   the pension plan, with appropriate documenting detail, to the governing body of the
   municipality on or before the last business day in September, annually.  The submission shall include a certification by the chief administrative officer
   as to the accuracy of the calculations and their conformance with the applicable provisions
   of this chapter.

content:

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.211. Revised actuarial valuation report (2023)
content:
Upon enactment of legislation which would alter the actuarial valuation of a pension
   plan, a revised actuarial valuation report shall be filed with the commission as the
   commission directs.

Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.208. Modification of actuarial reporting requirement in certain instances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.208. Modification of actuarial reporting requirement in certain instances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.208. Modification of actuarial reporting requirement in certain instances (2023)
content:
Any municipality which complies with the municipal pension plan actuarial reporting
   requirements specified in this chapter shall be deemed to have complied with the act
   of December 6, 1972 (P.L. 1383, No. 293),1entitled “An act requiring municipal pension systems to have an actuarial investigation
   of the fund made by an actuary who shall report his findings to the Department of
   Community Affairs.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.305. Actuarial cost estimate required for benefit plan modification
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.305. Actuarial cost estimate required for benefit plan modification
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.305. Actuarial cost estimate required for benefit plan modification (2023)
content:
(a) Presentation of cost estimate.--Prior to the adoption of any benefit plan modification by the governing body of the
      municipality, the chief administrative officer of each pension plan shall provide
      to the governing body of the municipality a cost estimate of the effect of the proposed
      benefit plan modification.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.301. Municipal pension plan minimum funding standard; application and general provisions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.301. Municipal pension plan minimum funding standard; application and general provisions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.301. Municipal pension plan minimum funding standard; application and general provisions (2023)
content:
(a) Application.--Notwithstanding any provision of law, municipal ordinance, municipal resolution, municipal
      charter, pension plan agreement or pension plan contract to the contrary, the applicable
      provisions of this chapter shall apply to any municipality which has established and
      maintains, directly or indirectly, a pension plan for the benefit of its employees,
      irrespective of the manner in which the pension plan is administered, and to the respective
      pension plan.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.306. Enforcement of funding standard by mandamus action
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.306. Enforcement of funding standard by mandamus action
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.306. Enforcement of funding standard by mandamus action (2023)
content:
(a) Legislative finding and declaration.--The General Assembly finds and declares that any actual or potential failure by a
      municipality to comply with the applicable funding standard established by this act
      threatens serious injury to the affected municipal pension plan, to the entire system
      of public employee pension plans in the Commonwealth and to the Commonwealth itself.  By expressly authorizing the remedy of mandamus in this section, the General Assembly
      intends to assist all persons with a beneficial or special interest in a municipal
      pension plan, in addition to all persons or entities with a special responsibility
      or duty in relation to municipal pension plans, in securing that compliance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.302. Minimum funding standard; defined benefit plans self-insured in whole or in part
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.302. Minimum funding standard; defined benefit plans self-insured in whole or in part
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.302. Minimum funding standard; defined benefit plans self-insured in whole or in part (2023)
content:
(a) Generally.--This section applies to any municipality which has established and maintains a pension
      plan which is a defined benefit plan and which is self-insured in whole or in part.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 4. Revisions Applicable to Municipal Pension Fund Financing›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.401. Revision of financing from local revenue sources
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 4. Revisions Applicable to Municipal Pension Fund Financing › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.401. Revision of financing from local revenue sources
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.401. Revision of financing from local revenue sources (2023)
content:
(a) Evaluation.--Prior to applying for any remedy or combination of remedies pursuant to Chapter 6,1a municipality shall evaluate the current sources of financing for municipal pension
      plans and shall identify any revenue sources from which other personnel costs, including,
      but not limited to, salaries, employer contributions to the Federal old age, survivors,
      disability and health insurance program or premiums for health insurance coverage,
      are payable but from which municipal pension plan costs, including the amortization
      of any unfunded actuarial accrued liability, are not fully allocated.  Upon identifying these omitted or underutilized municipal revenue sources, the municipality
      shall undertake steps to utilize or increase utilization of these revenue sources.  Full utilization of these revenue sources shall occur within one year of identification.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 4. Revisions Applicable to Municipal Pension Fund Financing›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.402. Revision of financing from State revenue sources; General Municipal Pension System State Aid Program
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 4. Revisions Applicable to Municipal Pension Fund Financing › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.402. Revision of financing from State revenue sources; General Municipal Pension System State Aid Program
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.402. Revision of financing from State revenue sources; General Municipal Pension System State Aid Program (2023)
content:
(a) Establishment of program.--There is hereby established a General Municipal Pension System State Aid Program.  Notwithstanding any applicable provision of the act of June 28, 1895 (P.L. 408,
      No. 289),1referred to as the Foreign Fire Insurance Premium Tax Allocation Law, the act of
      May 12, 1943 (P.L. 259, No. 120),2referred to as the Foreign Casualty Insurance Premium Tax Allocation Law, or the
      act of March 4, 1971 (P.L. 6, No. 2),3known as the Tax Reform Code of 1971, to the contrary, the provisions of this section
      and sections 607 and 7064shall govern with respect to the insurance premium taxes on foreign fire insurance
      companies and foreign casualty insurance companies for allocation pursuant to the
      General Municipal Pension System State Aid Program.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.307. Enforcement proceedings by commission
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.307. Enforcement proceedings by commission
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.307. Enforcement proceedings by commission (2023)
content:
(a) Enforcement by commission.--Whenever the commission is of the opinion that any municipality has failed, omitted,
      neglected or refused to perform any duty enjoined upon it pursuant to this act, the
      commission shall have the power and its duty shall be to order compliance by the municipality
      with that duty.  If the municipality fails, omits, neglects or refuses to comply with any lawful
      order of the commission, then the commission may institute legal proceedings for injunction,
      mandamus or other appropriate remedy at law or equity to enforce compliance with,
      or restrain violation of, the order of the commission.

Pension plans for inclusion in determination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.502. Pension plans for inclusion in determination (2023)
content:
The determination provided for in this chapter shall be made for a municipality taking
   into account all pension plans which the municipality has established and maintains,
   except those created after the last biennial actuarial valuation date.  The initial actuarial valuation report for any plan shall not be recognized in the
   determination of a municipality's distress level.  If the municipality filed an actuarial valuation report for any pension plan in
   the prior reporting period, that valuation report shall control the determination
   of distress without regard to the funding status of any newly established plan.  If no other plan was previously maintained by a municipality, the newly established
   plan shall be assigned a distress score of 0.

content:
(a) Disclosure.--A person or an affiliated entity that intends to enter or that enters into a professional
      services contract shall disclose the employment or compensation of a third party intermediary,
      agent or lobbyist to directly or indirectly communicate with a municipal pension system
      official or employee or a municipal official or employee in connection with any transaction
      or investment involving the contractor and the municipal pension system.  The disclosure shall not apply to an officer or employee of the investment firm
      who is acting within the scope of the firm's standard professional duties on behalf
      of the firm, including the actual provision of legal, accounting, engineering, real
      estate or other professional advice, services or assistance pursuant to a professional
      services contract with the municipal pension system.

content:

      shall develop procedures to select the most qualified person to enter into a professional
      services contract.  The procedures shall ensure that the availability of a professional services contract
      is advertised to potential participants in a timely and efficient manner.  Procedures shall include applications and disclosure forms to be used to submit
      a proposal for review and to receive the award of a professional services contract.

      ‘An act to provide revenue by taxation, approved the seventh day of June, one thousand
      eight hundred and seventy-nine,’ approved the first day of June, one thousand eight

Participation in a DROP does not guarantee the DROP participant's employment by the
   local government during the specified period of the DROP.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 9. Modification of Actuarial Funding Standard›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.901. Modification of actuarial funding standard
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 9. Modification of Actuarial Funding Standard › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.901. Modification of actuarial funding standard
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.901. Modification of actuarial funding standard (2023)
content:
(a) Modification of actuarial funding standard.--The actuarial reporting and funding requirements established under Chapters 2, 3 and
      61are modified by this section for a municipality.  The amortization contribution established for each pension fund under this section
      shall be an integral component of the aggregate amortization contribution requirements
      determined under section 302(b)(3).2A municipality determining amortization contributions under this section shall continue
      to determine the total financial requirements of its pension funds under section 302.  If a municipality is delinquent in satisfying the total financial requirements of
      its pension funds, it shall be subject to the penalty and enforcement provisions specified
      in sections 302(e), 306 and 307.3

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 10. Provisions Relating to Cities of the First Class›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1002. Cities of the first class

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1002. Cities of the first class (2023)
content: (a) General rule;  benefit plan study.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 7-A. Standards for Municipal Pension Systems›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.706-A. Duty to act
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 7-A. Standards for Municipal Pension Systems › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.706-A. Duty to act
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.706-A. Duty to act (2023)
content:
If a person that enters into or has applied for, submitted an offer or bid for, responded
   to a request for proposal on or otherwise solicited a contract with a municipal pension
   system or an officer, director or employee of a municipal pension system is aware
   or reasonably should be aware of an apparent, potential or actual conflict of interest,
   the person shall disclose the conflict and promptly eliminate the conflict.

content: (a) Imposition of tax.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1112. Eligibility
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1112. Eligibility
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1112. Eligibility (2023)
content:
An active member of a local government retirement system that has a DROP as a part
   of its defined benefit pension plan who is eligible for a normal retirement benefit
   under the pension plan or will be eligible for a normal retirement benefit under the
   pension plan prior to participation in the DROP and who is not an elected official
   is eligible to participate in the DROP by filing a written application with the retirement
   system at least 30 days before the member's effective date of retirement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 10. Provisions Relating to Cities of the First Class›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1001. Alternative funding mechanism
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 10. Provisions Relating to Cities of the First Class › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1001. Alternative funding mechanism
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1001. Alternative funding mechanism (2023)
content:
(a) Authorization for alternative funding mechanism.--A city of the first class shall be authorized to use an alternative funding mechanism
      for the purpose of reducing or eliminating the unfunded actuarial accrued liability
      of its pension system.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1111. Establishment of DROP
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1111. Establishment of DROP
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1111. Establishment of DROP (2023)
content:
(a) Local governments.--A local government that has established or maintains a defined benefit pension plan
      for a group of its employees which is self-insured in whole or in part under section
      202(b),1except for a local government that has joined the Pennsylvania Municipal Retirement
      System, may establish by ordinance a DROP for those employees as part of the pension
      plan.  The ordinance establishing the DROP shall specify a uniform participation period
      of not more than five years in duration.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1113. Participation in DROP
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1113. Participation in DROP
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1113. Participation in DROP (2023)
content:
(a) Election.--An eligible active member may elect to participate in a DROP for the period specified
      in the ordinance under section 1111(a).1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans›Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1101. Scope of chapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans › Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1101. Scope of chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1101. Scope of chapter (2023)
content:
(a) Applicability.--This chapter shall apply to a local government which does not have a deferred retirement
      option plan on the effective date of this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1116. Subsequent employment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1116. Subsequent employment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1116. Subsequent employment (2023)
content:
After both the termination of a DROP participant's employment as a DROP participant
   by the local government and the expiration of the DROP participation period, a former
   DROP participant shall be subject to such reemployment limitations as other retired
   members and shall be eligible for renewed membership as an active member in the local
   government employees' retirement system.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans›Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1102. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans › Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1102. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1102. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this chapter shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1114. Benefits payable under DROP
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1114. Benefits payable under DROP
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1114. Benefits payable under DROP (2023)
content:
(a) Fixing retirement benefit, retirement date, retirement benefits and DROP dates.--Effective with the date of retirement, which shall be the day before the effective
      date of DROP participation, the member's monthly, normal retirement benefit under
      the pension plan, the member's effective date of retirement and the member's effective
      dates of beginning and terminating employment as a DROP participant shall be fixed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1115. Death benefits under DROP
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1115. Death benefits under DROP
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1115. Death benefits under DROP (2023)
content:
(a) Named beneficiary.--If a DROP participant dies, the DROP participant's named beneficiary shall be entitled
      to apply for and receive the benefits accrued in the DROP participant's subsidiary
      DROP participant account as provided in section 1114(d).1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans›Subchapter C. Administrative Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1122. Audit
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans › Subchapter C. Administrative Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1122. Audit
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1122. Audit (2023)
content:
The DROP established by the Pennsylvania Municipal Retirement Board shall be subject
   to financial and compliance audits conducted by the Auditor General with the initial
   audit conducted within one year of establishment of the DROP.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans›Subchapter D. Designations›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1131. Spouse
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans › Subchapter D. Designations › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1131. Spouse
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1131. Spouse (2023)
content:
(a) Authorization.--Notwithstanding any ordinance or any rule, regulation, procedure or policy of a
      municipal pension system to the contrary, an active member of a municipal pension
      system may designate the member's spouse to be the beneficiary of the member's pension,
      regardless of the date of the marriage.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans›Subchapter C. Administrative Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1124. Noncompliance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans › Subchapter C. Administrative Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1124. Noncompliance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1124. Noncompliance (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If a local government that established a DROP under section 1111(a)1or the Pennsylvania Municipal Retirement Board that established a DROP under section
      1111(c) fails to comply within 90 days with a finding by the Auditor General of noncompliance
      with this chapter or if the finding is appealed within 90 days of conclusion of the
      appeal process, the failure to comply shall be deemed sufficient refusal by the local
      government or the Pennsylvania Municipal Retirement Board to comply with its duty
      antecedent to the commencement of a mandamus action and the Auditor General shall
      refer the finding to the Attorney General.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans›Subchapter C. Administrative Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1121. DROP participant account
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans › Subchapter C. Administrative Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1121. DROP participant account
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1121. DROP participant account (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If a local government creates a DROP, it shall establish a DROP participant account
      as an interest-bearing ledger account in its pension trust fund.  The account balance shall be accounted for separately but need not be physically
      segregated from other pension trust fund assets.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 1. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.103. Methodology
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 1. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.103. Methodology
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.103. Methodology (2023)
content:
Notwithstanding any provisions of the act of August 31, 1971 (P.L. 398, No. 96),1known as the County Pension Law, to the contrary, in performing an actuarial study
   under this act or the act of December 6, 1972 (P.L. 1383, No. 293),2entitled “An act requiring municipal pension systems to have an actuarial investigation
   of the fund made by an actuary who shall report his findings to the Department of
   Community Affairs,” municipalities and counties may utilize any reasonable actuarial
   assumptions or methodologies provided for in this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 1. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.101. Short title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 1. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.101. Short title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.101. Short title (2023)
content:
This act shall be known and may be cited as the Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard
   and Recovery Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act›Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans›Subchapter C. Administrative Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1123. Existing DROPs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8C. Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act › Chapter 11. Deferred Retirement Option Plans › Subchapter C. Administrative Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1123. Existing DROPs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1123. Existing DROPs (2023)
content:
A local government that established a DROP prior to or on the effective date of this
   section that does not conform to the provisions of this chapter relating to elected
   officials shall amend its plan within 180 days of the effective date of this section
   or when the current labor-management contract creating the plan expires, whichever
   is later, to conform with the provisions of this chapter with respect to future DROP
   participants who are elected officials.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.203. Contents of experience investigation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.203. Contents of experience investigation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.203. Contents of experience investigation (2023)
content:
(a) Generally.--The experience investigation shall contain sufficient information to substantiate
      the actuarial assumptions upon which the actuarial exhibits of the most recent actuarial
      report shall be based.  The experience investigation shall be prepared only by an approved actuary.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 1. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.102. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 1. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.102. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.102. Definitions (2023)
content:
Except as provided in Chapter 7,1the following words and phrases when used in this act shall have the meanings given
   to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.201. Requirement to file actuarial valuation report or experience investigation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.201. Requirement to file actuarial valuation report or experience investigation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.201. Requirement to file actuarial valuation report or experience investigation (2023)
content:
(a) Actuarial valuation report required.--Each municipality which has established or maintains a pension plan for its employees,
      including any municipality which participates in the Pennsylvania Municipal Retirement
      System, shall cause to be made actuarial valuation reports.  Actuarial valuation reports shall be made biennially, unless the applicable municipality
      is applying or has previously applied for supplemental State assistance pursuant to
      section 603,1whereupon actuarial valuation reports shall be made annually.  Each municipality which has established or maintains a pension plan for its employees
      and has an active, vested inactive and benefit recipient membership equal to or greater
      than 1,000 shall also cause experience investigations to be made.  Experience investigations shall be made quadrennially.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.204. Delinquent actuarial valuation reports and experience investigations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.204. Delinquent actuarial valuation reports and experience investigations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.204. Delinquent actuarial valuation reports and experience investigations (2023)
content:
If a complete actuarial valuation report or experience investigation is not filed
   in a timely fashion, any and all financing which is provided to the municipality by
   the Commonwealth and is dedicated for pension plan purposes shall be withheld until
   the report or investigation is filed.  If a municipality fails to file an actuarial valuation report or experience investigation,
   the commission shall have the report or investigation prepared and the municipality
   shall reimburse the commission for the actual cost of the preparation of the report
   or investigation.  The commission shall issue rules and regulations specifying the procedures which
   the commission shall follow in obtaining delinquent actuarial valuation reports or
   experience investigations.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.205. Modification of requirements for contents of actuarial valuation reports and experience investigations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.205. Modification of requirements for contents of actuarial valuation reports and experience investigations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.205. Modification of requirements for contents of actuarial valuation reports and experience investigations (2023)
content:
The commission may issue rules and regulations specifying modifications in, additions
   to or elimination of requirements for the contents of actuarial valuation reports
   and experience investigations.  Any rules and regulations shall be issued in accordance with any provision of law
   governing the issuance of rules and regulations by Commonwealth agencies.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.210. Actuarial asset valuation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.210. Actuarial asset valuation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.210. Actuarial asset valuation (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A municipality may value the assets in each of its pension plans to equal the greater
      of:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.207. Actuarial valuation and experience investigation expenses allowable
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.207. Actuarial valuation and experience investigation expenses allowable
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.207. Actuarial valuation and experience investigation expenses allowable (2023)
content:
Notwithstanding any provision of law, municipal ordinance, municipal resolution, municipal
   charter, pension plan agreement or pension plan contract to the contrary, the expenses
   attributable to the preparation of any actuarial valuation report or experience investigation
   required pursuant to this chapter shall be an allowable administrative expense payable
   from the assets of the pension plan.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.206. Requirement for additional information in certain instances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.206. Requirement for additional information in certain instances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.206. Requirement for additional information in certain instances (2023)
content:
The commission may request any additional information, data or calculations in connection
   with any required actuarial valuation report or experience investigation which it
   deems necessary or desirable.  The requested information, data or calculations shall be transmitted to the commission
   as soon as is practicable following receipt of the request.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.302. Minimum funding standard; defined benefit plans self-insured in whole or in part
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.302. Minimum funding standard; defined benefit plans self-insured in whole or in part
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.302. Minimum funding standard; defined benefit plans self-insured in whole or in part (2023)
content:
(a) Generally.--This section applies to any municipality which has established and maintains a pension
      plan which is a defined benefit plan and which is self-insured in whole or in part.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.208. Modification of actuarial reporting requirement in certain instances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.208. Modification of actuarial reporting requirement in certain instances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.208. Modification of actuarial reporting requirement in certain instances (2023)
content:
Any municipality which complies with the municipal pension plan actuarial reporting
   requirements specified in this chapter shall be deemed to have complied with the act
   of December 6, 1972 (P.L. 1383, No. 293),1entitled “An act requiring municipal pension systems to have an actuarial investigation
   of the fund made by an actuary who shall report his findings to the Department of
   Community Affairs.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.209. Authorization for alternate amortization schedules to accommodate extraordinary events
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.209. Authorization for alternate amortization schedules to accommodate extraordinary events
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.209. Authorization for alternate amortization schedules to accommodate extraordinary events (2023)
content:
In the preparation of an actuarial valuation report as of the beginning of the plan
   year occurring in 2005 or thereafter, a municipality may adopt an alternate amortization
   schedule rather than the amortization schedule specified in section 202(b)(4)1for any increment of unfunded actuarial accrued liability that exceeds $9,000,000,
   causes at least a 30% increase in the aggregate actuarial accrued liability of the
   pension plan and is attributable to a single benefit enhancement granted prior to
   January 1, 2004, and being newly recognized in the actuarial valuation report.  The alternate amortization schedule shall be formally adopted by the governing body
   of the municipality and shall provide for an amortization target date that results
   in an amortization period of 30 years, level percentage amortization payments increasing
   by no more than 5% annually if adopted in an actuarial valuation report with a valuation
   date in 2005 and level dollar amortization payments if adopted in an actuarial valuation
   report with a valuation date occurring after December 31, 2005.  The initial and all subsequent actuarial valuation reports filed with the commission
   during the operation of the alternate amortization schedule shall separately disclose
   the initial amount of the increment of unfunded actuarial accrued liability, the date
   that the alternate amortization schedule was established, the amortization target
   date, the original amortization period, the remaining balance of the increment of
   unfunded actuarial accrued liability and the amortization payment for the year following
   the valuation date of the actuarial valuation report.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.202. Contents of actuarial valuation report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.202. Contents of actuarial valuation report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.202. Contents of actuarial valuation report (2023)
content:
(a) Generally.--The actuarial valuation report shall contain actuarial exhibits, financial exhibits
      and demographic exhibits.  The actuarial exhibits shall be prepared and certified by an approved actuary.  The remaining exhibits may be prepared by a qualified person other than an approved
      actuary.  The financial and demographic exhibits shall be prepared as of the end of the prior
      year.  The submission by a municipality of a single report setting forth the various required
      contents items in total for the various pension plans associated with the Pennsylvania
      Municipal Retirement System shall be deemed to be compliance by that municipality
      with the requirements of this chapter only if the report also separately sets forth
      the various required contents items for the municipality.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.211. Revised actuarial valuation report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 2. Municipal Pension Plan Actuarial Reporting › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.211. Revised actuarial valuation report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.211. Revised actuarial valuation report (2023)
content:
Upon enactment of legislation which would alter the actuarial valuation of a pension
   plan, a revised actuarial valuation report shall be filed with the commission as the
   commission directs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.306. Enforcement of funding standard by mandamus action
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.306. Enforcement of funding standard by mandamus action
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.306. Enforcement of funding standard by mandamus action (2023)
content:
(a) Legislative finding and declaration.--The General Assembly finds and declares that any actual or potential failure by a
      municipality to comply with the applicable funding standard established by this act
      threatens serious injury to the affected municipal pension plan, to the entire system
      of public employee pension plans in the Commonwealth and to the Commonwealth itself.  By expressly authorizing the remedy of mandamus in this section, the General Assembly
      intends to assist all persons with a beneficial or special interest in a municipal
      pension plan, in addition to all persons or entities with a special responsibility
      or duty in relation to municipal pension plans, in securing that compliance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.301. Municipal pension plan minimum funding standard; application and general provisions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.301. Municipal pension plan minimum funding standard; application and general provisions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.301. Municipal pension plan minimum funding standard; application and general provisions (2023)
content:
(a) Application.--Notwithstanding any provision of law, municipal ordinance, municipal resolution, municipal
      charter, pension plan agreement or pension plan contract to the contrary, the applicable
      provisions of this chapter shall apply to any municipality which has established and
      maintains, directly or indirectly, a pension plan for the benefit of its employees,
      irrespective of the manner in which the pension plan is administered, and to the respective
      pension plan.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.304. Certification of pension plan financial requirements and minimum municipal obligations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.304. Certification of pension plan financial requirements and minimum municipal obligations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.304. Certification of pension plan financial requirements and minimum municipal obligations (2023)
content:
The chief administrative officer of each pension plan shall submit the financial requirements
   of the pension plan and the minimum obligation of the municipality with respect to
   the pension plan, with appropriate documenting detail, to the governing body of the
   municipality on or before the last business day in September, annually.  The submission shall include a certification by the chief administrative officer
   as to the accuracy of the calculations and their conformance with the applicable provisions
   of this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.307. Enforcement proceedings by commission
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.307. Enforcement proceedings by commission
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.307. Enforcement proceedings by commission (2023)
content:
(a) Enforcement by commission.--Whenever the commission is of the opinion that any municipality has failed, omitted,
      neglected or refused to perform any duty enjoined upon it pursuant to this act, the
      commission shall have the power and its duty shall be to order compliance by the municipality
      with that duty.  If the municipality fails, omits, neglects or refuses to comply with any lawful
      order of the commission, then the commission may institute legal proceedings for injunction,
      mandamus or other appropriate remedy at law or equity to enforce compliance with,
      or restrain violation of, the order of the commission.

content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 4. Revisions Applicable to Municipal Pension Fund Financing›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.401. Revision of financing from local revenue sources
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 4. Revisions Applicable to Municipal Pension Fund Financing › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.401. Revision of financing from local revenue sources
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.401. Revision of financing from local revenue sources (2023)
content:
(a) Evaluation.--Prior to applying for any remedy or combination of remedies pursuant to Chapter 6,1a municipality shall evaluate the current sources of financing for municipal pension
      plans and shall identify any revenue sources from which other personnel costs, including,
      but not limited to, salaries, employer contributions to the Federal old age, survivors,
      disability and health insurance program or premiums for health insurance coverage,
      are payable but from which municipal pension plan costs, including the amortization
      of any unfunded actuarial accrued liability, are not fully allocated.  Upon identifying these omitted or underutilized municipal revenue sources, the municipality
      shall undertake steps to utilize or increase utilization of these revenue sources.  Full utilization of these revenue sources shall occur within one year of identification.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 4. Revisions Applicable to Municipal Pension Fund Financing›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.402. Revision of financing from State revenue sources; General Municipal Pension System State Aid Program
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 4. Revisions Applicable to Municipal Pension Fund Financing › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.402. Revision of financing from State revenue sources; General Municipal Pension System State Aid Program
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.402. Revision of financing from State revenue sources; General Municipal Pension System State Aid Program (2023)
content:
(a) Establishment of program.--There is hereby established a General Municipal Pension System State Aid Program.  Notwithstanding any applicable provision of the act of June 28, 1895 (P.L. 408,
      No. 289),1referred to as the Foreign Fire Insurance Premium Tax Allocation Law, the act of
      May 12, 1943 (P.L. 259, No. 120),2referred to as the Foreign Casualty Insurance Premium Tax Allocation Law, or the
      act of March 4, 1971 (P.L. 6, No. 2),3known as the Tax Reform Code of 1971, to the contrary, the provisions of this section
      and sections 607 and 7064shall govern with respect to the insurance premium taxes on foreign fire insurance
      companies and foreign casualty insurance companies for allocation pursuant to the
      General Municipal Pension System State Aid Program.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 4. Revisions Applicable to Municipal Pension Fund Financing›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.403. General municipal pension system State aid moneys
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 4. Revisions Applicable to Municipal Pension Fund Financing › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.403. General municipal pension system State aid moneys
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.403. General municipal pension system State aid moneys (2023)
content:
(a) Moneys paid.--Any funds paid to a municipality pursuant to the act of May 12, 1943 (P.L. 259, No.
      120),1referred to as the Foreign Casualty Insurance Premium Tax Allocation Law, prior to
      the effective date of this act, and which have been either actually expended or, by
      action of the municipality, are irrevocably committed to be expended only in accordance
      with the Foreign Casualty Insurance Premium Tax Allocation Law, shall not be returned
      for redistribution pursuant to section 1.22of the Foreign Casualty Insurance Premium Tax Allocation Law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 3. Minimum Funding Standard for Municipal Pension Plans›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.305. Actuarial cost estimate required for benefit plan modification

      benefit plan modification.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 5. Financially Distressed Municipal Pension Plan Determination Procedure›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.502. Pension plans for inclusion in determination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 5. Financially Distressed Municipal Pension Plan Determination Procedure › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.502. Pension plans for inclusion in determination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.502. Pension plans for inclusion in determination (2023)
content:
The determination provided for in this chapter shall be made for a municipality taking
   into account all pension plans which the municipality has established and maintains,
   except those created after the last biennial actuarial valuation date.  The initial actuarial valuation report for any plan shall not be recognized in the
   determination of a municipality's distress level.  If the municipality filed an actuarial valuation report for any pension plan in
   the prior reporting period, that valuation report shall control the determination
   of distress without regard to the funding status of any newly established plan.  If no other plan was previously maintained by a municipality, the newly established
   plan shall be assigned a distress score of 0.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 7-A. Standards for Municipal Pension Systems›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.702-A. Procurement for professional services contracts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 7-A. Standards for Municipal Pension Systems › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.702-A. Procurement for professional services contracts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.702-A. Procurement for professional services contracts (2023)
content:
(a) Procedures.--Each municipal pension system, including the Pennsylvania Municipal Retirement System,
      shall develop procedures to select the most qualified person to enter into a professional
      services contract.  The procedures shall ensure that the availability of a professional services contract
      is advertised to potential participants in a timely and efficient manner.  Procedures shall include applications and disclosure forms to be used to submit
      a proposal for review and to receive the award of a professional services contract.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 7-A. Standards for Municipal Pension Systems›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.703-A. Agents; solicitation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 7-A. Standards for Municipal Pension Systems › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.703-A. Agents; solicitation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.703-A. Agents; solicitation (2023)
content:
(a) Disclosure.--A person or an affiliated entity that intends to enter or that enters into a professional
      services contract shall disclose the employment or compensation of a third party intermediary,
      agent or lobbyist to directly or indirectly communicate with a municipal pension system
      official or employee or a municipal official or employee in connection with any transaction
      or investment involving the contractor and the municipal pension system.  The disclosure shall not apply to an officer or employee of the investment firm
      who is acting within the scope of the firm's standard professional duties on behalf
      of the firm, including the actual provision of legal, accounting, engineering, real
      estate or other professional advice, services or assistance pursuant to a professional
      services contract with the municipal pension system.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 9. Modification of Actuarial Funding Standard › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.901. Modification of actuarial funding standard
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.901. Modification of actuarial funding standard (2023)
content:
(a) Modification of actuarial funding standard.--The actuarial reporting and funding requirements established under Chapters 2, 3 and
      61are modified by this section for a municipality.  The amortization contribution established for each pension fund under this section
      shall be an integral component of the aggregate amortization contribution requirements
      determined under section 302(b)(3).2A municipality determining amortization contributions under this section shall continue
      to determine the total financial requirements of its pension funds under section 302.  If a municipality is delinquent in satisfying the total financial requirements of
      its pension funds, it shall be subject to the penalty and enforcement provisions specified
      in sections 302(e), 306 and 307.3

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 8. Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.801. Repeals

content:

      eight hundred and seventy-nine,’ approved the first day of June, one thousand eight
      hundred and eighty-nine, amending the twenty-fourth section, by providing for the
      payment by the State Treasurer of the two per centum tax on premiums paid by foreign
      fire insurance companies to the treasurers of the several cities, towns, townships
      and boroughs, within this Commonwealth,” is repealed.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 7-A. Standards for Municipal Pension Systems › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.704-A. Disqualification
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.704-A. Disqualification (2023)
content:
(a) Contributors.--A person or an affiliated entity that, within the past two years, has made a contribution
      to a municipal official or candidate for municipal office in the municipality which
      controls the municipal pension system may not enter into a professional services contract
      with the municipal pension system, except that the two-year restriction shall not
      apply to any contribution made prior to the effective date of this subsection.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 7-A. Standards for Municipal Pension Systems›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.706-A. Duty to act
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part I. General Municipal Law › Chapter 7-A. Standards for Municipal Pension Systems › PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.706-A. Duty to act
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.706-A. Duty to act (2023)
content:
If a person that enters into or has applied for, submitted an offer or bid for, responded
   to a request for proposal on or otherwise solicited a contract with a municipal pension
   system or an officer, director or employee of a municipal pension system is aware
   or reasonably should be aware of an apparent, potential or actual conflict of interest,
   the person shall disclose the conflict and promptly eliminate the conflict.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article I. Executive Power›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12101. Power vested in mayor and departments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article I. Executive Power › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12101. Power vested in mayor and departments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12101. Power vested in mayor and departments (2023)
content:
In each city of the first class of this Commonwealth, the executive power shall be
   vested in the mayor and in the departments authorized by this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article II. The Mayor›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12123. Oath
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article II. The Mayor › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12123. Oath
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12123. Oath (2023)
content:
The mayor shall take the usual oath of office in the presence of the council, to be
   administered by one of the judges of the courts in said city at twelve o'clock noon
   on the first day of the term for which he shall have been elected.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article II. The Mayor›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12121. Chief executive officer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article II. The Mayor › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12121. Chief executive officer
