The Mayor›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12125. Acting mayor pending election or during disability; resignation or inability of mayor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article II. The Mayor › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12125. Acting mayor pending election or during disability; resignation or inability of mayor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12125. Acting mayor pending election or during disability; resignation or inability of mayor (2023)
content:
Until the vacancy is filled, or in case of the mayor's temporary disability, the president
   of the council shall act as mayor;  or if he should resign or be unable to act, then
   the chairman of the finance committee of the council shall act as mayor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part I. General Municipal Law›Chapter 10. Provisions Relating to Cities of the First Class›PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1001. Alternative funding mechanism

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 895.1001. Alternative funding mechanism (2023)
content:
(a) Authorization for alternative funding mechanism.--A city of the first class shall be authorized to use an alternative funding mechanism
      for the purpose of reducing or eliminating the unfunded actuarial accrued liability
      of its pension system.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article II. The Mayor›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12122. Election; term; election by council in case of tie
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article II. The Mayor › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12122. Election; term; election by council in case of tie
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12122. Election; term; election by council in case of tie (2023)
content:
(a) The mayor shall be chosen at the municipal election, and shall hold office for
      the term of four years and until his successor is elected and qualified.  He shall be eligible to the office for one successive term and shall not thereafter
      be eligible for a successive term.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article II. The Mayor›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12126. Salary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article II. The Mayor › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12126. Salary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12126. Salary (2023)
content:
The mayor shall receive a salary to be fixed, from time to time, by ordinance, and
   to be paid out of the city treasury, which salary shall not be increased or diminished
   during the term for which he shall have been elected.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article II. The Mayor›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12128. Power of city to make building district regulations; appointment of zoning commission; powers of zoning or park commission
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article II. The Mayor › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12128. Power of city to make building district regulations; appointment of zoning commission; powers of zoning or park commission
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12128. Power of city to make building district regulations; appointment of zoning commission; powers of zoning or park commission (2023)
content:
For the purpose of promoting the public health, safety, order, and general welfare,
   any such city may regulate the location, size, and use of buildings therein, and may
   make different regulations for different districts thereof.  For the purpose of carrying out the foregoing authority, the mayor may appoint a
   zoning commission.  Any park commission having control over any public park within any such city may
   make such regulations as to the location, size, and use of buildings any portion of
   which shall come within two hundred feet of any park, parkway, playground, or other
   public place under its care or management.  Upon the approval by the council of such city, said regulations made by such zoning
   commission or park commission shall have the same effect as if originally made by
   the council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article II. The Mayor›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12129. Commission on city planning; appointment; powers and duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article II. The Mayor › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12129. Commission on city planning; appointment; powers and duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12129. Commission on city planning; appointment; powers and duties (2023)
content:
Any such city may create by ordinance a commission on city planning, the members of
   which shall be appointed by the mayor.  The commission may employ such engineers and other persons as may be provided for
   by ordinance of council.  The city planning commission may make or cause to be made, and lay before the council,
   and, in its discretion, cause to be published, a map or maps of the city, or any portions
   thereof, and adjacent territory beyond the city limits, showing the streets and highways
   and other natural or artificial features, and also locations proposed by it for any
   new public building, civic center, street, parkway, boulevard, park, playground, or
   any other public ground or public improvement, or any widening, extension, or relocation
   of the same, or any change in the city plan by it deemed advisable.  And it may make recommendations to the council concerning any such matters or things
   aforesaid for action by the council thereon, and in so doing have regard for the present
   conditions and future needs and growth of the city, and the distribution and relative
   location of all the principal and other streets, and railways, waterways, and all
   other means of public travel and business communications, as well as the distribution
   and relative location of all public buildings, public grounds, and open spaces devoted
   to public use, and the planning and laying out for urban uses of private grounds brought
   into the market from time to time.  The city planning commission may make recommendations to any public authorities
   or any corporation or individuals in said cities with reference to the location of
   any buildings, structure, or works to be erected or constructed by them.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12122. Election; term; election by council in case of tie

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12122. Election; term; election by council in case of tie (2023)
content:
(a) The mayor shall be chosen at the municipal election, and shall hold office for
      the term of four years and until his successor is elected and qualified.  He shall be eligible to the office for one successive term and shall not thereafter
      be eligible for a successive term.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article II. The Mayor›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12127. Duties and powers

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12127. Duties and powers (2023)
content: (a) It shall be the duty of the mayor:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12123. Oath
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12123. Oath
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12123. Oath (2023)
content:
The mayor shall take the usual oath of office in the presence of the council, to be
   administered by one of the judges of the courts in said city at twelve o'clock noon
   on the first day of the term for which he shall have been elected.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article II. The Mayor›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12124. Filling of vacancy; election
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article II. The Mayor › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12124. Filling of vacancy; election
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12124. Filling of vacancy; election (2023)
content:
When a vacancy shall take place in the office of mayor, a successor shall be elected
   for the unexpired term at the next election occurring more than thirty days after
   the commencement of such vacancy, unless such election should occur in the last year
   of said term, in which case a mayor shall be chosen by the council by a majority vote
   of all the members elected thereto.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article II. The Mayor›Art Jury›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12130. Appointment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article II. The Mayor › Art Jury › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12130. Appointment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12130. Appointment (2023)
content:
There shall be an art jury, composed of the mayor of the city ex officio and eight
   other members to be appointed by him as now provided by law.  In all matters within the jurisdiction of the jury pertaining to work under the
   special charge of a bureau in any department of the city, the head of such bureau
   shall also for the time being act as a member of the jury ex officio.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article II. The Mayor›Art Jury›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12135. Powers of commissions to execute trust not affected
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article II. The Mayor › Art Jury › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12135. Powers of commissions to execute trust not affected
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12135. Powers of commissions to execute trust not affected (2023)
content:
This article1shall not limit or affect in any way the authority conferred by law upon any commission
   to lay out, improve, or maintain any public park in any such city now under the control
   of such commission, nor shall it restrict in any way the exercise of full discretion
   by such commission in the execution of any trust created by deed or will.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12121. Chief executive officer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12121. Chief executive officer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12121. Chief executive officer (2023)
content: The mayor shall be the chief executive officer of the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article II. The Mayor›Art Jury›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12131. Qualifications of members
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article II. The Mayor › Art Jury › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12131. Qualifications of members
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12131. Qualifications of members (2023)
content:
The members of the jury, other than the mayor, shall consist of a painter, a sculptor,
   an architect, a member of a commission having control of a public park in said city
   not holding any other office under the city government, and four other persons not
   engaged in the practice of the professions of painting, sculpture, or architecture,
   but at least three of whom, at the date of their appointment, shall be members of
   the governing body or teaching force of a corporation or corporations organized under
   the laws of this Commonwealth and conducting a school of art or architecture in said
   city.  One of such members shall be an experienced business executive.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article II. The Mayor›Art Jury›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12132. Organization of jury; employes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article II. The Mayor › Art Jury › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12132. Organization of jury; employes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12132. Organization of jury; employes (2023)
content:
The members of the jury shall elect from their own number a president and a vice-president
   to serve for one year and until their successors are elected.  The jury shall have power to adopt its own rules of procedure, and to prescribe
   regulations for the submission to it of all matters within its jurisdiction.  Five members shall constitute a quorum.  The jury shall have power to employ a secretary and such clerks, stenographers,
   and other assistants, as may be provided for by ordinance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article II. The Mayor›Art Jury›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12133. Approval of works of art purchased by or donated to city; “work of art” defined
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article II. The Mayor › Art Jury › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12133. Approval of works of art purchased by or donated to city; “work of art” defined
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12133. Approval of works of art purchased by or donated to city; “work of art” defined (2023)
content:
Hereafter no work of art shall become the property of any such city, by purchase,
   gift, or otherwise, unless such work of art of1design for the same, and the proposed location of such work of art, shall first have
   been submitted to, and approved by, the art jury of said city;  nor shall any work
   of art, until so approved, be erected or placed in or upon, or allowed to extend over,
   any building, highway, stream, lake, square, park, or other public place belonging
   to, or under the control of, said city.  The jury may, when it deems proper, also require a complete model of the proposed
   work of art to be submitted to it before taking final action thereon.  The term “work of art,” as used in this act, shall include all paintings, mural
   decorations, inscriptions, stained glass, statues, reliefs, or other sculptures, monuments,
   fountains, arches, or other structures, intended for ornament or commemoration.  No existing work of art in the possession of the city shall be removed, relocated,
   or altered in any way, without the approval of the jury.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article II. The Mayor›Art Jury›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12134. Approval of buildings, bridges and other structures
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article II. The Mayor › Art Jury › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12134. Approval of buildings, bridges and other structures
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12134. Approval of buildings, bridges and other structures (2023)
content:
No construction or erection in any such city of any building, bridge, or its approaches,
   arch, gate, fence, or other structure or fixture, which is to be paid for, either
   wholly or in part, from the city treasury, or for which the city or any other public
   authority is to furnish a site, shall be begun unless the design and proposed location
   thereof shall have been submitted to the jury and approved by it, except as herein
   provided, before the final approval thereof by the officer or other person having
   authority to contract therefor.  The approval of the jury shall also be required in respect to all structures or
   fixtures belonging to any person or corporation which shall be erected upon, or extend
   over, any highway, stream, lake, square, park, or other public place within the city,
   except as provided in this act.  In deeds for land made by any such city, restrictions may be imposed, requiring
   that the design and location of structures to be altered or erected thereon shall
   be first approved by the art jury.  Nothing requiring the approval of the jury shall be erected or changed in design
   or location without its approval.  If the jury fails to act upon any matter submitted to it within sixty days after
   such submission, its approval of the matter submitted shall be presumed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12126. Salary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12126. Salary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12126. Salary (2023)
content:
The mayor shall receive a salary to be fixed, from time to time, by ordinance, and
   to be paid out of the city treasury, which salary shall not be increased or diminished
   during the term for which he shall have been elected.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12127. Duties and powers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12127. Duties and powers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12127. Duties and powers (2023)
content: (a) It shall be the duty of the mayor:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12128. Power of city to make building district regulations; appointment of zoning commission; powers of zoning or park commission
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12128. Power of city to make building district regulations; appointment of zoning commission; powers of zoning or park commission
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12128. Power of city to make building district regulations; appointment of zoning commission; powers of zoning or park commission (2023)
content:
For the purpose of promoting the public health, safety, order, and general welfare,
   any such city may regulate the location, size, and use of buildings therein, and may
   make different regulations for different districts thereof.  For the purpose of carrying out the foregoing authority, the mayor may appoint a
   zoning commission.  Any park commission having control over any public park within any such city may
   make such regulations as to the location, size, and use of buildings any portion of
   which shall come within two hundred feet of any park, parkway, playground, or other
   public place under its care or management.  Upon the approval by the council of such city, said regulations made by such zoning
   commission or park commission shall have the same effect as if originally made by
   the council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12125. Acting mayor pending election or during disability; resignation or inability of mayor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12125. Acting mayor pending election or during disability; resignation or inability of mayor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12125. Acting mayor pending election or during disability; resignation or inability of mayor (2023)
content:
Until the vacancy is filled, or in case of the mayor's temporary disability, the president
   of the council shall act as mayor;  or if he should resign or be unable to act, then
   the chairman of the finance committee of the council shall act as mayor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12124. Filling of vacancy; election
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12124. Filling of vacancy; election
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12124. Filling of vacancy; election (2023)
content:
When a vacancy shall take place in the office of mayor, a successor shall be elected
   for the unexpired term at the next election occurring more than thirty days after
   the commencement of such vacancy, unless such election should occur in the last year
   of said term, in which case a mayor shall be chosen by the council by a majority vote
   of all the members elected thereto.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Art Jury›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12130. Appointment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Art Jury › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12130. Appointment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12130. Appointment (2023)
content:
There shall be an art jury, composed of the mayor of the city ex officio and eight
   other members to be appointed by him as now provided by law.  In all matters within the jurisdiction of the jury pertaining to work under the
   special charge of a bureau in any department of the city, the head of such bureau
   shall also for the time being act as a member of the jury ex officio.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Art Jury›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12132. Organization of jury; employes

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12132. Organization of jury; employes (2023)
content:
The members of the jury shall elect from their own number a president and a vice-president
   to serve for one year and until their successors are elected.  The jury shall have power to adopt its own rules of procedure, and to prescribe
   regulations for the submission to it of all matters within its jurisdiction.  Five members shall constitute a quorum.  The jury shall have power to employ a secretary and such clerks, stenographers,
   and other assistants, as may be provided for by ordinance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Art Jury›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12131. Qualifications of members
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Art Jury › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12131. Qualifications of members
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12131. Qualifications of members (2023)
content:
The members of the jury, other than the mayor, shall consist of a painter, a sculptor,
   an architect, a member of a commission having control of a public park in said city
   not holding any other office under the city government, and four other persons not
   engaged in the practice of the professions of painting, sculpture, or architecture,
   but at least three of whom, at the date of their appointment, shall be members of
   the governing body or teaching force of a corporation or corporations organized under
   the laws of this Commonwealth and conducting a school of art or architecture in said
   city.  One of such members shall be an experienced business executive.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12129. Commission on city planning; appointment; powers and duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12129. Commission on city planning; appointment; powers and duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12129. Commission on city planning; appointment; powers and duties (2023)
content:
Any such city may create by ordinance a commission on city planning, the members of
   which shall be appointed by the mayor.  The commission may employ such engineers and other persons as may be provided for
   by ordinance of council.  The city planning commission may make or cause to be made, and lay before the council,
   and, in its discretion, cause to be published, a map or maps of the city, or any portions
   thereof, and adjacent territory beyond the city limits, showing the streets and highways
   and other natural or artificial features, and also locations proposed by it for any
   new public building, civic center, street, parkway, boulevard, park, playground, or
   any other public ground or public improvement, or any widening, extension, or relocation
   of the same, or any change in the city plan by it deemed advisable.  And it may make recommendations to the council concerning any such matters or things
   aforesaid for action by the council thereon, and in so doing have regard for the present
   conditions and future needs and growth of the city, and the distribution and relative
   location of all the principal and other streets, and railways, waterways, and all
   other means of public travel and business communications, as well as the distribution
   and relative location of all public buildings, public grounds, and open spaces devoted
   to public use, and the planning and laying out for urban uses of private grounds brought
   into the market from time to time.  The city planning commission may make recommendations to any public authorities
   or any corporation or individuals in said cities with reference to the location of
   any buildings, structure, or works to be erected or constructed by them.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article III. Executive Departments›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12163. Rules and regulations of departments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article III. Executive Departments › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12163. Rules and regulations of departments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12163. Rules and regulations of departments (2023)
content:
Each department shall have power to prescribe rules and regulations, not inconsistent
   with any law or ordinance or with the provisions of this act, for its own government,
   regulating the conduct of its officers and employes, the distribution and performance
   of its business, and the custody, use, and preservation of the books, records, papers,
   and property under its control.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article III. Executive Departments›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12165. Bonds of heads of departments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article III. Executive Departments › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12165. Bonds of heads of departments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12165. Bonds of heads of departments (2023)
content:
The directors of public safety, public works, public health, public welfare, wharves,
   docks, and ferries, and city transit, and the city solicitor shall each give bond,
   in the usual form, in the sum of twenty-five thousand dollars, to be approved as now
   provided by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Art Jury›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12135. Powers of commissions to execute trust not affected
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Art Jury › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12135. Powers of commissions to execute trust not affected
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12135. Powers of commissions to execute trust not affected (2023)
content:
This article1shall not limit or affect in any way the authority conferred by law upon any commission
   to lay out, improve, or maintain any public park in any such city now under the control
   of such commission, nor shall it restrict in any way the exercise of full discretion
   by such commission in the execution of any trust created by deed or will.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12161. Departments enumerated (2023)
content: There shall be the following executive departments:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article III. Executive Departments›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12164. Information and reports to be furnished
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article III. Executive Departments › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12164. Information and reports to be furnished
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12164. Information and reports to be furnished (2023)
content:
(a) Each department shall furnish to the mayor or council such information as he or
      it may at any time demand in relation to the affairs of such department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article IV. Officers and Employes in General›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12195. Qualifications of officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article IV. Officers and Employes in General › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12195. Qualifications of officers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12195. Qualifications of officers (2023)
content:
All officers elected by the qualified voters of any such city shall be residents thereof
   at the time of their nomination and election, and shall reside therein during their
   term of service.  The mayor and city treasurer shall have been citizens and inhabitants of the State
   for five years, and residents of the city three years, next before their election.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article IV. Officers and Employes in General›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12191. Powers and duties, except as modified, to continue
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article IV. Officers and Employes in General › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12191. Powers and duties, except as modified, to continue
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12191. Powers and duties, except as modified, to continue (2023)
content:
Except as herein otherwise provided, the powers, functions, and duties of all executive
   departments, bureaus, boards, divisions, officers, and employes of such cities shall
   continue as now provided by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article IV. Officers and Employes in General›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12192. Filling of vacancies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article IV. Officers and Employes in General › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12192. Filling of vacancies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12192. Filling of vacancies (2023)
content:
(a) During the recess of the council, the mayor shall have power to fill all vacancies
      that may happen in offices to which he may appoint by and with the advice and consent
      of the council, and any such appointment shall be submitted to the council at its
      next meeting, and, if not rejected within thirty days thereafter, the same shall be
      considered confirmed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article IV. Officers and Employes in General›Impeachment, Suspension and Removal›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12200. Complaint to court by electors; rule
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article IV. Officers and Employes in General › Impeachment, Suspension and Removal › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12200. Complaint to court by electors; rule
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12200. Complaint to court by electors; rule (2023)
content:
Complaint in writing may be made to a court of common pleas of the proper county by
   not less than twenty qualified electors of the city, each of whom shall write his
   occupation and residence opposite his signature, charging any municipal officer with
   any offense, setting forth the facts on which the said charge is founded, supported
   by the oaths or affirmations of at least five of the complainants according to the
   best of their knowledge, information, and belief.  If in the judgment of the court there appears to be reasonable ground for such proceeding,
   the court shall direct the complaint to be filed of record, and grant a rule upon
   the accused, returnable on a day certain, to appear and answer the same.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article IV. Officers and Employes in General›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12193. Person can hold only one office; exceptions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article IV. Officers and Employes in General › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12193. Person can hold only one office; exceptions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12193. Person can hold only one office; exceptions (2023)
content:
No person shall hold more than one office or position of profit under the city government,
   and no person shall hold any office or position of profit under the city, or any department
   thereof, while holding any other office or position of profit in or under the Government
   of the United States, of this Commonwealth, or any county, city, or other political
   subdivision thereof:  Provided, That nothing in this act contained shall apply to
   the office of notary public, commissioner of deeds, or any office in the military
   or naval service of the United States or of this Commonwealth, and that nothing in
   this act shall prevent persons holding office ex officio by virtue of occupying another
   office or position.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article IV. Officers and Employes in General›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12197. Fees to belong to city; salaries
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article IV. Officers and Employes in General › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12197. Fees to belong to city; salaries
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12197. Fees to belong to city; salaries (2023)
content:
No officer or employe of such city shall collect any fees or perquisites for his own
   use, but all such fees or perquisites, collectible under the law, shall be paid into
   the city treasury;  and the council shall provide by ordinance for the payment of
   proper salaries or other compensation, to be fixed by council, to all officers and
   employes of the city, except for such of them whose salaries are fixed by law or who
   it is provided by law shall serve without compensation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article IV. Officers and Employes in General›Impeachment, Suspension and Removal›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12201. Committee of investigation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article IV. Officers and Employes in General › Impeachment, Suspension and Removal › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12201. Committee of investigation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12201. Committee of investigation (2023)
content:
If on the return-day of the rule the court shall find sufficient cause for further
   proceedings, it shall appoint a committee of five competent and reputable citizens
   to investigate the charges contained in said complaint, who, having been first severally
   sworn or affirmed to perform the duties of their appointment with fidelity, shall
   have full authority, for that purpose, to examine the books of the office held by
   the accused and any papers, contracts, letters, or documents filed therein, and examine
   witnesses under oath or affirmation, whose attendance the court shall enforce, if
   necessary, by subpoena and attachment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article III. Executive Departments›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12162. Powers of council with reference to departments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article III. Executive Departments › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12162. Powers of council with reference to departments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12162. Powers of council with reference to departments (2023)
content:
(a) The council shall have power to organize and, from time to time, reorganize any
      department of the city government.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article IV. Officers and Employes in General›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12194. Commencement of terms of office
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article IV. Officers and Employes in General › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12194. Commencement of terms of office
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12194. Commencement of terms of office (2023)
content:
The terms of officers elected by the qualified voters of such cities shall commence
   on the first Monday of January next succeeding their election, except in the case
   of elections to fill vacancies.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article IV. Officers and Employes in General›Impeachment, Suspension and Removal›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12204. Trial
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article IV. Officers and Employes in General › Impeachment, Suspension and Removal › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12204. Trial
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12204. Trial (2023)
content:
The president judge of the said court of common pleas or, in his absence, and1associate judge thereof, shall preside during the trial, and decide finally all questions
   of law and evidence that may arise in the case.  He shall have the power to issue subpoenas for witnesses, and compel their attendance
   by attachment and the production of books, papers, and documentary evidence required
   or called for by the said court of impeachment, and to punish witnesses and others
   for contempt, as fully as any court of this Commonwealth may lawfully do in any case.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article IV. Officers and Employes in General›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12198. Pension funds continued
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article IV. Officers and Employes in General › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12198. Pension funds continued
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12198. Pension funds continued (2023)
content:
There shall continue to be pension funds for the employes of such city as now provided
   by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article IV. Officers and Employes in General›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12196. Bonds; itemized return of receipts; oath
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article IV. Officers and Employes in General › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12196. Bonds; itemized return of receipts; oath
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12196. Bonds; itemized return of receipts; oath (2023)
content:
Every officer or agent receiving moneys for the city and payable to the city treasurer
   shall give a bond for the faithful performance of his duty, and shall be required
   to make return to the city controller once in every week, or oftener if the council
   shall direct, under oath or affirmation, of each item of the moneys received by him,
   and to pay the amount in his hands to the city treasurer.  The said city controller is hereby authorized to administer such oath or affirmation,
   and any person falsely making such oath of1affirmation or guilty of falsehood in any other oath or affirmation required by the
   provisions of this act or by any ordinance of council made in pursuance thereof shall
   be guilty of perjury.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article IV. Officers and Employes in General›Impeachment, Suspension and Removal›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12202. Report of committee; suspension of accused
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article IV. Officers and Employes in General › Impeachment, Suspension and Removal › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12202. Report of committee; suspension of accused
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12202. Report of committee; suspension of accused (2023)
content:
It shall be the duty of the committee to make a written report to the court of the
   facts found by it, which shall be filed of record, accompanied by the testimony taken,
   within three weeks next after its appointment, unless the time shall be extended by
   the court upon its application.  In any stage of the proceedings, if the public interest so require, the court may,
   by an order to be filed of record in the case, suspend the accused from office until
   he shall be tried and acquitted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article IV. Officers and Employes in General›Impeachment, Suspension and Removal›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12199. Grounds for impeachment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article IV. Officers and Employes in General › Impeachment, Suspension and Removal › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12199. Grounds for impeachment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12199. Grounds for impeachment (2023)
content:
Municipal officers shall be liable to impeachment, suspension, and removal from office,
   for any corrupt act or practice, malfeasance, mismanagement, mental incapacity, or
   incompetency for the proper performance of official duties, extortion, receiving any
   gift or present from any contractor or from any person seeking or engaged in any work
   for, or furnishing material to, the city, or from any incumbent or occupant of, or
   candidate or applicant for, any municipal office, and for wilfully concealing any
   fraud committed against the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12191. Powers and duties, except as modified, to continue
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12191. Powers and duties, except as modified, to continue
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12191. Powers and duties, except as modified, to continue (2023)
content:
Except as herein otherwise provided, the powers, functions, and duties of all executive
   departments, bureaus, boards, divisions, officers, and employes of such cities shall
   continue as now provided by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12194. Commencement of terms of office
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12194. Commencement of terms of office
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12194. Commencement of terms of office (2023)

The terms of officers elected by the qualified voters of such cities shall commence

   of elections to fill vacancies.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12195. Qualifications of officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12195. Qualifications of officers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12195. Qualifications of officers (2023)
content:
All officers elected by the qualified voters of any such city shall be residents thereof
   at the time of their nomination and election, and shall reside therein during their
   term of service.  The mayor and city treasurer shall have been citizens and inhabitants of the State
   for five years, and residents of the city three years, next before their election.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12192. Filling of vacancies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12192. Filling of vacancies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12192. Filling of vacancies (2023)
content:
(a) During the recess of the council, the mayor shall have power to fill all vacancies
      that may happen in offices to which he may appoint by and with the advice and consent
      of the council, and any such appointment shall be submitted to the council at its
      next meeting, and, if not rejected within thirty days thereafter, the same shall be
      considered confirmed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12193. Person can hold only one office; exceptions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12193. Person can hold only one office; exceptions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12193. Person can hold only one office; exceptions (2023)
content:
No person shall hold more than one office or position of profit under the city government,
   and no person shall hold any office or position of profit under the city, or any department
   thereof, while holding any other office or position of profit in or under the Government
   of the United States, of this Commonwealth, or any county, city, or other political
   subdivision thereof:  Provided, That nothing in this act contained shall apply to
   the office of notary public, commissioner of deeds, or any office in the military
   or naval service of the United States or of this Commonwealth, and that nothing in
   this act shall prevent persons holding office ex officio by virtue of occupying another
   office or position.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article IV. Officers and Employes in General›Impeachment, Suspension and Removal›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12203. Report sustaining charges to be submitted to council; copy served on accused
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article IV. Officers and Employes in General › Impeachment, Suspension and Removal › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12203. Report sustaining charges to be submitted to council; copy served on accused
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12203. Report sustaining charges to be submitted to council; copy served on accused (2023)
content:
If the committee, or any three members thereof, shall find that any charge made as
   aforesaid is well founded, it shall in its report so state in specific form, and,
   in such case, the court shall cause a certified copy of the whole record, with the
   specifications of the charges against the accused, to be transmitted to the council,
   which shall be assembled within ten days thereafter, in special and open session,
   as a court of impeachment, and the members shall be severally sworn to try and decide
   the same according to the evidence.  A copy of the specifications shall be served on the accused, or left at his last
   place of residence, at least five days before the commencement of the trial, and he
   shall be entitled to be heard thereon in person or by counsel and to produce evidence
   in his defense, and the prosecution before the council shall be conducted by the committee
   or by counsel appointed by it.  The compensation of counsel and the cost of investigation and prosecution by the
   committee shall be provided for by ordinance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article IV. Officers and Employes in General›Impeachment, Suspension and Removal›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12205. Decision of court of impeachment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article IV. Officers and Employes in General › Impeachment, Suspension and Removal › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12205. Decision of court of impeachment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12205. Decision of court of impeachment (2023)
content:
The decision of the court of impeachment shall be entered upon the record of its proceedings,
   and certified by the clerk to the court in which the complaint was filed.  If the accused shall be found guilty on any of the specifications, the said court
   of common pleas shall enter judgment accordingly, and declare the said office vacant.

   incompetency for the proper performance of official duties, extortion, receiving any
   gift or present from any contractor or from any person seeking or engaged in any work

   candidate or applicant for, any municipal office, and for wilfully concealing any

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12197. Fees to belong to city; salaries
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12197. Fees to belong to city; salaries
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12197. Fees to belong to city; salaries (2023)
content:
No officer or employe of such city shall collect any fees or perquisites for his own
   use, but all such fees or perquisites, collectible under the law, shall be paid into
   the city treasury;  and the council shall provide by ordinance for the payment of
   proper salaries or other compensation, to be fixed by council, to all officers and
   employes of the city, except for such of them whose salaries are fixed by law or who
   it is provided by law shall serve without compensation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Impeachment, Suspension and Removal›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12200. Complaint to court by electors; rule
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Impeachment, Suspension and Removal › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12200. Complaint to court by electors; rule
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12200. Complaint to court by electors; rule (2023)
content:
Complaint in writing may be made to a court of common pleas of the proper county by
   not less than twenty qualified electors of the city, each of whom shall write his
   occupation and residence opposite his signature, charging any municipal officer with
   any offense, setting forth the facts on which the said charge is founded, supported
   by the oaths or affirmations of at least five of the complainants according to the
   best of their knowledge, information, and belief.  If in the judgment of the court there appears to be reasonable ground for such proceeding,
   the court shall direct the complaint to be filed of record, and grant a rule upon
   the accused, returnable on a day certain, to appear and answer the same.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Impeachment, Suspension and Removal›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12201. Committee of investigation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Impeachment, Suspension and Removal › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12201. Committee of investigation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12201. Committee of investigation (2023)
content:
If on the return-day of the rule the court shall find sufficient cause for further
   proceedings, it shall appoint a committee of five competent and reputable citizens
   to investigate the charges contained in said complaint, who, having been first severally
   sworn or affirmed to perform the duties of their appointment with fidelity, shall
   have full authority, for that purpose, to examine the books of the office held by
   the accused and any papers, contracts, letters, or documents filed therein, and examine
   witnesses under oath or affirmation, whose attendance the court shall enforce, if
   necessary, by subpoena and attachment.

   by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article V. Department of Public Safety›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12232. Assistant director; other officers and employes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article V. Department of Public Safety › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12232. Assistant director; other officers and employes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12232. Assistant director; other officers and employes (2023)
content:
The director of public safety shall have the power to appoint an assistant director,
   who, in the absence or incapacity of the director to act, shall possess all the powers
   and perform all the duties of the director until the incapacity or inability of the
   director is removed or until a new director is appointed and qualified as hereinbefore
   provided.  The director shall also appoint such other officers and employes as may be provided
   for by ordinance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article V. Department of Public Safety›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12235. Uniforms of policemen and firemen
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article V. Department of Public Safety › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12235. Uniforms of policemen and firemen
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12235. Uniforms of policemen and firemen (2023)
content:
The department shall make suitable regulations under which the officers and members
   of the fire and police forces shall be required to wear appropriate uniforms.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article V. Department of Public Safety›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12233. Powers of department; exception
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article V. Department of Public Safety › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12233. Powers of department; exception
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12233. Powers of department; exception (2023)
content:
The department of public safety shall have the care, management, administration, and
   supervision of the police affairs and all matters relating to the fire and police
   forces, electrical service (except electrical lighting), erection of fire-escapes,
   and the inspection of buildings, elevators, engines, and boilers.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article VI. Department of Public Works›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12261. Director of public works; appointment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article VI. Department of Public Works › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12261. Director of public works; appointment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12261. Director of public works; appointment (2023)
content:
There shall be a department of public works of which the director of public works
   shall be the head.  He shall be appointed by the mayor, by and with the advice and consent of the council,
   and shall hold office during the term for which the mayor appointing him was elected
   and until his successor is appointed and qualified.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article V. Department of Public Safety›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12231. Director of public safety; appointment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article V. Department of Public Safety › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12231. Director of public safety; appointment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12231. Director of public safety; appointment (2023)
content:
There shall be a department of public safety of which the director of public safety
   shall be the head.  He shall be appointed by the mayor, by and with the advice and consent of the council,
   and shall hold office during the term for which the mayor appointing him was elected
   and until his successor is appointed and qualified.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Impeachment, Suspension and Removal›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12204. Trial
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Impeachment, Suspension and Removal › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12204. Trial
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12204. Trial (2023)
content:
The president judge of the said court of common pleas or, in his absence, and1associate judge thereof, shall preside during the trial, and decide finally all questions
   of law and evidence that may arise in the case.  He shall have the power to issue subpoenas for witnesses, and compel their attendance
   by attachment and the production of books, papers, and documentary evidence required
   or called for by the said court of impeachment, and to punish witnesses and others
   for contempt, as fully as any court of this Commonwealth may lawfully do in any case.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article V. Department of Public Safety›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12234. Qualifications of policemen and firemen
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article V. Department of Public Safety › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12234. Qualifications of policemen and firemen
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12234. Qualifications of policemen and firemen (2023)
content:
No person shall be employed in the department of public safety as a policeman or fireman
   who is not a citizen of the United States, or who has been convicted of crime unless
   pardoned, or who cannot read or write understandingly in the English language, or
   who shall not have resided within the State at least one year preceding his appointment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article VI. Department of Public Works›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12262. Assistant director; other officers and employes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article VI. Department of Public Works › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12262. Assistant director; other officers and employes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12262. Assistant director; other officers and employes (2023)
content:
The director of public works shall have the power to appoint an assistant director,
   who, in the absence or incapacity of the director to act, shall possess all the powers
   and perform all the duties of the director until the incapacity or inability of the
   director is removed or until a new director is appointed and qualified as hereinbefore
   provided.  The director shall also appoint such other officers and employes as may be provided
   for by ordinance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article V. Department of Public Safety›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12236. Additional patrolmen for special places
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article V. Department of Public Safety › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12236. Additional patrolmen for special places
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12236. Additional patrolmen for special places (2023)
content:
The director of public safety may appoint, and cause to be sworn in, any number of
   additional patrolmen to do duty at any place in the city designated by, and at the
   charge and expense of, the person or persons who may ask for such appointment.  They shall be subject to and obey the orders, rules, and regulations of the department,
   and conform to the general discipline and special regulations thereof.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article VII. Department of Public Health›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12291. Director of public health; appointment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article VII. Department of Public Health › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12291. Director of public health; appointment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12291. Director of public health; appointment (2023)
content:
There shall be a department of public health of which the director of public health
   shall be the head.  He shall be appointed by the mayor, by and with the advice and consent of the council,
   and shall hold office during the term for which the mayor appointing him was elected
   and until his successor is appointed and qualified.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article VI. Department of Public Works›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12263. Powers of department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article VI. Department of Public Works › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12263. Powers of department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12263. Powers of department (2023)
content:
The department of public works shall have the care, management, administration, and
   supervision of waterworks, gas-works, and other public utilities (except as otherwise
   provided in this act) owned or controlled by the city, the supply and distribution
   of water and gas, the grading, paving, repairing, cleaning, and lighting of streets,
   alleys, and highways, including footways, the construction, protection, maintenance,
   operation, and repair of public buildings, bridges, and structures of every kind for
   public use, public squares, real estate (except as otherwise provided by this act
   or as is now or may hereafter be provided by law or ordinance), surveys, engineering,
   sewerage, drainage, and all matters and things in any way relating to or affecting
   the highways or footways of the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article VIII. Department of Public Welfare›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12321. Director of human services; appointment

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article VII. Department of Public Health›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12294. Board of health
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article VII. Department of Public Health › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12294. Board of health
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12294. Board of health (2023)
content:
The board of health shall consist of the director of public health, who shall be president
   thereof, and two other members, who shall be appointed by the mayor, by and with the
   advice and consent of the council, and shall hold office during the term for which
   the mayor appointing them was elected and until their successors shall be appointed
   and qualified.  Two of the members of the said board shall be physicians.  The said board shall be attached to, and be a part of, the department of public
   health, and shall have the powers and duties now vested in it by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article VIII. Department of Public Welfare›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12324. Charge of grounds offered temporarily for playgrounds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article VIII. Department of Public Welfare › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12324. Charge of grounds offered temporarily for playgrounds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12324. Charge of grounds offered temporarily for playgrounds (2023)
content:
The department of public welfare1may, on its own initiative, take charge of any grounds, with buildings thereon erected,
   the use of which is offered to it temporarily by individuals or corporations for the
   purpose of using such grounds for public playgrounds and recreation activities.  It may assume the charge and care of school playgrounds during vacation periods
   if so requested by resolution of the proper school authorities.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article VII. Department of Public Health›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12293. Powers of department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part II. Cities of the First Class › Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law › Article VII. Department of Public Health › PA ST 53 P.S. § 12293. Powers of department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12293. Powers of department (2023)
content:
The department of public health shall have the care, management, administration, and
   supervision of city activities relating to public health, including hospitals, control
   of housing, and sanitation, and collection of vital statistics.  The department shall have all the powers and duties now conferred by law upon the
   bureau of health in such city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part II. Cities of the First Class›Chapter 31. First Class City Government Law›Article IX. Department of Wharves, Docks and Ferries›PA ST 53 P.S. § 12351. Director of wharves, docks and ferries; appointment

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 12351. Director of wharves, docks and ferries; appointment (2023)
content:
There shall be a department of wharves, docks, and ferries, of which the director
   of wharves, docks, and ferries shall be the head.  He shall be appointed by the mayor, by and with the advice and consent of the council,
   and shall hold office during the term for which the mayor appointing him was elected
   and until his successor is appointed and qualified.
