title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22508. Appointment of departmental officers; term of office
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22508. Appointment of departmental officers; term of office (2023)
content:
The city recorder shall nominate and, by and with the advice and consent of the select
   council, appoint the following officers, who shall hold office during the term for
   which the city recorder was elected, and until their successors shall be respectively
   appointed and qualified:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article I. General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22506. Bonds of officers and employees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22506. Bonds of officers and employees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22506. Bonds of officers and employees (2023)
content:
The heads and members of all departments, and all subordinate officers, clerks, and
   employés, shall give bonds as may be fixed by ordinance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article I. General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22507. Salaries of heads of departments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22507. Salaries of heads of departments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22507. Salaries of heads of departments (2023)
content:
The salaries of the director or head of each department of cities of the second class
   of this Commonwealth shall be fixed by the council of said cities.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article I. General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22510. Appointment and removal of subordinate officers, etc.
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22510. Appointment and removal of subordinate officers, etc.
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22510. Appointment and removal of subordinate officers, etc. (2023)
content:
The directors or chief officers of departments shall appoint all subordinate officers,
   clerks, employés, and by written order, giving their reasons therefor, may remove
   or suspend subordinate officers and clerks, provided the same is not done for political
   reasons.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article II. Department of Public Safety›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22531. Director of public safety; jurisdiction of department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article II. Department of Public Safety › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22531. Director of public safety; jurisdiction of department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22531. Director of public safety; jurisdiction of department (2023)
content:
The department of public safety shall be under the charge of one director, who shall
   be the head thereof.  The care, management, administration and supervision of the police affairs, and
   all matters relating to the public health, to the fire and police force, fire alarm
   telegraph, erection of fire-escapes, and the inspection of buildings and boilers,
   markets and food sold therein, and the construction, protection and repair of buildings
   erected for police and fire purposes, shall be in charge of this department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article I. General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22511. Appointment in case of removal
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22511. Appointment in case of removal
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22511. Appointment in case of removal (2023)
content:
In case of any removal, as provided for in the preceding section,1the director, or head of the department, shall appoint a successor, but all such
   appointments shall be made by reason of the fitness of the appointee and not for political
   purposes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article I. General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22514. Subpoenas and subpoenas duces tecum; contempt
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22514. Subpoenas and subpoenas duces tecum; contempt
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22514. Subpoenas and subpoenas duces tecum; contempt (2023)
content:
In any case where an official or officer of a city of the second class or any agency
   thereof specifically empowered to conduct public hearings, such officer, official
   or agency shall have authority for the purposes of such hearings to issue subpoenas
   for the attendance and giving of testimony of such witnesses as are subject to the
   subpoenas of the courts of record of this Commonwealth, and to issue subpoenas duces
   tecum as to such witnesses.  In the case of an agency, such subpoenas shall issue in the name of the city and
   of the agency upon the signature of the presiding officer thereof and the official
   seal, if any, of the agency.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article I. General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22512. Salaries of municipal officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22512. Salaries of municipal officers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22512. Salaries of municipal officers (2023)
content:
All city officers and employés shall receive a fixed salary for their services, and
   all fees and penalties shall be collected for the city and paid directly into the
   city treasury:  Provided, That the provisions of this article shall not apply to the
   collector of delinquent taxes, who shall receive such compensation as may be fixed
   by councils.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article I. General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22509. Election of city controller; term of office
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22509. Election of city controller; term of office
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22509. Election of city controller; term of office (2023)
content:
The city controller shall be chosen by the qualified electors of the city, at the
   regular municipal election occurring immediately before the expiration of the term
   of the present controller in each of said cities, for the term of three years from
   the first Monday of April next ensuing his election, and until the election and qualification
   of his successor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article II. Department of Public Safety›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22536. Dismissal of policemen; trial; composition of trial court; witnesses; oaths
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article II. Department of Public Safety › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22536. Dismissal of policemen; trial; composition of trial court; witnesses; oaths
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22536. Dismissal of policemen; trial; composition of trial court; witnesses; oaths (2023)
content:
No policeman appointed under this act shall be dismissed without his written consent,
   except by the decision of a court either of trial or inquiry, duly determined and
   certified in writing to the mayor, which court shall be composed of not less than
   three and not more than five persons belonging to the police force, equal or superior
   in official position therein to the accused.  Such decision shall only be determined by trial of charges, with plain specifications
   made by or lodged with the director of the department of public safety, of which trial
   the accused shall have due notice, and at which he shall have the right to be present
   in person.  The persons composing such court shall be appointed and sworn by the director of
   the department of public safety to perform their duties impartially and without fear
   or favor;  and the person of highest rank in such court shall have the same authority
   to issue and enforce process to secure the attendance of witnesses, and to administer
   oaths to witnesses, as is possessed by any justice of the peace1of this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article I. General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22513. Department of public welfare; abolition; transfer of powers, property, etc.
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article I. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22513. Department of public welfare; abolition; transfer of powers, property, etc.
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22513. Department of public welfare; abolition; transfer of powers, property, etc. (2023)
content:
The Department of Public Welfare is hereby abolished.  All of its powers and duties shall hereafter be exercised and performed by the county
   institution district of the county in which the city is located, under the provisions
   of the “County Institution District Law,” approved the twenty-fourth day of June,
   one thousand nine hundred thirty-seven (Pamphlet Laws, two thousand seventeen).1All property of the city, real and personal, used in carrying on the functions of
   the Department of Public Welfare, and all records of said department, shall be transferred
   to the county institution district on the effective day of this act.  All indebtedness of the city, whether current or bonded, incurred in the acquisition
   of any such property, shall continue the debt and obligation of the city and shall
   be paid by it.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article II. Department of Public Safety›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22533. Uniforms
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article II. Department of Public Safety › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22533. Uniforms
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22533. Uniforms (2023)
content:
The department shall make suitable regulations, under which the officers and members
   of the fire, telegraph and police force shall be required to wear an appropriate uniform.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article II. Department of Public Safety›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22537. Nature of trial; decision; penalties; appeal
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article II. Department of Public Safety › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22537. Nature of trial; decision; penalties; appeal
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22537. Nature of trial; decision; penalties; appeal (2023)
content:
Such charges may be of disability for service, in which case the court shall be one
   of inquiry, whose decision may be for the honorable discharge from the service of
   the person concerned;  or, of neglect or violation of law or duty, inefficiency, intemperance,
   disobedience of orders, or unbecoming official or personal conduct, in which cases
   the court shall be one of trial, and its decision may authorize the director of the
   department of public safety to impose fines and pecuniary penalties, to be stopped
   from pay, or to suspend from pay or duty, or both, for a period fixed by them, not
   exceeding one year, or to dismiss from the service.  The right of appeal of the decision of the trial board shall be made within five
   days to the civil service board.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article II. Department of Public Safety›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22532. Qualifications of employees; hours of duty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article II. Department of Public Safety › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22532. Qualifications of employees; hours of duty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22532. Qualifications of employees; hours of duty (2023)
content:
No person shall be employed in this department as a policeman or fireman who is not
   a citizen of the United States, or who has been convicted of crime, unless pardoned,
   or who cannot read and write understandingly in the English language, or who shall
   not have resided within the State at least one year preceding his appointment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article IV. Department of Collector of Delinquent Taxes›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22581. Collector head of department; certain laws to remain in force; compensation of collector
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article IV. Department of Collector of Delinquent Taxes › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22581. Collector head of department; certain laws to remain in force; compensation of collector
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22581. Collector head of department; certain laws to remain in force; compensation of collector (2023)
content:
The collector of delinquent taxes shall be the head of the department of delinquent
   taxes, and all laws and ordinances in force at the passage of this act, relative to
   said offices and the collection of delinquent taxes, shall be and remain in full force,
   except so far as the election of the collector of delinquent taxes is therein given
   to councils.  The head of this department shall receive such compensation, either by a stated
   salary or by fees, as may be fixed by councils.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article II. Department of Public Safety›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22535. Police and firemen's pension fund
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article II. Department of Public Safety › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22535. Police and firemen's pension fund
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22535. Police and firemen's pension fund (2023)
content:
The city councils may provide by ordinance a fund for the care, maintenance, and relief
   of aged, retired, disabled, or injured policemen or firemen, and the families of such
   as may be injured or killed in the service.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article IV. Department of Collector of Delinquent Taxes›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22582. Abolition of office of collector in cities of second class; unexecuted warrants; interest and penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article IV. Department of Collector of Delinquent Taxes › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22582. Abolition of office of collector in cities of second class; unexecuted warrants; interest and penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22582. Abolition of office of collector in cities of second class; unexecuted warrants; interest and penalties (2023)
content:
Wherever the office of collector of delinquent taxes now exists in any city of the
   second class by virtue either of any general, special or local act, the office may
   be abolished by ordinance of such cities.  The collectors of delinquent taxes, who shall, upon the effective date of any such
   ordinance, have in their possession a warrant or warrants for the collection of delinquent
   taxes that are not fully executed, shall continue to collect such taxes with the same
   powers as heretofore and shall receive therefor the same compensation.  None of the interest or penalties for delinquent payments of taxes imposed under
   the provisions of existing laws, whether as compensation to the delinquent tax collectors
   or otherwise, shall be abated or otherwise affected by the provisions of any such
   ordinance, but the full amount of the same shall be collected as hereinafter provided
   and paid into the city fund of the city treasury for the use of the city, unless abated
   by other legislation heretofore or hereafter enacted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article II. Department of Public Safety›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22539. Finding of court to be approved by mayor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article II. Department of Public Safety › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22539. Finding of court to be approved by mayor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22539. Finding of court to be approved by mayor (2023)
content:
The finding of the court of trial or inquiry, as aforesaid, shall be of no effect
   until approved by the mayor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article II. Department of Public Safety›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22538. Suspension of accused; trial not to be delayed
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article II. Department of Public Safety › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22538. Suspension of accused; trial not to be delayed
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22538. Suspension of accused; trial not to be delayed (2023)
content:
It shall be lawful for the director of the department of public safety, at his discretion,
   to suspend from duty before trial any person charged, as aforesaid, until such trial
   can be had, with or without pay as such court shall afterward determine, but no trial
   shall be delayed for more than one month after charge has been made.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article III. . Department of Public Works›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22562. Offal, garbage and swill; duties transferred to Department of Public Works
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article III. . Department of Public Works › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22562. Offal, garbage and swill; duties transferred to Department of Public Works
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22562. Offal, garbage and swill; duties transferred to Department of Public Works (2023)
content:
All the powers and authority set forth in section twenty of the act, approved the
   twenty-sixth day of June, one thousand eight hundred ninety-five (Pamphlet Laws, three
   hundred fifty),1conferred upon the Director of the Department of Public Safety relative to entering
   into contracts for the removal and disposal of all offal, garbage, and swill, and
   all the duties imposed by said section upon the Bureau of Health and which were later
   transferred to the Department of Public Health by section four of the act, approved
   the first day of April, one thousand nine hundred nine (Pamphlet Laws, eighty-three),2are hereby transferred and retransferred to, and shall hereafter by exercised by,
   the Department of Public Works.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article IV. Department of Collector of Delinquent Taxes›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22583. Collection of delinquent taxes by city treasurer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article IV. Department of Collector of Delinquent Taxes › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22583. Collection of delinquent taxes by city treasurer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22583. Collection of delinquent taxes by city treasurer (2023)
content:
Any such ordinance abolishing the office of collector of delinquent taxes in any city
   of the second class shall provide that the treasurer of the city shall collect all
   delinquent city taxes, interest and penalties, and shall have all powers of delinquent
   tax collectors in cities of such class under the provisions of existing laws, and
   for such purpose the city treasurers in cities of the second class may appoint clerks
   and employes whose positions shall be established and the compensation therefor fixed
   as prescribed by law for similar employes in the department of the city treasurer.  The city treasurer shall receive no additional compensation for the collection of
   delinquent taxes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article IV. Department of Collector of Delinquent Taxes›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22584. Collection of delinquent city taxes; salaries and expenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article IV. Department of Collector of Delinquent Taxes › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22584. Collection of delinquent city taxes; salaries and expenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22584. Collection of delinquent city taxes; salaries and expenses (2023)
content:
Concurrently with or subsequent to abolishing the office of collector of delinquent
   taxes, the council in cities of the second class shall, at the cost of the city, provide
   for and pay the compensation of the clerks and employes appointed by the city treasurer
   for the collection of delinquent taxes as hereinabove provided, and shall also furnish
   the city treasurer at the cost of the city with office space, office furniture, equipment,
   supplies, books of record, stationery, postage and pay all other necessary expense
   in connection with the collection of such delinquent city taxes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article V. Department of City Treasurer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22602. Qualifications of city treasurer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article V. Department of City Treasurer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22602. Qualifications of city treasurer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22602. Qualifications of city treasurer (2023)
content:
No person shall be eligible to the office of treasurer except a citizen of the city,
   a resident therein for seven years next preceding his appointment, unless he shall
   have been absent on public business of the United States or of this state.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article II. Department of Public Safety›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22540. Health and building laws unaffected
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article II. Department of Public Safety › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22540. Health and building laws unaffected
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22540. Health and building laws unaffected (2023)
content:
The laws in relation to health, buildings and building inspection, remain unaffected
   by any of the provisions thereof, and the board of health and the building inspectors
   shall remain as heretofore, and shall be attached to the Department of Public Safety.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article V. Department of City Treasurer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22601. City treasurer head of department; term of office
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article V. Department of City Treasurer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22601. City treasurer head of department; term of office
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22601. City treasurer head of department; term of office (2023)
content:
The department of city treasurer shall be under the charge of the city treasurer,
   who shall be the head thereof;  who shall hold his office for the term of three years,
   and until his successor is chosen and qualified.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article IV. Department of Collector of Delinquent Taxes›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22585. Transfer of employees to city treasurer's office; membership in retirement system
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article IV. Department of Collector of Delinquent Taxes › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22585. Transfer of employees to city treasurer's office; membership in retirement system
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22585. Transfer of employees to city treasurer's office; membership in retirement system (2023)
content:
All clerks and employes employed in the office of the collector of delinquent city
   taxes, abolished by ordinance pursuant to this act, shall be transferred to and become
   employes of the city treasurer's office.  All such clerks and employes shall become eligible to membership in the retirement
   system established for city employes, and shall be entitled to receive credit in the
   retirement system as city employes for all years of service in the office of the collector
   of delinquent taxes upon payment into the retirement fund of a sum equal to the amount
   such persons would have paid into such fund, if they had joined the retirement system
   at the time the same was established if them employed in the office of the delinquent
   tax collector, or if employed first at a later date then a sum equal to the amount
   such persons would have paid into such fund from the time they were first so employed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article III. . Department of Public Works›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22561. Director of public works; jurisdiction of department; laws relating to parks to remain in force
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article III. . Department of Public Works › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22561. Director of public works; jurisdiction of department; laws relating to parks to remain in force
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22561. Director of public works; jurisdiction of department; laws relating to parks to remain in force (2023)
content:
The Department of Public Works shall be under the charge of one director, who shall
   be the head thereof.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article V. Department of City Treasurer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22603. Duties and powers of city treasurer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article V. Department of City Treasurer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22603. Duties and powers of city treasurer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22603. Duties and powers of city treasurer (2023)
content:
The city treasurer shall receive the proceeds of all public loans, and shall demand
   and receive from the proper officers all moneys payable to the city from whatever
   source, and pay all warrants duly issued and countersigned;  the receipt and collection
   of funds derived from assessments, taxes, water rents, licenses, permits and rents,
   from markets, landings, wharves and other public property, excepting delinquent taxes
   and water rents, shall be attached and subordinate to this department and subject
   to its supervision, control and direction:  Provided, however, That nothing herein
   contained shall prohibit the city treasurer from enforcing collection of delinquent
   taxes in accordance with the provisions of the act, approved the thirtieth day of
   March, one thousand nine hundred and three (Pamphlet Laws, one hundred six), entitled,
   “An act authorizing and empowering the city treasurers of the several cities of second
   class and third class of this Commonwealth to sell at public sale all properties upon
   which the taxes, assessed and levied, are delinquent and remain unpaid”.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article V. Department of City Treasurer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22605. Accounts of treasurer; deposits; reports; security for deposits
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article V. Department of City Treasurer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22605. Accounts of treasurer; deposits; reports; security for deposits
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22605. Accounts of treasurer; deposits; reports; security for deposits (2023)
content:
The treasurer shall keep the accounts, arising from the several sources of revenue
   and income, separate and distinct from one another, and shall make daily deposits
   of all moneys received by him in such banks or institutions as may be designated by
   councils, and shall make specific reports daily to the controller, of all receipts
   and deposits, and of all moneys withdrawn from the treasury, and shall present and
   verify his cash account in such manner and as often as may be required.  All depositories of city funds or other funds for which such city, or any officer
   or employe thereof, shall act as custodian or trustee, wherein the legal or equitable
   title in such funds, shall belong to persons, copartnerships, corporations or the
   Federal or State government, or any agency or subdivision thereof, other than such
   city, shall, upon the receipt of notice of their selection as depositories of city
   or other funds, furnish a bond to secure payment of deposits and interest to the city
   with a proper warrant of attorney to confess judgment in favor of the city, secured
   by a surety company or individual sureties to be approved by the court of common pleas.  Such bonds shall in all cases be in the amount of the deposit to be made.  If a corporate bond is given, no one surety company shall be approved in an aggregate
   amount in excess of five times the capital, surplus and reserve.  Whenever individual sureties are presented for approval they shall qualify in an
   aggregate over and above their individual liabilities to three times the amount of
   the deposit.  No one person may qualify for more than one-fourth of the total amount of the bond
   required:  Provided, That in lieu of surety bonds of surety companies or of individual
   sureties, the deposit of city or other moneys may be secured by the deposit with the
   city treasurer of bonds or other interest bearing obligations of the United States,
   or of any county, municipality or municipal district of the Commonwealth, in an amount
   equal to the deposit so secured and twenty per centum in addition thereto:  And provided
   also, That the city treasurer may direct that the said bonds or other interest-bearing
   obligations be deposited in a Federal Reserve Bank, or a branch thereof located in
   the city, or with any bank or bank and trust company organized under the laws of this
   Commonwealth, or any national banking association located in this Commonwealth, which
   shall be approved by the city treasurer to secure the deposit of city or other moneys.  Said bonds or other interest-bearing obligations shall be accompanied by a proper
   assignment or power of attorney to transfer the same, and any such deposit of securities
   shall be maintained to the full amount required in case of any depreciation in value
   thereof.  When said bonds and other interest-bearing obligations are deposited with the Federal
   Reserve Bank, or a branch thereof, the bank shall perform such functions as may be
   prescribed by agreement between the city and the bank.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article V. Department of City Treasurer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22604. Drawing money from treasury
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article V. Department of City Treasurer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22604. Drawing money from treasury
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22604. Drawing money from treasury (2023)
content:
No money shall be drawn from the city treasury except by due process of law, or upon
   warrants on the treasurer, or by checks signed in the manner prescribed by the council
   and countersigned by the controller which warrants or checks shall state the consideration
   of the same and the particular fund or appropriation to which the same is chargeable.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article V. Department of City Treasurer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22606. City monies to be deposited daily in city treasury
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article V. Department of City Treasurer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22606. City monies to be deposited daily in city treasury
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22606. City monies to be deposited daily in city treasury (2023)
content:
All the moneys of the city, received by any officer or agent thereof, except those
   received by the collector of delinquent taxes, the department of law and police magistrate,1shall be deposited daily in the city treasury.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VI. Department of City Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22621. City controller to be head of department; term of office
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VI. Department of City Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22621. City controller to be head of department; term of office
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22621. City controller to be head of department; term of office (2023)
content:
The city controller shall be the head of this department;  he shall hold his office
   for a term of three years, and until his successor shall be duly chosen and qualified.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VI. Department of City Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22625. Drawing of appropriations regulated
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VI. Department of City Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22625. Drawing of appropriations regulated
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22625. Drawing of appropriations regulated (2023)
content:
He shall not suffer any appropriation to be overdrawn, or the appropriation for one
   item of expense to be drawn upon for any other purpose, or by any department other
   than that for which the appropriation was specifically made, except on transfers made
   by ordinance of councils;  or unless sufficient funds, out of which said warrant is
   payable, shall actually be in the treasury at the time.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VI. Department of City Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22631. Audit of accounts of officers; proceedings in case officer is indebted to city; appeal
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VI. Department of City Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22631. Audit of accounts of officers; proceedings in case officer is indebted to city; appeal
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22631. Audit of accounts of officers; proceedings in case officer is indebted to city; appeal (2023)
content:
The controller shall, at the end of each fiscal year, or oftener if so required by
   councils, and also upon the death, resignation, removal or expiration of the term
   of any officer, audit, examine and settle the accounts of such officer;  and if he
   shall be found indebted to the city, the controller shall state an account and file
   the same in the court of common pleas of the proper county, together with a copy of
   the official bond of such officer, and give notice thereof to him or his legal representatives,
   and if any person or persons affected thereby shall be dissatisfied with such settlement
   he or they may appeal therefrom.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VI. Department of City Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22628. Other duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VI. Department of City Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22628. Other duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22628. Other duties (2023)
content:
He shall also perform all duties required of him by law or ordinance, not inconsistent
   with the provision1hereof.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VI. Department of City Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22623. Audit of accounts; annual report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VI. Department of City Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22623. Audit of accounts; annual report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22623. Audit of accounts; annual report (2023)
content:
Audit the accounts of the several departments and trusts, and all other accounts in
   which the city is concerned, and submit annually to councils, in such manner as may
   by ordinance be directed, a report of the accounts of the city, verified by his oath
   or affirmation, exhibiting the revenues, receipts and expenditures, the sources from
   which the revenues and funds are derived, and in what manner the same have been disbursed,
   which report shall be published in pamphlet or book form.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VI. Department of City Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22630. Contracts to be certified and charged against appropriation; liability for certification in excess of appropriation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VI. Department of City Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22630. Contracts to be certified and charged against appropriation; liability for certification in excess of appropriation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22630. Contracts to be certified and charged against appropriation; liability for certification in excess of appropriation (2023)
content:
Every contract involving an appropriation of money shall designate the item of appropriation
   on which it is founded, and shall be numbered by the controller in the order of its
   date, and charged as numbered against such item, and so certified by him, before it
   shall take effect as a contract, and shall not be payable out of any other fund; 
   and if he shall certify any contract in excess of the appropriation properly applicable
   thereto, the city shall not be liable for such excess, but the controller and his
   sureties shall be liable in damages for an amount not exceeding such excess, which
   may be recovered in an action on the case for negligence by the contracting party
   aggrieved:  Provided, That so much of this section that enacts that a contract, certified
   by the controller, shall not be payable out of any other fund than the item of appropriation
   against which it is numbered, shall not apply to such contracts for public improvement
   as are referred to in Article XV, Section 1,1hereof.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VI. Department of City Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22624. Appropriation accounts; detailed statements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VI. Department of City Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22624. Appropriation accounts; detailed statements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22624. Appropriation accounts; detailed statements (2023)
content:
Keep separate accounts for each specific item or appropriation made by councils to
   each department, and require all warrants to state specifically against which of said
   items the warrant is drawn.  Each account shall be accompanied by a statement in detail, in separate columns,
   of the several appropriations made by councils, the amount drawn on each appropriation,
   the unpaid contracts charged against it, and the balance standing to the credit of
   the same.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VI. Department of City Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22627. Examination into propriety of claims
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VI. Department of City Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22627. Examination into propriety of claims
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22627. Examination into propriety of claims (2023)
content:
Whenever a warrant or claim shall be presented to him, he shall have power to require
   evidence that the amount claimed is justly due, and for that purpose may summon before
   him any officer, agent or employés of any department of the city, or any other person,
   and examine him, upon oath or affirmation, relative to such warrant or claim.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VI. Department of City Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22635. Deputy controller; election by council; bond and compensation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VI. Department of City Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22635. Deputy controller; election by council; bond and compensation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22635. Deputy controller; election by council; bond and compensation (2023)
content:
The controller of the cities of the second class is hereby authorized to appoint a
   deputy controller, who, in case of death, resignation, sickness, absence or inability
   of such controller to act, shall have the same powers and shall perform the same duty
   as imposed by law upon the city controller.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VI. Department of City Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22632. Proceedings in case of appeal
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VI. Department of City Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22632. Proceedings in case of appeal
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22632. Proceedings in case of appeal (2023)
content:
The appeal, with his or their exceptions to the account as stated, verified by the
   oath of the person or persons appealing, shall be filed in the office of the prothonotary
   of said court within ten days after the service of notice.  The appellant shall, within ten days, enter security, to be approved by the court,
   to prosecute the appeal with effect, and pay the costs and the debt and interest which
   may appear by the judgment of the court to be due to the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VI. Department of City Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22636. Solicitor for department; salary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VI. Department of City Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22636. Solicitor for department; salary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22636. Solicitor for department; salary (2023)
content:
The city controller of each city of the second class shall designate and appoint one
   person, learned in the law, to act as solicitor for the department of city controller.  Such solicitor shall be an attorney at law, admitted and qualified to practice in
   the courts of this Commonwealth.  Such solicitor shall be the legal adviser of the city controller in matters pertaining
   to or affecting his department, and he shall, when requested by the city controller,
   act as his counsel in any litigation involving any matter or thing pertaining to or
   affecting the department of city controller.  The authorization, in writing, of the city controller in all cases shall be a sufficient
   warrant of attorney for appearing for and representing him in any such litigation.  The solicitor shall hold office at the pleasure of the city controller, and shall
   be paid a salary not less than three thousand six hundred dollars ($3,600) per annum,
   as the city by ordinance shall provide, and there shall be appropriated a sufficient
   sum of money for that purpose.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VI. Department of City Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22622. Duties of city controller; inspection and revision of accounts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VI. Department of City Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22622. Duties of city controller; inspection and revision of accounts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22622. Duties of city controller; inspection and revision of accounts (2023)
content: The city controller shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VI. Department of City Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22626. Notice when warrant should not be approved; liability for improper approval
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VI. Department of City Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22626. Notice when warrant should not be approved; liability for improper approval
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22626. Notice when warrant should not be approved; liability for improper approval (2023)
content:
If any warrant presented to the controller contain an item for which no appropriation
   has been made, or there shall not be a sufficient balance of the proper fund for the
   payment thereof, or which for any other cause should not be approved, he shall notify
   the proper department of the fact;  and if the controller shall approve any warrant,
   contrary to the provisions hereof, he and his sureties shall be individually liable
   for the amount of the same to the holder thereof.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VI. Department of City Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22634. Notice of audit of account; hearing
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VI. Department of City Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22634. Notice of audit of account; hearing
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22634. Notice of audit of account; hearing (2023)
content:
Notice of the audit shall be given by the controller to the officer or his legal representatives,
   before the final statement of the account, and if desired by such officer or his legal
   representatives, opportunity shall be given for a hearing.  A copy of such notice, with an affidavit of the proof of service thereof, shall
   be filed with the statement of account, as evidence of service of notice.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VI. Department of City Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22629. Departments to make monthly statements to controller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VI. Department of City Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22629. Departments to make monthly statements to controller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22629. Departments to make monthly statements to controller (2023)
content:
Detailed statements of the receipts and expenditures of the several departments shall
   be made on the third Monday of each month to the controller.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VI. Department of City Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22637. Probate clerks; appointment; powers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VI. Department of City Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22637. Probate clerks; appointment; powers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22637. Probate clerks; appointment; powers (2023)
content:
Controllers of the several cities of this Commonwealth shall be and are hereby authorized
   to appoint, from among their employes, one or more persons to be probate clerks, who
   shall have power to administer oaths or affirmations in all matters relating to accounts
   against said city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VI. Department of City Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22633. Balance of account to be a lien; proceedings to enforce lien; limitation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VI. Department of City Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22633. Balance of account to be a lien; proceedings to enforce lien; limitation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22633. Balance of account to be a lien; proceedings to enforce lien; limitation (2023)
content:
The balance of account, as shown by the settlement filed as aforesaid, shall constitute
   a lien on the real estate of the officer, so indebted, and his sureties from the date
   of the filing thereof, which lien shall continue for the period of five years from
   the date of filing.  A writ of scire facias to enforce the lien shall be issued thereon within six months,
   which shall contain a clause warning the sureties, or the executors or administrators
   of the officer or of his sureties, to appear and make defense, and the case shall
   thereupon be proceeded with to final judgment, according to law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VII. Department of Law›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22652. Duties of city solicitor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VII. Department of Law › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22652. Duties of city solicitor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22652. Duties of city solicitor (2023)
content: The city solicitor shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VII. Department of Law›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22653. Employment of other counsel by departments; by mayor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VII. Department of Law › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22653. Employment of other counsel by departments; by mayor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22653. Employment of other counsel by departments; by mayor (2023)
content:
No department of the city shall employ and other solicitor, but assistant counsel
   may be employed in any particular matter or cause by the city recorder, with the consent
   of councils, but he shall be selected by the city solicitor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VII. Department of Law›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22651. City solicitor head of department; term of office; assistants and clerks; qualifications
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VII. Department of Law › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22651. City solicitor head of department; term of office; assistants and clerks; qualifications
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22651. City solicitor head of department; term of office; assistants and clerks; qualifications (2023)
content:
The department of law shall consist of a city solicitor, who shall be the head thereof,
   and shall hold his office for a term of three years, and until his successor shall
   be duly chosen and qualified.  The department shall have as many assistants and clerks as may be authorized by
   ordinance, who shall be appointed by the city solicitor.  The solicitor and assistant solicitors shall be attorneys-at-law, admitted and qualified
   to practice in the courts of this commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VII. Department of Law›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22654. Bureau of conciliation, small claims, and legal aid
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VII. Department of Law › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22654. Bureau of conciliation, small claims, and legal aid
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22654. Bureau of conciliation, small claims, and legal aid (2023)
content:
That cities of the second class be, and they are hereby, authorized and empowered
   to maintain, as part of their legal department, a Bureau of Conciliation, Small Claims,
   and Legal Aid, and through such bureau, to render legal aid, in meritorious cases,
   without charge, to applicants whose claims and means are such as to make it impracticable
   to employ counsel, and, to that end, to take over the funds and like cases of any
   existing legal aid society desirous of surrendering its functions and assets to such
   city;  and such city is hereby empowered to select and pay such employés, and incur
   such expenses, and make such appropriations, and do all such other things as, in the
   discretion of the municipal authorities, may be necessary or convenient to carry out
   the power and authority hereby conferred.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VIII. Sinking Fund Commission›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22675. Fund for retirement of funded indebtedness; accounts; appropriations; amortization schedule
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VIII. Sinking Fund Commission › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22675. Fund for retirement of funded indebtedness; accounts; appropriations; amortization schedule
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22675. Fund for retirement of funded indebtedness; accounts; appropriations; amortization schedule (2023)
content:
It shall be the duty of said Sinking Fund Commission to establish and maintain a fund
   for the reduction and retirement of the funded indebtedness of said cities, the whole
   or any part of which is outstanding.  Proper accounts shall be kept thereof;  and there shall be appropriated to and set
   apart annually for the Sinking Fund Commission, for each issue of bonds, such nearly
   equal amounts at least, as appropriated annually over the term of such bonds, as will,
   at the earning or established rate of interest, at the maturity of each issue of bonds
   equal the total amount of such issue.  The Sinking Fund Commission shall provide each year an amortization schedule, to
   be based upon the actual earning rate of interest on its investments;  and this amortization
   schedule shall be a calculation taking into account any amounts of loss or gain there
   may be by reason of a lesser or greater rate of interest being received than that
   used in the calculation for the preceding annual schedule.  Said1commission shall always have on hand investments and moneys at least equal in amount
   to the total sum of such payments into the sinking fund, plus the accrued interest
   earnings calculated on said basis.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VIII. Sinking Fund Commission›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22673. To have charge of sinking funds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VIII. Sinking Fund Commission › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22673. To have charge of sinking funds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22673. To have charge of sinking funds (2023)
content:
All moneys applicable to sinking funds shall be under the charge of the commission,
   and shall be used for the extinguishment of the city debt.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VIII. Sinking Fund Commission›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22678. Cancellation of bonds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VIII. Sinking Fund Commission › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22678. Cancellation of bonds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22678. Cancellation of bonds (2023)
content:
All matured bonds held in such sinking fund shall at maturity be cancelled.  As often as the sinking fund shall be in excess of the amount required by section
   three of this act,1said commission shall have the right to cancel, to the extent of such excess, any
   of its own bonds held in such sinking fund.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VIII. Sinking Fund Commission›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22676. Reduction of appropriations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VIII. Sinking Fund Commission › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22676. Reduction of appropriations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22676. Reduction of appropriations (2023)
content:
If at any time the amount of cash and investments held in the sinking fund exceed
   the proportionate amount required by section three hereof, the Sinking Fund Commission
   shall, if it deems it expedient so to do, have the right to credit such excess, or
   any part thereof, against the appropriation that would otherwise be required for the
   following year or years, and the next and succeeding annual amounts required to be
   appropriated shall be reduced accordingly.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A›Chapter 71. General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 30101. Official advertising; matter to be published; contracts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A › Chapter 71. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 30101. Official advertising; matter to be published; contracts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 30101. Official advertising; matter to be published; contracts (2023)
content:
At the expiration of present contracts for official advertising in cities of the second
   class A, and every three years thereafter, the mayor of any said city shall contract
   for a term of three years with not less than four nor more than five newspapers of
   general circulation, one of which may be a newspaper published weekly on Sundays and
   the others daily newspapers published within the county in which such city of the
   second class A is situated, for the publication of all official advertising, the cost
   of which is payable out of the city treasury;  which said official advertising shall
   include all ordinances of councils, mayors' proclamations, all official reports of
   the city officers, all notices for the opening, widening, straightening, grading,
   paving, and curbing and vacation of streets, lanes, and alleys, and the construction
   of sewers, including all viewers' reports and proposals for public work and supplies;
   such contracts to be let to the lowest bidder, agate measure per line for each thousand
   of circulation;  the basis of the circulation to be the average daily sales (exclusive
   of Sunday, weekly, semi-weekly, and tri-weekly issues, and also exclusive of all credits
   for returned or unsold newspapers and newspapers distributed free of charge) of such
   daily newspaper and the average weekly sales (exclusive of any semi-weekly and tri-weekly
   issues, and also exclusive of all credits for returned or unsold newspapers and newspapers
   distributed free of charge) of such Sunday newspaper for the period of six months
   next preceding the month in which such advertising may be published.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VIII. Sinking Fund Commission›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22677. Deposit of funds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VIII. Sinking Fund Commission › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22677. Deposit of funds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22677. Deposit of funds (2023)
content:
All moneys applicable to sinking fund purposes shall be deposited in separate accounts,
   to the credit of the Sinking Fund Commission of such cities, in such depositories
   as shall be selected by such cities, and said commission shall require satisfactory
   security from all depositories to protect it from any loss by reason of making deposits
   therein.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A›Chapter 71. General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 30102. Annual budget, adoption of
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A › Chapter 71. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 30102. Annual budget, adoption of
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 30102. Annual budget, adoption of (2023)
content:
In all cities of the second class A in this Commonwealth the city council of such
   cities shall adopt an annual budget only in accordance with the procedure set forth
   in this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VIII. Sinking Fund Commission›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22671. Members of commission; classification; filling of vacancies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VIII. Sinking Fund Commission › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22671. Members of commission; classification; filling of vacancies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22671. Members of commission; classification; filling of vacancies (2023)
content:
The Sinking Fund Commission shall consist of five persons.  Those first appointed under this act shall divide themselves in classes, by lot,
   so that the term of one of the members shall expire each year.  All vacancies shall be filled by appointment, for the term of five years.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VIII. Sinking Fund Commission›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22672. Regulations of department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VIII. Sinking Fund Commission › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22672. Regulations of department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22672. Regulations of department (2023)
content: Councils shall make all necessary rules for the government of this department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A›Chapter 71. General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 30106. Compiling, codifying and reenacting ordinances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A › Chapter 71. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 30106. Compiling, codifying and reenacting ordinances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 30106. Compiling, codifying and reenacting ordinances (2023)
content:
(a) The city council of any city of the second class-A may compile, codify, recodify
      and reenact any existing two or more ordinances with or without repeals, amendments
      and additions, and enact the same as one codified ordinance arranged in appropriate
      divisions with one title and one enacting clause.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VIII. Sinking Fund Commission›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22674. Investment of funds; sale or exchange of bonds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VIII. Sinking Fund Commission › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22674. Investment of funds; sale or exchange of bonds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22674. Investment of funds; sale or exchange of bonds (2023)
content:
The commission shall, from time to time and without unreasonable delay, invest all
   balances remaining to the credit of the sinking funds, not immediately applicable
   to the extinguishment of the city debt, in any proper bonds issued by such city, the
   United States, State of Pennsylvania, and not otherwise.  Said commission shall, as and when it deems it necessary, have the right to sell
   or exchange at the market rate any bonds so purchased:  Provided, That no bonds so
   purchased shall be sold at less than par value and accrued interest, unless said commission
   shall be authorized so to do by an ordinance of the council, and the council shall
   appropriate and pay over to such Sinking Fund Commission any such difference between
   the selling price thereof and par value of accrued interest.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A›Chapter 71. General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 30103. Inspection of records, books and documents by taxpayers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A › Chapter 71. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 30103. Inspection of records, books and documents by taxpayers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 30103. Inspection of records, books and documents by taxpayers (2023)
content:
All fiscal records, minute books and documents of cities of the second class A shall
   be open to the inspection of any taxpayer, his, her or its agent, upon demand therefor,
   but the proper officers charged with the custody of such records, books and documents
   may make reasonable rules and regulations designating the time and place of such inspection.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A›Chapter 73. Officers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 30352. Deputy mayor, appointment of
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A › Chapter 73. Officers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 30352. Deputy mayor, appointment of
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 30352. Deputy mayor, appointment of (2023)
content:
In all cities of the second class A of this Commonwealth, the mayor thereof, in addition
   to the powers now possessed, is hereby authorized and empowered to designate, in writing,
   and file with the city clerk of said city, one of the heads of the city departments,
   entitled to vote as set forth in section four, except the city controller, to act
   as deputy mayor in case of the necessary absence of the mayor from the city, or his
   illness or other temporary disability.  The person so designated shall be known as deputy mayor, and shall exercise all
   the powers and discharge all the duties of mayor, during said absence, illness or
   temporary disability, except the power of appointing to or discharging from office
   in the city government.  Such head of department shall serve without additional compensation;  and such deputy
   mayor shall give bond, to be approved by the city solicitor, in an amount equal to
   one-half of the bond furnished by the mayor;  said bond to be deposited with the city
   controller.  The deputy mayor shall take the same oath of office as that prescribed by law for
   the mayor.  The premium for said bond shall be paid by said city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A›Chapter 73. Officers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 30351. Salary of officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A › Chapter 73. Officers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 30351. Salary of officers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 30351. Salary of officers (2023)
content:
The city council in cities of the second class A shall fix the salary of the mayor,
   the members of council, the controller, and appointed city officers.  The salary of the mayor shall be not less than seven thousand five hundred dollars
   ($7,500) per annum;  the salary of each member of council shall be not less than five
   thousand dollars ($5,000) per annum;  the salary of the controller and the salaries
   of appointed city officers shall be fixed by the city council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part III. Cities of the Second Class›Article VIII. Sinking Fund Commission›PA ST 53 P.S. § 22679. Bonds to be payable in annual installments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part III. Cities of the Second Class › Article VIII. Sinking Fund Commission › PA ST 53 P.S. § 22679. Bonds to be payable in annual installments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 22679. Bonds to be payable in annual installments (2023)
content: All bonds hereafter issued by said cities shall be made payable in equal annual installments.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A›Chapter 71. General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 30107. Borrowing money and increasing indebtedness
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A › Chapter 71. General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 30107. Borrowing money and increasing indebtedness
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 30107. Borrowing money and increasing indebtedness (2023)
content:
Every city of the second class A, in its corporate capacity, is authorized and empowered
   to enact ordinances to borrow money on the credit of the city, and to pledge the credit
   and revenue thereof for the payment of the same, to an amount not exceeding five percent
   upon the assessed value of the taxable property in said city, and with the consent
   of the people of the said city, obtained at an election held under the provisions
   of the Constitution and the general laws of this Commonwealth, to increase the indebtedness
   of such city to an amount not exceeding, in the aggregate, fifteen percent upon the
   assessed valuation of the taxable property therein.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A›Chapter 73. Officers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 30354. Present mayors to designate deputy mayors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A › Chapter 73. Officers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 30354. Present mayors to designate deputy mayors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 30354. Present mayors to designate deputy mayors (2023)
content:
The mayors of cities of the second class A shall, within thirty days after the effective
   date of this act, designate, in writing to the city clerk, the appointment of a deputy
   mayor in accordance with the provisions of this act.  Any person, elected mayor of a city of the second class A, or vested with the power
   of mayor shall, within the period of thirty days after assuming the duties of said
   office, file a designation in the city clerk's office, in writing, appointing a deputy
   mayor in accordance with the provisions of this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A›Chapter 73. Officers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 30359. Controller's reports; appeal; bond
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A › Chapter 73. Officers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 30359. Controller's reports; appeal; bond
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 30359. Controller's reports; appeal; bond (2023)
content:
The city controller of each city of the second class A shall make annual reports,
   to council on the first Monday of April, and oftener if so required by council, of
   the audits which he shall have made of the accounts of the officers having charge,
   custody, control and disbursements of public moneys, showing the balance in their
   hands respectively at the end of the fiscal year, and at the same time shall file
   a copy of the annual report with the prothonotary of the court of common pleas.  It shall be lawful for the city or any taxpayer thereof on its behalf or any officer
   whose account is settled or audited, to appeal from the settlement or audit to the
   court of common pleas of the county within forty-five days after the annual report
   to council has been filed in the court of common pleas.  If the appellant is a taxpayer or any officer charged as aforesaid, he shall file
   a bond, with one or more sufficient sureties, conditioned to pay all costs thereafter
   accruing in case a decision shall not be obtained more favorable to the party on whose
   behalf the appeal shall be taken than that contained in the report.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A›Chapter 73. Officers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 30353. Deputy mayor, revocation of appointment of
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A › Chapter 73. Officers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 30353. Deputy mayor, revocation of appointment of
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 30353. Deputy mayor, revocation of appointment of (2023)
content:
The mayor shall have the power to revoke any designation so made, at any time, without
   giving reasons therefor, by filing said revocation, in writing, with the city clerk.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A›Chapter 74. Employees›Article I. Civil Service›PA ST 53 P.S. § 30451. Dismissal of employees; inquiry or trial; suspension pending trial
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IV. Cities of the Second Class A › Chapter 74. Employees › Article I. Civil Service › PA ST 53 P.S. § 30451. Dismissal of employees; inquiry or trial; suspension pending trial
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 30451. Dismissal of employees; inquiry or trial; suspension pending trial (2023)
content:
No regularly appointed employee in either the competitive or noncompetitive class
   of the classified civil service of any city of the second class A in this Commonwealth
   shall be removed, discharged or dismissed without his written consent, except after
   a decision to that effect, rendered against him by a tribunal of trial or inquiry
