content: The township treasurer shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article IX. Township Secretary›PA ST 53 P.S. § 55901.1. Assistant secretary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article IX. Township Secretary › PA ST 53 P.S. § 55901.1. Assistant secretary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 55901.1. Assistant secretary (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may, by resolution, appoint an assistant secretary.  The assistant secretary shall assist the secretary in the performance of the secretary's
   duties and, in the absence or disability of the secretary, perform the duties and
   exercise the powers of the secretary.  The compensation of an assistant secretary shall be determined by the board of commissioners,
   and the assistant secretary shall be required to give bond in an amount as required
   by the board of commissioners.  The assistant secretary may be appointed from the membership of the board of commissioners
   but shall not be any other officer of the board.  If a member of the board of commissioners is appointed as the assistant secretary,
   the appointed member shall not receive compensation for the services and shall be
   bonded.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article VIII-A. Appointed Township Treasurer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 55805-A. Use of special funds; penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article VIII-A. Appointed Township Treasurer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 55805-A. Use of special funds; penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 55805-A. Use of special funds; penalty (2023)
content:
When money is collected for a special purpose, a township treasurer or township commissioner
   may not apply that money to any purpose other than that for which it was collected.  Every misapplication shall be a misdemeanor of the third degree, and, in addition
   to the fine or penalty which may be imposed upon conviction, the defendant shall be
   required to pay restitution in the amount of money improperly spent.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article X. Auditors›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56001. Meetings; general duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article X. Auditors › (a) Elected Auditors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56001. Meetings; general duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56001. Meetings; general duties (2023)
content:
(a) The township auditors shall meet annually, on the day following the day which
      is fixed by this act for the organization of the township commissioners.  The auditors shall organize by the election of a chair and secretary.  Two auditors shall constitute a quorum.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article VIII-A. Appointed Township Treasurer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 55804-A. Penalty for failure to perform duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article VIII-A. Appointed Township Treasurer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 55804-A. Penalty for failure to perform duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 55804-A. Penalty for failure to perform duties (2023)
content:
A township treasurer or deputy treasurer who fails to perform any duties of the office
   other than those for which specific penalties are provided commits a summary offense
   and, in addition to the fine or penalty which may be imposed upon conviction, is required
   to pay to the township an amount equal to the amount of the financial loss that occurred,
   if any, for not performing the duties of the office.  That person is disqualified from holding the office of township treasurer or deputy
   treasurer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article VIII-B. Tax Collector›PA ST 53 P.S. § 55801-B. Powers and duties of tax collector
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article VIII-B. Tax Collector › PA ST 53 P.S. § 55801-B. Powers and duties of tax collector
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 55801-B. Powers and duties of tax collector (2023)
content:
(a) Collection of taxes required.--The township tax collector shall collect all county, institution district, township,
      school and other taxes levied within the townships by authorities authorized to levy
      taxes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article IX. Township Secretary›PA ST 53 P.S. § 55901. Appointment of secretary and salary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article IX. Township Secretary › PA ST 53 P.S. § 55901. Appointment of secretary and salary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 55901. Appointment of secretary and salary (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners shall appoint a secretary to serve at the pleasure of the
   board and who shall not be a member of the board.  The secretary shall act as secretary of the board.  The secretary's salary shall be fixed by ordinance or resolution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article X. Auditors›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56002. Subpoenas, oaths and perjury

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56002. Subpoenas, oaths and perjury (2023)
content: (a) The auditors of each township may:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article X. Auditors›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56001.1. Compensation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article X. Auditors › (a) Elected Auditors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56001.1. Compensation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56001.1. Compensation (2023)
content:
(a) Subject to the limitations set forth in subsection (b), each auditor shall receive
      twenty dollars ($20) per diem, to be paid by the township, for each day necessarily
      employed in the discharge of the auditor's duties.  A day shall consist of not less than five hours in the aggregate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article IX. Township Secretary›PA ST 53 P.S. § 55903. Records open to inspection
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article IX. Township Secretary › PA ST 53 P.S. § 55903. Records open to inspection
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 55903. Records open to inspection (2023)
content:
The minutes and other records and documents of every township shall be open in accordance
   with the act of February 14, 2008 (P.L. 6, No. 3),1known as the Right-to-Know Law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article X. Auditors›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56006. Attorney to auditors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article X. Auditors › (a) Elected Auditors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56006. Attorney to auditors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56006. Attorney to auditors (2023)
content:
(a) The auditors may employ an attorney if a disagreement occurs between the auditors
      and any official or board of officials whose accounts the auditors are required to
      audit.  The attorney shall not be employed until reasonable effort to reach an agreement
      has been made, and only after notice of the auditors' intention to hire the attorney
      has been given to the official or board of officials.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article IX. Township Secretary›PA ST 53 P.S. § 55902. Duties and penalty

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 55902. Duties and penalty (2023)
content: (a) The secretary of a township shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article VIII-A. Appointed Township Treasurer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 55801-A. Township treasurer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article VIII-A. Appointed Township Treasurer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 55801-A. Township treasurer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 55801-A. Township treasurer (2023)
content:
(a) Appointment.--The board of commissioners shall appoint a township treasurer, who may be the elected
      tax collector or an employee of the township, to serve at the pleasure of the board
      of commissioners.  The township treasurer shall not be a member of the board of commissioners.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article X. Auditors›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56005. Penalty for failure to perform duty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article X. Auditors › (a) Elected Auditors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56005. Penalty for failure to perform duty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56005. Penalty for failure to perform duty (2023)
content:
Any auditor who fails to comply with the provisions of this subdivision commits a
   summary offense.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article X. Auditors›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56006.1. Surcharge by auditors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article X. Auditors › (a) Elected Auditors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56006.1. Surcharge by auditors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56006.1. Surcharge by auditors (2023)
content:
(a) The amount of a balance or shortage or of an expenditure of a kind or made in
      a manner prohibited or not authorized by statute that causes a financial loss to the
      township shall be a surcharge against an officer or person responsible for the balance
      or shortage, or who by vote, act or neglect has permitted or approved the expenditure.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article X. Auditors›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56012. Procedure on appeals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article X. Auditors › (a) Elected Auditors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56012. Procedure on appeals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56012. Procedure on appeals (2023)
content:
(a) In any proceeding upon an appeal from a report of the auditors, the accounts of
      the officer or the person in question may be investigated de novo, and the burden
      shall be upon each officer or person whose accounts are involved in the appeal of
      establishing the right to credits claimed by the officer or person, but the opposing
      party in the appeal may use any facts, figures or findings of the report of the auditors
      as prima facie evidence against any officer or person.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article X. Auditors›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56004. Canceling orders
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article X. Auditors › (a) Elected Auditors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56004. Canceling orders
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56004. Canceling orders (2023)
content:
The auditors shall cancel all orders and vouchers that the auditors find have been
   paid by writing the word “audited” on the face of the orders or vouchers.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article X. Auditors›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56003. Completion, filing and publication of auditor's report and financial statement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article X. Auditors › (a) Elected Auditors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56003. Completion, filing and publication of auditor's report and financial statement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56003. Completion, filing and publication of auditor's report and financial statement (2023)
content:
(a) The auditors shall complete the annual audit, settlement, and adjustment as soon
      as possible after the end of the fiscal year.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article X. Auditors›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56009. Appeals from report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article X. Auditors › (a) Elected Auditors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56009. Appeals from report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56009. Appeals from report (2023)
content:
The township, or any registered elector or taxpayer of the township on its behalf,
   or any officer or person whose account is settled or audited by the township auditors,
   may appeal from the settlement or audit to the court of common pleas within forty-five
   days from the date of the filing of the auditors' report with the clerk of the court
   of common pleas.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article X. Auditors›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56007. Balances due to be entered as judgments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article X. Auditors › (a) Elected Auditors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56007. Balances due to be entered as judgments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56007. Balances due to be entered as judgments (2023)
content:
Any balance, in any report of the auditors, against any officer of the township shall
   constitute a surcharge against such officer as fully as if expressly stated in the
   report to be a surcharge.  The amount of a balance and of any express surcharge shall, if no appeal is taken
   or after an appeal has been finally determined in favor of the township, be entered
   by the prothonotary as a judgment against the officer.  The clerk of the court of common pleas shall certify the amount of every balance
   or surcharge contained in a report from which no appeal has been taken within the
   time provided under this subarticle to the court of common pleas for entry by the
   prothonotary as a judgment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article X. Auditors›(b) Appointed Independent Auditor›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56050. Appointment of independent auditor

content:

   lieu of elected auditors under section 503(a)(3),1the board of commissioners shall appoint an independent auditor by resolution and
   the provisions of this subarticle shall apply.  The independent auditor shall be a certified public accountant or a firm of certified
   public accountants.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article X. Auditors›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56016. Findings of facts and law, judgment and appeals

content:

   accordingly, and the judgment entered may be enforced by the prevailing party by any

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article X. Auditors›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56017. Cost
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article X. Auditors › (a) Elected Auditors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56017. Cost
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56017. Cost (2023)
content:
In all cases of appeal from the report or audit of the township auditors to the court
   of common pleas, the costs shall be determined by the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article X. Auditors›(b) Appointed Independent Auditor›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56051. Audits
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article X. Auditors › (b) Appointed Independent Auditor › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56051. Audits
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56051. Audits (2023)
content:
(a) Annual audit.--The independent auditor shall conduct an annual audit of the finances of the township,
      as presented in the annual audit and financial report, which shall include each account
      in which the township is concerned and the accounts of township officers, departments
      and offices which collect, receive and disburse public money or are authorized with
      the management, control or custody of public money on which the independent auditor
      is required to report under this subarticle.  Nothing under this subarticle shall prohibit the board of commissioners from requiring
      the independent auditor to conduct a more complete or comprehensive audit than is
      required under this subarticle.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56001.1. Compensation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › (a) Elected Auditors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56001.1. Compensation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56001.1. Compensation (2023)
content:
(a) Subject to the limitations set forth in subsection (b), each auditor shall receive
      twenty dollars ($20) per diem, to be paid by the township, for each day necessarily
      employed in the discharge of the auditor's duties.  A day shall consist of not less than five hours in the aggregate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article X. Auditors›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56010. Appeal bond
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article X. Auditors › (a) Elected Auditors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56010. Appeal bond
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56010. Appeal bond (2023)
content:
No appeal by a registered elector or taxpayer or officer shall be allowed unless the
   appellant secures a bond with sufficient surety to prosecute the appeal and to pay
   all costs of appeal in case, if the appellant is a registered elector or taxpayer,
   the appellant fails to obtain a final decision more favorable to the township than
   that awarded by the auditors, or in case the appellant is an accounting officer, the
   appellant fails to obtain a final decision more favorable to the officer than that
   awarded by the auditors.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56001. Meetings; general duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › (a) Elected Auditors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56001. Meetings; general duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56001. Meetings; general duties (2023)
content:
(a) The township auditors shall meet annually, on the day following the day which
      is fixed by this act for the organization of the township commissioners.  The auditors shall organize by the election of a chair and secretary.  Two auditors shall constitute a quorum.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56052. Completion, filing and publication of annual audit and financial report (2023)
content:
(a) Completion.--The independent auditor shall complete the annual audit as soon as practical after
      the end of the fiscal year as directed by the board of commissioners.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56006.1. Surcharge by auditors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › (a) Elected Auditors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56006.1. Surcharge by auditors

content:
(a) The amount of a balance or shortage or of an expenditure of a kind or made in
      a manner prohibited or not authorized by statute that causes a financial loss to the
      township shall be a surcharge against an officer or person responsible for the balance
      or shortage, or who by vote, act or neglect has permitted or approved the expenditure.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56004. Canceling orders

content:
The auditors shall cancel all orders and vouchers that the auditors find have been
   paid by writing the word “audited” on the face of the orders or vouchers.

content:
(a) The auditors shall complete the annual audit, settlement, and adjustment as soon
      as possible after the end of the fiscal year.

   summary offense.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › (a) Elected Auditors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56007. Balances due to be entered as judgments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56007. Balances due to be entered as judgments (2023)
content:
Any balance, in any report of the auditors, against any officer of the township shall
   constitute a surcharge against such officer as fully as if expressly stated in the
   report to be a surcharge.  The amount of a balance and of any express surcharge shall, if no appeal is taken
   or after an appeal has been finally determined in favor of the township, be entered
   by the prothonotary as a judgment against the officer.  The clerk of the court of common pleas shall certify the amount of every balance
   or surcharge contained in a report from which no appeal has been taken within the
   time provided under this subarticle to the court of common pleas for entry by the
   prothonotary as a judgment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article X. Auditors›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56008. Collection of surcharges
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article X. Auditors › (a) Elected Auditors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56008. Collection of surcharges
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56008. Collection of surcharges (2023)
content:
Any auditor, registered elector or taxpayer of the township may enforce the collection
   of a judgment entered for a surcharge for the benefit of the township, by any appropriate
   action or execution, upon filing in the court of common pleas a bond, with one or
   more sureties (in the case of a registered elector or taxpayer), conditioned to indemnify
   the township from all costs of the proceedings undertaken by the registered elector
   or taxpayer, subject, however, to all rights of appeal from the report of the auditors
   granted by this subarticle.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56006. Attorney to auditors

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56006. Attorney to auditors (2023)
content:
(a) The auditors may employ an attorney if a disagreement occurs between the auditors
      and any official or board of officials whose accounts the auditors are required to
      audit.  The attorney shall not be employed until reasonable effort to reach an agreement
      has been made, and only after notice of the auditors' intention to hire the attorney
      has been given to the official or board of officials.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›(a) Elected Auditors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56012. Procedure on appeals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › (a) Elected Auditors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56012. Procedure on appeals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56012. Procedure on appeals (2023)
content:
(a) In any proceeding upon an appeal from a report of the auditors, the accounts of
      the officer or the person in question may be investigated de novo, and the burden
      shall be upon each officer or person whose accounts are involved in the appeal of
      establishing the right to credits claimed by the officer or person, but the opposing
      party in the appeal may use any facts, figures or findings of the report of the auditors
      as prima facie evidence against any officer or person.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56009. Appeals from report (2023)
content:
The township, or any registered elector or taxpayer of the township on its behalf,
   or any officer or person whose account is settled or audited by the township auditors,
   may appeal from the settlement or audit to the court of common pleas within forty-five
   days from the date of the filing of the auditors' report with the clerk of the court
   of common pleas.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XI. Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56103. General powers and duties of controller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XI. Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56103. General powers and duties of controller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56103. General powers and duties of controller (2023)
content:
(a) The township controller shall manage the fiscal affairs of the township. The controller shall examine, audit, and settle all accounts in which the township
      is concerned, either as debtor or creditor, if provisions for the settlement are made
      by law.  If no provisions, or an insufficient provision, has been made, the controller shall
      examine the accounts and report to the board of commissioners the relevant facts and
      opinions on the accounts.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XI. Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56102. Salary of controller

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56102. Salary of controller (2023)
content:
The annual salary of the controller shall be fixed by ordinance, passed at least thirty
   days before the controller's election.  Any change in salary, compensation or emoluments of the elected office shall become
   effective at the beginning of the next term of the controller.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XI. Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56104. Countersigned warrants
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XI. Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56104. Countersigned warrants
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56104. Countersigned warrants (2023)
content:
The township controller shall countersign all warrants upon the township treasurer,
   with the form of the warrant to be prescribed by the board of commissioners, but no
   warrant shall be countersigned unless there is sufficient unencumbered money in the

   the person presenting the warrant shall, if the controller requires, produce evidence

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XI. Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56110. Controller to retain financial records, pending appeals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XI. Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56110. Controller to retain financial records, pending appeals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56110. Controller to retain financial records, pending appeals (2023)
content:
Every township controller shall retain possession, during the forty-five days’ period
   elapsing between the date of filing the report and the expiration of the time for
   filing the appeal from the report, all financial records and other papers that were
   submitted to the controller for audit of the accounts of township officers.  If an appeal is taken, the controller shall continue to hold the financial records
   and papers for production in the proceeding to determine the appeal.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XI. Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56107. Management and improvement of township finances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XI. Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56107. Management and improvement of township finances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56107. Management and improvement of township finances (2023)
content:
The township controller shall, as often as the controller may deem expedient or the
   board of commissioners shall direct, suggest plans to the board of commissioners for
   the management and improvement of the township finances.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XI. Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56109. Appeals from controller’s report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XI. Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56109. Appeals from controller’s report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56109. Appeals from controller’s report (2023)
content:
Appeals may be taken from the settlement and audit of the controller as shown in the
   controller's report to the court of common pleas of the county, by the same persons,
   in the same manner, within the same time, subject to the same conditions and procedure,
   and with like effect in every respect as provided in this act in the cases of appeals
   from the settlement and audit of the auditors as shown in their report.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XI. Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56108. Financial records to be kept by controller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XI. Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56108. Financial records to be kept by controller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56108. Financial records to be kept by controller (2023)
content:
The township controller shall maintain financial records and maintain as many accounts,
   under appropriate titles, as may be necessary to show separately and distinctly all
   the estates and property, real and personal, vested in the township, all trusts in
   the care of the township, all debts due and owing the township, all receipts and expenditures
   of the various departments of the township government, and all appropriations made
   by the board of commissioners and the sums under the same, respectively.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XI. Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56106. Amount of contracts to be charged against appropriations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XI. Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56106. Amount of contracts to be charged against appropriations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56106. Amount of contracts to be charged against appropriations (2023)
content:
(a) Every contract involving appropriation of money shall designate the item of appropriation
      on which it is founded, and the estimated amount of the expenditure which shall be
      charged against the item and certified by the township controller on the contract,
      before it shall take effect as a contract.  Payment required by the contract shall be made from the fund for which the contract
      is appropriated.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XII. Township Solicitor›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56201. Township solicitor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XII. Township Solicitor › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56201. Township solicitor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56201. Township solicitor (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may appoint and determine the compensation of a township
   solicitor and, as needed, special counsel.  The township solicitor or special counsel must be licensed to practice law in this
   Commonwealth and may be an individual or a law firm, partnership, association or professional
   corporation.  The township solicitor or special counsel shall serve at the pleasure of the board
   of commissioners.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XI. Controller›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56105. Prevention of appropriation overdrafts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XI. Controller › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56105. Prevention of appropriation overdrafts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56105. Prevention of appropriation overdrafts (2023)
content:
The township controller shall not permit any appropriation made by the board of commissioners
   to be overdrawn.  If an appropriation is exhausted, the object of which is not complete, the commissioner
   shall immediately report the fact to the board of commissioners, and accompany the
   report with a statement of the money which has been drawn on the appropriation and
   the particular purpose for which it was drawn.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56204. Duties of solicitor (2023)
content: The township solicitor or special counsel, as applicable, shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIII. Township Engineer›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56306. Surveys
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIII. Township Engineer › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56306. Surveys
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56306. Surveys (2023)
content:
The township engineer shall have the charge and direction of all surveys and regulations
   authorized by any act of Assembly or ordinance of the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56301. Township engineer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56301. Township engineer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56301. Township engineer (2023)
content:
(a) The board of commissioners may appoint and determine the compensation of a township
      engineer who must be a registered professional engineer.  The township engineer serves at the pleasure of the board of commissioners.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIII. Township Engineer›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56303. Control of engineering matters
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIII. Township Engineer › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56303. Control of engineering matters
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56303. Control of engineering matters (2023)
content:
(a) Except where the board of commissioners has appointed an engineer for a specific
      matter, the township engineer shall direct and control the engineering matters of
      the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIII. Township Engineer›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56305. Certificate of commencement and of completion of municipal improvements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIII. Township Engineer › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56305. Certificate of commencement and of completion of municipal improvements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56305. Certificate of commencement and of completion of municipal improvements (2023)
content:
(a) The township engineer shall certify to the township secretary the date of commencement
      and date of completion of all municipal improvements, the cost of which, in whole
      or in part, is to be paid by the owners of the abutting property.  The certification shall be made a part of the permanent records of the township.  The certified date of commencement and certified date of completion shall be conclusive
      on all parties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIII. Township Engineer›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56304. Duties; preparation of plans
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIII. Township Engineer › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56304. Duties; preparation of plans
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56304. Duties; preparation of plans (2023)
content:
The township engineer shall perform duties and provide reports as the board of commissioners
   may direct for the construction, reconstruction, maintenance and repair of streets,
   bridges, culverts and other engineering work.  The township engineer may prepare plans, specifications and estimates of the work
   undertaken by the township and shall furnish the board of commissioners and the committees
   of the township with reports, information or estimates on any township engineering
   work or on questions submitted by the board of commissioners.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56303. Control of engineering matters

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIII-A. Township Manager›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56301-A. Township manager
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIII-A. Township Manager › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56301-A. Township manager
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56301-A. Township manager (2023)
content:
(a) Authorization.--The board of commissioners may create by ordinance the office of township manager
      and, in like manner, abolish the office.  While the office exists, the board of commissioners may appoint one individual,
      a partnership, a limited partnership, an association or a professional corporation
      as the township manager.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XII. Township Solicitor›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56203. Control of legal matters

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56203. Control of legal matters (2023)
content:
(a) Except where the board of commissioners has appointed special counsel for a specific
      matter, the township solicitor shall advise on the legal matters of the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIII-A. Township Manager›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56302-A. Powers and duties; agreement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIII-A. Township Manager › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56302-A. Powers and duties; agreement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56302-A. Powers and duties; agreement (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The powers and duties of the township manager shall be regulated by ordinance.  The board of commissioners may delegate, subject to recall, any of their nonlegislative
      and nonjudicial powers and duties to the township manager.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIII-A. Township Manager›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56304-A. Incompatibility
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIII-A. Township Manager › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56304-A. Incompatibility
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56304-A. Incompatibility (2023)
content: (a) General rule.--No township manager may be eligible to hold the office of township commissioner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIII-B. Veterans’ Affairs›(a) Pennsylvania National Guard›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56301-B. Eminent domain for National Guard purposes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIII-B. Veterans’ Affairs › (a) Pennsylvania National Guard › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56301-B. Eminent domain for National Guard purposes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56301-B. Eminent domain for National Guard purposes (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as provided in subsection (b), the board of commissioners may take, by the
      right of eminent domain for the purpose of appropriating to the township for the use
      of the Pennsylvania National Guard, public lands, easements and public property in
      the township's possession or control and used or held by the township for any other
      purpose notwithstanding any limitation of the use by the township whether by donation,
      dedication, appropriation, statute or otherwise.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIII-A. Township Manager›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56303-A. Bond
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIII-A. Township Manager › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56303-A. Bond
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56303-A. Bond (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The township manager shall, if required by the board of commissioners, give a bond
      to the township, with a surety company or other company authorized by law to act as
      surety, to be approved by the board of commissioners, in such sum as the board of
      commissioners, by ordinance or resolution, directs, conditioned for the faithful performance
      of the township manager's duties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIII-B. Veterans’ Affairs›(a) Pennsylvania National Guard›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56302-B. Land for armory purposes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIII-B. Veterans’ Affairs › (a) Pennsylvania National Guard › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56302-B. Land for armory purposes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56302-B. Land for armory purposes (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as provided in subsection (b), the board of commissioners may acquire, by purchase,
      gift or eminent domain, land for the use of the Pennsylvania National Guard, to be
      conveyed to the Commonwealth in order to assist the State Armory Board in the erection
      of armories.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIII-B. Veterans’ Affairs›(b) Support of Veterans’ Organizations and Memorials›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56311-B. Appropriations to Veterans’ Home Associations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIII-B. Veterans’ Affairs › (b) Support of Veterans’ Organizations and Memorials › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56311-B. Appropriations to Veterans’ Home Associations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56311-B. Appropriations to Veterans’ Home Associations (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may make an annual appropriation not to exceed $300 for
   the support of any Veterans’ Home Association that provides a home or meeting facility
   within the township for the use of United States war veterans, and which is not maintained
   in whole or in part by the United States or any governmental agency other than the
   township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIII-B. Veterans’ Affairs›(a) Pennsylvania National Guard›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56304-B. Support of Pennsylvania National Guard units
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIII-B. Veterans’ Affairs › (a) Pennsylvania National Guard › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56304-B. Support of Pennsylvania National Guard units
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56304-B. Support of Pennsylvania National Guard units (2023)
content:
(a) Annual appropriation.--The board of commissioners may appropriate annually a sum not to exceed $1,500 for
      the support, maintenance, discipline and training of a unit of the Pennsylvania National
      Guard.  If the units are organized as a battalion, regiment or similar organization, the
      total amount due may be paid to the commanding officer of the battalion, regiment
      or similar organization.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIII-B. Veterans’ Affairs›(a) Pennsylvania National Guard›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56303-B. Assistance to armories

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56312-B. Memorial Day or Veterans’ Day appropriations (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may appropriate money for the expenses of services for
   Memorial Day, Veterans’ Day or a similar day provided for by Federal or State law.

content:
The board of commissioners may appropriate money and purchase plots of ground in a
   cemetery or burial ground for the interment of deceased service persons:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIII-B. Veterans’ Affairs›(b) Support of Veterans’ Organizations and Memorials›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56313-B. Care of memorials
