citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56313-B. Care of memorials (2023)
content:
(a) Maintenance and repair.--The board of commissioners may maintain and keep in good order and repair, at the
      expense of the township, a soldiers’ monument, gun or carriage or similar memorial
      if the memorial is not in the charge or care of an individual, body or organization
      and the memorial was not erected by the Federal Government, the Commonwealth or the
      commissioners of the county or by the direction or authority of any other state.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIV. Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56401. Appointment, compensation and training of police officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIV. Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56401. Appointment, compensation and training of police officers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56401. Appointment, compensation and training of police officers (2023)
content:
(a) The board of commissioners may, subject to the civil service provisions of this
      act, appoint and fix the number, rank and compensation of the members of the township
      police force.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›(a) Pennsylvania National Guard›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56302-B. Land for armory purposes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › (a) Pennsylvania National Guard › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56302-B. Land for armory purposes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56302-B. Land for armory purposes (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as provided in subsection (b), the board of commissioners may acquire, by purchase,
      gift or eminent domain, land for the use of the Pennsylvania National Guard, to be
      conveyed to the Commonwealth in order to assist the State Armory Board in the erection
      of armories.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›(b) Support of Veterans’ Organizations and Memorials›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56313-B. Care of memorials
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › (b) Support of Veterans’ Organizations and Memorials › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56313-B. Care of memorials
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56313-B. Care of memorials (2023)
content:
(a) Maintenance and repair.--The board of commissioners may maintain and keep in good order and repair, at the
      expense of the township, a soldiers’ monument, gun or carriage or similar memorial
      if the memorial is not in the charge or care of an individual, body or organization
      and the memorial was not erected by the Federal Government, the Commonwealth or the
      commissioners of the county or by the direction or authority of any other state.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›(b) Support of Veterans’ Organizations and Memorials›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56311-B. Appropriations to Veterans’ Home Associations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › (b) Support of Veterans’ Organizations and Memorials › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56311-B. Appropriations to Veterans’ Home Associations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56311-B. Appropriations to Veterans’ Home Associations (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may make an annual appropriation not to exceed $300 for
   the support of any Veterans’ Home Association that provides a home or meeting facility
   within the township for the use of United States war veterans, and which is not maintained
   in whole or in part by the United States or any governmental agency other than the
   township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›(a) Pennsylvania National Guard›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56301-B. Eminent domain for National Guard purposes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › (a) Pennsylvania National Guard › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56301-B. Eminent domain for National Guard purposes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56301-B. Eminent domain for National Guard purposes (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as provided in subsection (b), the board of commissioners may take, by the
      right of eminent domain for the purpose of appropriating to the township for the use
      of the Pennsylvania National Guard, public lands, easements and public property in
      the township's possession or control and used or held by the township for any other
      purpose notwithstanding any limitation of the use by the township whether by donation,
      dedication, appropriation, statute or otherwise.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›(b) Support of Veterans’ Organizations and Memorials›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56312-B. Memorial Day or Veterans’ Day appropriations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › (b) Support of Veterans’ Organizations and Memorials › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56312-B. Memorial Day or Veterans’ Day appropriations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56312-B. Memorial Day or Veterans’ Day appropriations (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may appropriate money for the expenses of services for
   Memorial Day, Veterans’ Day or a similar day provided for by Federal or State law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›(a) Pennsylvania National Guard›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56304-B. Support of Pennsylvania National Guard units
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › (a) Pennsylvania National Guard › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56304-B. Support of Pennsylvania National Guard units
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56304-B. Support of Pennsylvania National Guard units (2023)
content:
(a) Annual appropriation.--The board of commissioners may appropriate annually a sum not to exceed $1,500 for
      the support, maintenance, discipline and training of a unit of the Pennsylvania National
      Guard.  If the units are organized as a battalion, regiment or similar organization, the
      total amount due may be paid to the commanding officer of the battalion, regiment
      or similar organization.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›(a) Pennsylvania National Guard›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56303-B. Assistance to armories
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › (a) Pennsylvania National Guard › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56303-B. Assistance to armories
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56303-B. Assistance to armories (2023)
content:
(a) Appropriation or conveyance.--The board of commissioners may appropriate money or convey land, either independently
      or in conjunction with any other municipality, to the Commonwealth for the following
      purposes:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›(b) Support of Veterans’ Organizations and Memorials›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56314-B. Purchase of burial grounds for deceased service persons
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › (b) Support of Veterans’ Organizations and Memorials › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56314-B. Purchase of burial grounds for deceased service persons
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56314-B. Purchase of burial grounds for deceased service persons (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may appropriate money and purchase plots of ground in a
   cemetery or burial ground for the interment of deceased service persons:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIV. Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56403. Powers of police officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIV. Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56403. Powers of police officers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56403. Powers of police officers (2023)
content:
A township police officer shall have those powers and duties as are granted to police
   officers under the laws of this Commonwealth, the rules of the Supreme Court or the
   ordinances of the township, for the violation of which a fine or penalty may be imposed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIV. Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56401.1. Special fire police
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIV. Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56401.1. Special fire police
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56401.1. Special fire police (2023)
content:
The president of the board of commissioners may confirm any member of a volunteer
   fire company nominated to serve as special fire police under 35 Pa.C.S. Ch. 74 Subch.
   D1(relating to special fire police).  The president of the board of commissioners may swear in or affirm special fire
   police officers.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIV. Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56405. Supervision of police
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIV. Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56405. Supervision of police
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56405. Supervision of police (2023)
content:
The chief of police and police officers shall obey the orders of the board of commissioners
   or any other person or committee as designated by ordinance or resolution of the board
   for that purpose.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIV. Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56404. Service of process; fees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIV. Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56404. Service of process; fees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56404. Service of process; fees (2023)
content:
Police officers may serve and execute criminal process or processes issued for the
   violation of township ordinances and shall charge the same fees and costs as pertain
   by law to constables of the township for similar services, but the fees and costs
   shall be paid to the township treasurer for the use of the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIV. Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56402. Chief of police and other officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIV. Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56402. Chief of police and other officers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56402. Chief of police and other officers (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may designate the superintendent or the chief of police
   and other officers who shall serve until their successors are duly designated and
   qualified.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIV. Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56407. Badge
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIV. Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56407. Badge
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56407. Badge (2023)
content:
Township police officers, when on duty, shall wear a badge or shield with the words
   “Township Police” and the name of the township inscribed on the badge or shield.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501.4. Surcharge from sale or lease
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501.4. Surcharge from sale or lease
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501.4. Surcharge from sale or lease (2023)
content:
A commissioner who votes in favor of or knowingly participates in the sale or lease
   of township real or personal property in violation of this article is subject to a
   surcharge to the extent of any loss or injury to the township as a result of the sale
   or lease.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIV. Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56409.1. Private police pension funds; optional transfers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIV. Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56409.1. Private police pension funds; optional transfers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56409.1. Private police pension funds; optional transfers (2023)
content:
(a) If there is a private organization or association constituting and managing an
      existing pension fund for the members of the police force in any township, the  township
      shall establish a police pension fund for the purpose of paying pensions to the members
      of the police force if the membership of the organization or association, by a two-thirds
      vote, elects to transfer its funds with all its assets and liabilities into a township
      police pension fund as required to be established by this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIV. Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56409. Police pension fund
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIV. Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56409. Police pension fund
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56409. Police pension fund (2023)
content:
(a) If a police force of less than three full-time members is maintained, the township
      shall, unless there is a private organization or association constituting and managing
      an existing pension fund for the members of the police force in the township, by ordinance,
      establish a police pension fund to be maintained by member contributions of an equal
      percentage charge against each member of the police force.  The member contributions, except to the extent that subsection (c) of section 607
      of the act of December 18, 1984 (P.L. 1005, No. 205),1known as the “Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act,” applies,
      shall not exceed annually four percent of the pay of the member.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501.1. Real property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501.1. Real property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501.1. Real property (2023)
content:
(a) No real estate owned by the township may be sold for a consideration in excess
      of six thousand dollars except to the highest bidder after due notice by advertisement
      for bids or advertisement of a public auction.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIV. Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56408. Compensation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIV. Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56408. Compensation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56408. Compensation (2023)
content:
(a) A township that employs police officers shall pay to all the police officers a
      fixed or stipulated salary.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501. Suits; property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501. Suits; property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501. Suits; property (2023)
content: Townships of the first class may:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XIV. Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56416. School crossing guards
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XIV. Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56416. School crossing guards
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56416. School crossing guards (2023)
content:
(a)(1) The board of commissioners, by resolution, may appoint school crossing guards
         who shall be authorized only to manage traffic and pedestrians at or near schools
         while the school crossing guards are in uniform.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.1. Officers, positions and departments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.1. Officers, positions and departments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.1. Officers, positions and departments (2023)
content:
(a) The board of commissioners may create any office, position or department which
      the board may deem necessary for the good of government and interests of the township
      and may fix the compensation of appointed individuals.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501.5. General powers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501.5. General powers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501.5. General powers (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may make and adopt any ordinances, bylaws, rules and regulations
   not inconsistent with or restrained by the Constitution and laws of this Commonwealth
   as may be expedient or necessary for the proper management, care and control of the
   township and its finances, and the maintenance of peace, good government and welfare
   of the township and its trade, commerce and manufactures.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.2. Police force
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.2. Police force
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.2. Police force (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may establish, equip, maintain and define the duties of
   a police force.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.3. Lockup facilities
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.3. Lockup facilities
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.3. Lockup facilities (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may provide for lockup facilities in the township for the
   temporary detention and confinement of individuals.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.4. Rewards
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.4. Rewards
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.4. Rewards (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may offer rewards for information leading to the arrest
   and conviction of an individual guilty of a crime within the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.5. Disorderly conduct
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.5. Disorderly conduct
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.5. Disorderly conduct (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may, by ordinance, prohibit disorderly conduct within the
   limits of the township and provide for the imposition of penalties for the conduct
   in accordance with this act.  If an ordinance is enacted, it shall define disorderly conduct in a manner substantially
   similar to the provisions of18 Pa.C.S. § 5503(relating to disorderly conduct).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56502. Specific powers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56502. Specific powers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56502. Specific powers (2023)
content:
The corporate power of a township of the first class shall be vested in a board of
   commissioners.  In the exercise of any specific powers involving the enactment of an ordinance,
   passage of a resolution or the making of any regulation, restriction or prohibition,
   the township may provide for enforcement and penalties for violations.  The specific powers of the township shall include the powers provided under this
   article.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501.2. Personal property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501.2. Personal property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501.2. Personal property (2023)
content:
(a) Except as provided in subsection (d), no township personal property may be disposed
      of, by sale or otherwise, except upon approval of the board of commissioners.  In cases when the board of commissioners approves a sale of the property, the board
      of commissioners shall estimate the fair market value of the entire lot to be disposed
      of.  If the board of commissioners estimates the fair market value to be two thousand
      dollars or more, the entire lot shall be advertised for sale once, in at least one
      newspaper of general circulation, not less than ten days prior to the date fixed for
      the opening of bids or public auction.  The date of opening of bids or public auction shall be announced in the advertisement,
      and sale of the property advertised shall be made to the highest bidder.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.7. Fire protection
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.7. Fire protection
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.7. Fire protection (2023)
content: The board of commissioners may:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501.3. Exceptions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501.3. Exceptions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501.3. Exceptions (2023)
content:
(a) Nothing under this article requiring advertising for bids or sale at public auction
      and sale to the highest bidder shall apply if township real or personal property is
      to be sold to any of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.11. Nuisances and dangerous structures
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.11. Nuisances and dangerous structures
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.11. Nuisances and dangerous structures (2023)
content:
(a) A board of commissioners may prohibit and remove any nuisance or dangerous structure
      on public or private grounds, including, but not limited to weeds, accumulations of
      municipal waste, the storage of abandoned or junked automobiles and obstructions or
      nuisances in the streets of the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.14. Smoke regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.14. Smoke regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.14. Smoke regulations (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may regulate the emission of smoke from chimneys, smokestacks
   and other sources, except locomotive smokestacks, to the extent that the regulation
   is not otherwise prohibited by applicable Federal or State law.

content:

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.8. Building and housing regulations (2023)
content:
In addition to other remedies provided by law, the board of commissioners may enact
   and enforce suitable ordinances relating to building and housing regulations in accordance
   with Article XXXI-A.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.15. Prohibition of fire producing devices and smoking
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.15. Prohibition of fire producing devices and smoking
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.15. Prohibition of fire producing devices and smoking (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may prohibit and regulate the smoking or carrying of lighted
   cigarettes, cigars, pipes or matches and the use of matches or fire-producing devices.  An ordinance enacted or regulation or resolution adopted under this section shall
   not regulate smoking in a manner that conflicts with the act of June 13, 2008 (P.L.
   182, No. 27),1known as the Clean Indoor Air Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.17. Regulation of foundations, party walls and partition fences

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.17. Regulation of foundations, party walls and partition fences (2023)
content:
(a) Subject to the provisions of and regulations adopted pursuant to the act of November
      10, 1999 (P.L. 491, No. 45),1known as the Pennsylvania Construction Code Act, and other applicable law, the board
      of commissioners may provide regulations for foundations, party walls and partition
      fences.

content:
The board of commissioners may, by ordinance, require and regulate the numbering of
   buildings and lots.

The board of commissioners may take all necessary means to secure the safety of persons
   or property within the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.12. Municipal waste
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.12. Municipal waste
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.12. Municipal waste (2023)
content:
(a) A board of commissioners, in the manner authorized by the act of July 7, 1980
      (P.L. 380, No. 97),1known as the Solid Waste Management Act, and the act of July 28, 1988 (P.L. 556,
      No. 101),2known as the Municipal Waste Planning, Recycling and Waste Reduction Act, may prohibit
      accumulations of municipal waste on public and private property, including the imposition
      and collection of reasonable fees and charges for the collection, removal and disposal
      of the municipal waste.  As used in this act, “municipal waste” shall have the same meaning as given to the
      term in the Municipal Waste Planning, Recycling and Waste Reduction Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.21. Public facilities

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.21. Public facilities (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may acquire property for the purposes of providing, maintaining
   and operating public facilities, such as comfort and waiting stations, drinking fountains
   and watering troughs.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.19. Display of flags (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may display the flag of the United States, the Commonwealth,
   the official POW/MIA flag or the flag of any county or municipal corporation in this
   Commonwealth on any public building or grounds of the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.20. Health and cleanliness regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.20. Health and cleanliness regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.20. Health and cleanliness regulations (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may make regulations as necessary for the health, safety,
   morals, general welfare, cleanliness, beauty, convenience and comfort of the township
   and its inhabitants.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.22. Hospital appropriations (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may, in townships having a population of two thousand inhabitants
   or more, appropriate money for the support of any incorporated hospital that is engaged
   in charitable work and extends treatment and medical attention to the residents of
   the township.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.27. Appropriations for airports (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may appropriate funds to assist a municipality or municipal
   airport authority to acquire, establish, operate and maintain air navigation facilities
   lying either within or without the limits of the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.28. Purchase and planting of trees

   and planting of, shade trees and shrubs along the streets, highways and sidewalks
   of the township and have the care, custody and control of shade trees pursuant to

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.30. Widening and deepening of watercourses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.30. Widening and deepening of watercourses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.30. Widening and deepening of watercourses (2023)
content:
(a) After permits have been secured from all applicable agencies, the board of commissioners
      or an agent or employe of the board may widen and deepen a watercourse running through
      the township and erect dykes, retaining walls and embankments along the watercourse
      as necessary to prevent water from overflowing the watercourse's banks.

content: The board of commissioners may make and regulate charges for the use of township facilities.

content:
The board of commissioners may appropriate money annually for improvements to any
   street, as defined in section 102,1located wholly or partially within the township which has been adversely affected
   by parking availability as determined by the board.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.26. Airports
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.26. Airports (2023)
content:
(a) A township is authorized and empowered to acquire by grant, lease, purchase or
      condemnation proceedings, subject to the limitations in26 Pa.C.S. § 206(relating to extraterritorial takings), any land lying either within or without the
      limits of the township which, in the judgment of the board of commissioners, may be
      necessary and desirable for the purpose of establishing and maintaining a municipal
      airport, landing field, intermediate landing field, aviation easement or other airport
      facility.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.35. Surplus foods

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.35. Surplus foods (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may make an appropriation for the handling, storage and
   distribution of surplus foods obtained through a Federal, State or local agency.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.38. Historical properties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.38. Historical properties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.38. Historical properties (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may appropriate money to nonprofit associations or corporations
   organized for the purpose of acquiring and maintaining historical properties.  The appropriations shall only be used by the association or corporation for the
   acquisition, restoration and maintenance of the historical properties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.41. Open burning

content:
The board of commissioners may regulate open burning, including the prohibition of
   the open burning of combustible material.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.42. Community development

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.42. Community development (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may undertake community development programs, including,
   but not limited to, urban renewal, public housing, model cities programs and neighborhood
   development projects.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.50. Drug and alcohol abuse programs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.50. Drug and alcohol abuse programs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.50. Drug and alcohol abuse programs (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may appropriate annually, out of the general funds of the
   township, a sum to be divided in amounts as the commissioners may determine and to
   be used for education and development of programs within the community dealing with
   drug and alcohol abuse.  The funds may also be contributed to existing programs available to the township's
   residents in adjacent communities or in the county where the township is situate at
   the discretion of the board of commissioners.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.48. Nonprofit art corporations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.48. Nonprofit art corporations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.48. Nonprofit art corporations (2023)
content:
(a) The board of commissioners may appropriate funds annually, of an amount not more
      than equal to one mill of the real estate tax, to any nonprofit art corporation for
      the conduct of the corporation's artistic and cultural activities.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.44. Building hospitals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.44. Building hospitals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.44. Building hospitals (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may appropriate funds toward the purchase, erection, maintenance
   or support of any medical center or hospital building facilities.  Approval by the appropriate health planning agency is required if the total cost
   of the purchase or erection exceeds $100,000.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.39. Insurance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.39. Insurance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.39. Insurance (2023)
content:
(a) The board of commissioners may secure insurance or compensation in accordance
      with Article VI of the act of June 2, 1915 (P.L. 736, No. 338),1known as the Workers' Compensation Act, for:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.40. Appropriations for urban common carrier mass transportation

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.51. Watershed associations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.51. Watershed associations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.51. Watershed associations (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may make appropriations to nonprofit watershed associations
   for watersheds serving the township.  Appropriations may not be used to undertake litigation against any municipality
   or to seek redress against any individual landowner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.49. Neighborhood crime watch programs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.49. Neighborhood crime watch programs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.49. Neighborhood crime watch programs (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may appropriate annually an amount toward a neighborhood
   crime watch program.  Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no township or official of a township
   shall become subject to contractual, tort or other liability as a result of having
   made an appropriation pursuant to this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.43. Observances and celebrations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.43. Observances and celebrations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.43. Observances and celebrations (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may appropriate funds annually for the observance of holidays,
   centennials or other anniversaries or for township celebrations or civic projects
   or programs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.52. Emergency services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.52. Emergency services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.52. Emergency services (2023)
content:
(a) The township shall be responsible for ensuring that fire and emergency medical
      services are provided within the township by the means and to the extent determined
      by the township, including the appropriate financial and administrative assistance
      for these services.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.45. Tourist promotion agencies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.45. Tourist promotion agencies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.45. Tourist promotion agencies (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may appropriate funds annually to any tourist promotion
   agency to assist the agencies in carrying out tourist promotional activities. “Tourist promotion agency” shall have the same meaning given to it under section 2
   of the act of July 4, 2008 (P.L. 621, No. 50),1known as the Tourism Promotion Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.53. Mines and quarries
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.53. Mines and quarries
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.53. Mines and quarries (2023)
content:
(a) The owner, operator or superintendent of each mine, colliery or quarry located
      wholly or partially within the limits of the township shall furnish maps, plans and
      drawings of workings, excavations and surface support to the township as the board
      of commissioners may require, and the following shall apply:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Article I. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 55101. Short title; effective date
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Article I. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 55101. Short title; effective date
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 55101. Short title; effective date (2023)
content:
This act shall be known, and may be cited, as “The First Class Township Code.”  This reenactment, revision, amendment and consolidation of the laws relating to townships
   of the first class shall become effective the first day of January, 1950.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56590. Typewritten, printed, photocopied, microfilmed and electronically or digitally stored records valid and recording or transcribing records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56590. Typewritten, printed, photocopied, microfilmed and electronically or digitally stored records valid and recording or transcribing records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56590. Typewritten, printed, photocopied, microfilmed and electronically or digitally stored records valid and recording or transcribing records (2023)
content:
(a) All township records required to be recorded or transcribed shall be deemed valid
      if typewritten, printed, photocopied, microfilmed or electronically or digitally stored
      or retained by any other process that accurately reproduces the original and forms
      a durable medium for recording, storing and reproducing in accordance with the act
      of May 9, 1949 (P.L. 908, No. 250),1entitled “An act relating to public records of political subdivisions other than
      cities and counties of the first class;  authorizing the recording and copying of
      documents, plats, papers and instruments of writing by digital, photostatic, photographic,
      microfilm or other process, and the admissibility thereof and enlargements thereof
      in evidence;  providing for the storage of duplicates and sale of microfilm and digital
      copies of official records and for the destruction of other records deemed valueless;
      and providing for the services of the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission
      to political subdivisions.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.54. Conservation district
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.54. Conservation district
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.54. Conservation district (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may make appropriations to a conservation district, as
   the term is defined under section 3 of the act of May 15, 1945 (P.L. 547, No. 217),1known as the Conservation District Law, in which the township is located.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.56. Storm water
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.56. Storm water
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.56. Storm water (2023)
content:
A township may, by ordinance, after obtaining any required permit from the Department
   of Environmental Protection or other Federal or State entity, acquire, operate and
   maintain areas for the infiltration, detention or retention of storm water and for
   other methods of storm water management authorized by the Department of Environmental
   Protection.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.55. Electricity
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.55. Electricity
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56579.55. Electricity (2023)
content:
The board of commissioners may manufacture and sell electricity and regulate its use
   and prices pursuant to Article XXVII-A.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Article I. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 55104. Construction of act generally
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Article I. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 55104. Construction of act generally
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 55104. Construction of act generally (2023)
content:
(a) The provisions of this act so far as they are the same as those of laws in effect
      prior to June 24, 1931, are intended as a continuation of laws in effect prior to
      June 24, 1931, and not as new enactments.  The repeal by this act of any act of Assembly, or part thereof, shall not revive
      any act, or part thereof, repealed or superseded prior to June 24, 1931, nor affect
      the existence of class of any township created prior to June 24, 1931.  The provisions of this act shall not affect any act done, liability incurred, or
      right accrued or vested, or affect any suit or prosecution, pending or to be instituted,
      to enforce any right or penalty or punish any offense under the authority of the repealed
      laws.  All ordinances, resolutions, regulations, and rules, made pursuant to any act of
      Assembly repealed by this act, shall continue with the same force and effect as if
      the act had not been repealed.  Any person, holding office under any act of Assembly repealed by this act, shall
      continue to hold office until the expiration of the term thereof, subject to the conditions
      attached to the office prior to June 24, 1931.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Article I. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 55105. Constitutional Construction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Article I. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 55105. Constitutional Construction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 55105. Constitutional Construction (2023)
content:
The provisions of this act shall be severable, and if any of the provisions shall
   be held to be unconstitutional, such decision shall not affect the validity of any
   of the remaining provisions of this act.  It is hereby declared as the legislative intent that this act would have been adopted
   had such unconstitutional provision not been included therein.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Chapter 131. First Class Township Code›Article XV-A. Real Estate Registry›PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501-A. Real estate registry
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Chapter 131. First Class Township Code › Article XV-A. Real Estate Registry › PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501-A. Real estate registry
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 56501-A. Real estate registry (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--For the purpose of procuring accurate information on the ownership of all real estate,
      the board of commissioners may provide, by ordinance, for a real estate registry in
      a manner not inconsistent with the act of October 9, 2008 (P.L. 1400, No. 110),1known as the Uniform Municipal Deed Registration Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Article I. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 55107. How act applies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Article I. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 55107. How act applies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 55107. How act applies (2023)
content:
This act shall apply to all townships of the first class within the Commonwealth existing
   on June 24, 1931, or created thereafter.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Article I. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 55110. Legal advertising
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 55110. Legal advertising (2023)
content:
(a) Whenever, under the provisions of this act, notice is required to be published
      in one or more newspapers, the publication shall be made in a newspaper of general
      circulation, as defined in45 Pa.C.S. § 101(relating to definitions), printed in the township, if there is such a newspaper,
      and, if not, then in a newspaper circulating generally in the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article I. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65104. Construction of act generally
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article I. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65104. Construction of act generally

   accrued or vested or affect any suit or prosecution pending or to be instituted to
   enforce any right or penalty or punish any offense under the authority of any repealed
   laws.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article I. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65105. Constitutional construction

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article I. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65109. Legal advertising
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article I. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65109. Legal advertising
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65109. Legal advertising (2023)
content:
When notice is required to be published by a township in one or more newspapers, unless
   otherwise specified, publication shall be made in the legal notice section in a newspaper
   of general circulation in the township, as defined by 45 Pa.C.S. (relating to legal
   notices).  When the notice relates to any proceeding or matter in any court or the holding
   of an election for the increase of indebtedness or the issue and sale of bonds to
   be paid by taxation, the notice shall also be published in the legal newspaper of
   the county, if any, so designated by the rules of court.  Auditors' statements, summaries of auditors' statements, notices of public meetings
   and hearings, notices of budget proposals, ordinances, lists of delinquent taxpayers
   and advertisements inviting proposals for public contracts and for bids for materials
   and supplies shall be published only in newspapers of general circulation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part IX. Townships of the First Class›Article I. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 55108. Saving clauses where class of township changed
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part IX. Townships of the First Class › Article I. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 55108. Saving clauses where class of township changed
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 55108. Saving clauses where class of township changed (2023)
content:
If a township of the second class is designated a township of the first class, or
   if a township of the first class is reestablished as a township of the second class,
   all liabilities incurred, rights accrued or vested, obligations issued or contracted,
   and all suits and prosecutions pending or to be instituted to enforce any right or
   penalty accrued or to punish any offense committed before the change of class, and
   all ordinances, resolutions, rules and regulations shall continue with the same force
   and effect as if no change had been made.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article I. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65108. Saving clauses when class of township changed
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article I. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65108. Saving clauses when class of township changed
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65108. Saving clauses when class of township changed (2023)
content:
When any township of the second class is reestablished as a township of the first
   class or when any township of the first class is reestablished as a township of the
   second class, all liabilities incurred, rights accrued or vested, obligations issued
   or contracted and all suits and prosecutions pending or to be instituted to enforce
   any right or penalty accrued or punish any offense committed before the change of
   class and all resolutions, rules and regulations shall continue with the same force
   and effect as if no change had been made.

content: This act shall be known and may be cited as “The Second Class Township Code.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article I. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65107. How act applies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article I. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65107. How act applies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65107. How act applies (2023)
content:
This act shall apply to all townships of the second class as now exist and those created,
   established or reestablished after this act takes effect.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article II. Classification, Creation, Reestablishment and Change of Name of Townships›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65201. Classification of townships
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article II. Classification, Creation, Reestablishment and Change of Name of Townships › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65201. Classification of townships
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65201. Classification of townships (2023)
content:
The townships now in existence and those to be created after this act takes effect
   are divided into two classes, townships of the first class and townships of the second
   class.  Townships of the first class are those having a population of at least three hundred
   inhabitants to the square mile, which are now established as townships of the first
   class, or which may be created townships of the first class under laws relating to
   townships of the first class.  All townships that are not townships of the first class or home rule townships are
   townships of the second class.  A change from one class to the other shall be made only under this act or the laws
   relating to townships of the first class.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article II. Classification, Creation, Reestablishment and Change of Name of Townships›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65203. Creation of townships by annulment of charter of borough
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article II. Classification, Creation, Reestablishment and Change of Name of Townships › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65203. Creation of townships by annulment of charter of borough
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65203. Creation of townships by annulment of charter of borough (2023)
content:
Townships of the second class may be created by the annulment of a charter of a borough
   under laws governing boroughs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article II. Classification, Creation, Reestablishment and Change of Name of Townships›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65204. Classification of new townships
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article II. Classification, Creation, Reestablishment and Change of Name of Townships › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65204. Classification of new townships
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65204. Classification of new townships (2023)
content:
When a new township is created either by consolidation of two or more townships or
   reestablishment of a township of the first class as a township or by annulment of
   a charter of a borough, the new township shall be classified as a township of the
   second class.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article II. Classification, Creation, Reestablishment and Change of Name of Townships›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65206. Certificates of clerk of court; fee; penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article II. Classification, Creation, Reestablishment and Change of Name of Townships › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65206. Certificates of clerk of court; fee; penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65206. Certificates of clerk of court; fee; penalty (2023)
content:
(a) When a township of the second class results from the consolidation of two or more
      townships or is created or reestablished, the clerk of the court of common pleas within
      thirty days shall certify the action to the Department of Community Affairs and the
      Department of Transportation.  The clerk may charge a fee of three dollars and fifty cents ($3.50) to be paid as
      part of the costs of the proceedings.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IV. Election of Officers; Vacancies in Office›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65401. Township officers to be electors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IV. Election of Officers; Vacancies in Office › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65401. Township officers to be electors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65401. Township officers to be electors (2023)
content:
No person is eligible for the office of supervisor, auditor or tax collector in any
   township unless that person is an elector of the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article V. Township Officers Generally›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65502. Bonds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article V. Township Officers Generally › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65502. Bonds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65502. Bonds (2023)
content:
When any officer or employe of any township is required to give bond for the faithful
   performance of the duties of the office, the bond shall be with a surety company or
   other company authorized by law to act as surety, and the township may pay the premium
   on the bond.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IV. Election of Officers; Vacancies in Office›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65407. Vacancies in general
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IV. Election of Officers; Vacancies in Office › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65407. Vacancies in general
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65407. Vacancies in general (2023)
content:
(a) If the electors of any township fail to choose a supervisor, tax collector or
      auditor, or if any person elected to any office fails to serve in the office, or if
      a vacancy occurs in the office by death, resignation under subsection (b), removal
      from the township or otherwise, the board of supervisors may appoint a successor who
      is a registered elector of the township and has resided in that township continuously
      for at least one year prior to their appointment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article II. Classification, Creation, Reestablishment and Change of Name of Townships›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65205. Appointment and election of officers of new townships
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article II. Classification, Creation, Reestablishment and Change of Name of Townships › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65205. Appointment and election of officers of new townships
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65205. Appointment and election of officers of new townships (2023)
content:
When a new township results from the consolidation of townships or is created as a
   result of the annulment of a charter of a borough or when a township of the first
   class is reestablished as a township of the second class, the court of common pleas
   shall appoint the elective officers for the new township and determine the polling
   place or places in the new township.  The appointed officers shall hold their offices until the first Monday of January
   after the next municipal election which occurs at least ninety days after the appointments.  At the municipal election, a tax collector shall be elected for a regular four-year
   term if the election occurs in the year when such officer is elected for a regular
   term, and, if not, he shall be elected for a term of two years and his successor shall
   be elected for a four-year term.  At the first municipal election, one supervisor and one auditor shall be elected
   for terms of six years each, one supervisor and one auditor for terms of four years
   each and one supervisor and one auditor for terms of two years each.  All officers shall take office on the first Monday of January after their election.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article II. Classification, Creation, Reestablishment and Change of Name of Townships›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65207. Change of name of township
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article II. Classification, Creation, Reestablishment and Change of Name of Townships › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65207. Change of name of township
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65207. Change of name of township (2023)
content:
(a) Upon petition to the court of common pleas of at least ten percent of the electors
      of a township or upon passage of a resolution by the board of supervisors seeking
      a change of the name of the township, the court shall order a referendum on the question.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IV. Election of Officers; Vacancies in Office›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65406. Tax collector
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IV. Election of Officers; Vacancies in Office › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65406. Tax collector
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65406. Tax collector (2023)
content:
(a) At the municipal election in the year 1993 and at the municipal election every
      four years after that, the electors of each township shall elect one tax collector
      to serve for a term of four years, except when vacancies create shorter terms, from
      the first Monday of January after the election.  Tax collectors shall reside in the township from which elected and shall have resided
      in that township continuously for at least one year immediately preceding their election.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IV. Election of Officers; Vacancies in Office›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65402. Officers to be elected
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IV. Election of Officers; Vacancies in Office › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65402. Officers to be elected
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65402. Officers to be elected (2023)
content:
(a) Except as provided in subsection (b), the electors of each township shall elect
      three supervisors, three auditors and one tax collector.  No person shall at the same time hold more than one elective township office.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article V. Township Officers Generally›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65501. Oath of office
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article V. Township Officers Generally › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65501. Oath of office
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65501. Oath of office (2023)
content:
Every person elected or appointed to any township office shall before assuming the
   duties of the office take and subscribe an oath or affirmation before a notary public,
   district justice or judge to support the Constitutions of the United States and of
   the Commonwealth and to perform the duties of the office with fidelity.  A copy of the oath or affirmation shall be filed with the township secretary before
   assuming the duties of the office.
