path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article V. Township Officers Generally›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65503. Removal of township officers and appointees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article V. Township Officers Generally › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65503. Removal of township officers and appointees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65503. Removal of township officers and appointees (2023)
content:
Whether elected or duly appointed to fill a vacancy in elective office, a township
   officer shall be removable from office only by impeachment, or by the Governor for
   reasonable cause after due notice and full hearing on the advice of two-thirds of
   the Senate, or upon conviction of misbehavior in office, or of an infamous crime in
   accordance with the Constitution of Pennsylvania, but the officer's title to office
   may be tried by proceedings of quo warranto as provided by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IV. Election of Officers; Vacancies in Office›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65403. Supervisors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IV. Election of Officers; Vacancies in Office › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65403. Supervisors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65403. Supervisors (2023)
content:
(a) Except as provided under section 402(b)1for the election of additional supervisors or under section 402(e) for a return to
      a three-member board, or when vacancies create shorter terms, at each municipal election,
      the electors of each township shall elect one supervisor to serve for a term of six
      years from the first Monday of January after the election.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article VI. Township Supervisors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65602. Organization meeting; appointment of secretary and treasurer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article VI. Township Supervisors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65602. Organization meeting; appointment of secretary and treasurer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65602. Organization meeting; appointment of secretary and treasurer (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors shall meet at a convenient time and place on the first
      Monday in January of each year.  If the first Monday is a legal holiday, the meeting shall be held the following
      day.  The board of supervisors shall elect one member as chairman and another as vice-chairman,
      and it shall appoint a treasurer and a secretary.  The secretary shall be an individual;  however, the board of supervisors may select
      either a trust company, a banking institution or an individual to serve as treasurer,
      or the board of supervisors may appoint one individual to serve as both secretary
      and treasurer.  Members of the board of supervisors may be appointed as secretary-treasurer, secretary
      or treasurer.  With regard to boards of supervisors which are designated as three-member boards,
      any supervisor who is to be considered by the board for any appointed township position
      or for employment by the township as authorized by law shall not be excluded from
      voting on the issue of such appointment or employment.  Action taken by a supervisor shall be deemed to be within the scope of authority
      as a supervisor and shall not be deemed to constitute an illegal or an improper conflict
      of interest.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article VI. Township Supervisors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65603. Monthly meetings; quorum; and voting
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article VI. Township Supervisors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65603. Monthly meetings; quorum; and voting
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65603. Monthly meetings; quorum; and voting (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors shall meet for the transaction of business at least once
   each month at a time and place determined by the board of supervisors.  A quorum is two members of a three-member board of supervisors or three members
   of a five-member board of supervisors.  An affirmative vote of a majority of the entire board of supervisors at a public
   meeting is necessary in order to transact any business.  A member of the board shall not be disqualified from voting on any issue before
   the board solely because the member has previously expressed an opinion on the issue
   in either an official or unofficial capacity.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article VI. Township Supervisors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65601. Supervisors and government of townships
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article VI. Township Supervisors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65601. Supervisors and government of townships
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65601. Supervisors and government of townships (2023)
content:
Townships shall be governed and supervised by boards of supervisors.  Boards of supervisors shall consist of three members or, if approved by the electors
   under section 402(b),1five members.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article VI. Township Supervisors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65606. Compensation of supervisors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article VI. Township Supervisors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65606. Compensation of supervisors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65606. Compensation of supervisors (2023)
content:
(a) Supervisors may receive as compensation an amount established by ordinance not
      in excess of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IV. Election of Officers; Vacancies in Office›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65404. Auditors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IV. Election of Officers; Vacancies in Office › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65404. Auditors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65404. Auditors (2023)
content:
(a) Except when vacancies create shorter terms, at each municipal election, the electors
      of each township shall elect one auditor to serve for a term of six years from the
      first Monday of January after the election.  Auditors shall reside in the township from which elected and shall have resided
      in that township continuously for at least one year immediately preceding their election.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article VI. Township Supervisors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65604. Special meetings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article VI. Township Supervisors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65604. Special meetings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65604. Special meetings (2023)
content:
Upon call of the chairman or by agreement of a majority of its members, the board
   of supervisors may schedule special meetings of the board of supervisors after notice
   required under the act of July 3, 1986 (P.L. 388, No. 84), known as the “Sunshine
   Act.”1Notice of a special meeting shall state the nature of the business to be conducted
   at the meeting.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article VI. Township Supervisors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65605. Minutes and records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article VI. Township Supervisors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65605. Minutes and records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65605. Minutes and records (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors shall provide for the recording of minutes of its proceedings
      and other books it may find necessary in the performance of its duties.  The records shall be made available to the board of auditors during the annual audit.  Unless the custodian of the records agrees otherwise, the records shall be audited
      or inspected at the place where they are normally maintained.  Supervisors who leave office shall deliver all township records in their possession
      to their successors or to the township secretary.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article VII. Township Treasurer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65705. Assistant treasurer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article VII. Township Treasurer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65705. Assistant treasurer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65705. Assistant treasurer (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may appoint an assistant treasurer who shall assist the township
   treasurer or, in the absence or disability of the township treasurer, perform the
   duties of the township treasurer.  The assistant treasurer may be appointed from the membership of the board of supervisors.  The assistant treasurer shall be bonded for the same amount as the township treasurer
   when acting in the capacity of township treasurer.  The board of supervisors shall determine the compensation of the assistant treasurer.  When a supervisor is appointed assistant treasurer, the board of auditors shall
   determine the compensation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article VII. Township Treasurer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65702. Treasurer's bond
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article VII. Township Treasurer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65702. Treasurer's bond
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65702. Treasurer's bond (2023)
content:
The township treasurer, if an individual, shall give bond with a surety company in
   an amount established by the board of supervisors for the faithful performance of
   the duties of the office.  The amount of the bond shall equal the highest amount of township funds estimated
   by the board of supervisors to be available to the township treasurer at any time
   during the current year.  The bond shall be filed with the board of auditors of the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article VII. Township Treasurer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65701. Township treasurer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article VII. Township Treasurer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65701. Township treasurer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65701. Township treasurer (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors shall appoint a township treasurer to serve at the pleasure
   of the board of supervisors.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article VII. Township Treasurer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65706. Use of special funds; penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article VII. Township Treasurer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65706. Use of special funds; penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65706. Use of special funds; penalty (2023)
content:
When any moneys are collected for any special purpose, no township treasurer or board
   of supervisors may apply those moneys to any purpose other than that for which they
   were collected.  Every misapplication shall be a misdemeanor of the third degree, and, in addition
   to the fine or penalty which may be imposed upon conviction, the defendant shall be
   required to pay restitution in the amount of moneys improperly spent.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article VII. Township Treasurer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65707. Penalty for failure to perform duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article VII. Township Treasurer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65707. Penalty for failure to perform duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65707. Penalty for failure to perform duties (2023)
content:
A township treasurer or assistant treasurer who fails to perform any duties of the
   office other than those for which specific penalties are provided commits a summary
   offense and, in addition to the fine or penalty which may be imposed upon conviction,
   is required to pay to the township an amount equal to the amount of the financial
   loss that occurred, if any, for not performing the duties of the office.  That person is disqualified from holding the office of township treasurer or assistant
   treasurer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article VII. Township Treasurer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65704. Treasurer's duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article VII. Township Treasurer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65704. Treasurer's duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65704. Treasurer's duties (2023)
content: The township treasurer shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article VII. Township Treasurer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65703. Treasurer's compensation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article VII. Township Treasurer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65703. Treasurer's compensation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65703. Treasurer's compensation (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors shall determine the compensation of the township treasurer.  When a supervisor is appointed as township treasurer, the board of auditors shall
   determine the compensation.  A person may not receive hourly compensation for work as a superintendent, roadmaster
   or laborer for time spent in the performance of the duties of township treasurer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article VII. Township Treasurer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65708. Depositories of township funds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article VII. Township Treasurer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65708. Depositories of township funds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65708. Depositories of township funds (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors shall designate by resolution a depository or depositories
      for township funds.  Any funds deposited with any banking institution of this Commonwealth shall be insured
      with the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation or the National Credit Union Share
      Insurance Fund or their successor agencies, to the extent that accounts are so insured.  The board of supervisors shall require each banking institution to furnish additional
      bond, insurance or security to cover the amount of any deposits in excess of the insured
      limits.  The designation is valid for a period of one year or until another depository or
      other depositories are designated by similar action of the board of supervisors.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article VI. Township Supervisors›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65607. Duties of supervisors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article VI. Township Supervisors › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65607. Duties of supervisors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65607. Duties of supervisors (2023)
content: The board of supervisors shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article VIII. Township Secretary›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65803. Secretary's compensation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article VIII. Township Secretary › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65803. Secretary's compensation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65803. Secretary's compensation (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors shall determine the compensation of the township secretary.  When a supervisor is appointed township secretary, the board of auditors shall determine
   the compensation.  A person may not receive hourly compensation for work as a superintendent, roadmaster
   or laborer for time spent in the performance of the duties of township secretary.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article VIII. Township Secretary›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65804. Assistant secretary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article VIII. Township Secretary › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65804. Assistant secretary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65804. Assistant secretary (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may appoint an assistant secretary who shall assist the township
   secretary or, in the absence or disability of the township secretary, perform the
   duties of the township secretary.  The assistant secretary may be appointed from the membership of the board of supervisors.  The board of supervisors shall determine the compensation of the assistant secretary.  When a supervisor is appointed assistant secretary, the board of auditors shall
   determine the compensation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article VIII. Township Secretary›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65801. Township secretary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article VIII. Township Secretary › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65801. Township secretary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65801. Township secretary (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors shall appoint a township secretary to serve at the pleasure
   of the board of supervisors.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IX. Auditors; Accountants›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65902. Auditor's compensation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IX. Auditors; Accountants › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65902. Auditor's compensation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65902. Auditor's compensation (2023)
content:
(a) Each auditor shall receive ten dollars ($10) for each hour necessarily employed
      in the duties of the office upon presentation to the board of supervisors of an itemized
      listing of the dates, times, places and hours worked to perform the audit.  No auditor in a township having a population of ten thousand or less is entitled
      to receive more than one thousand eight hundred dollars ($1,800) for completing the
      annual audit, settlement and adjustment.  No auditor in a township having a population in excess of ten thousand is entitled
      to receive more than three thousand five hundred dollars ($3,500) for completing the
      annual audit, settlement and adjustment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IX. Auditors; Accountants›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65901. Township auditors; meetings; duties; quorum
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IX. Auditors; Accountants › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65901. Township auditors; meetings; duties; quorum
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65901. Township auditors; meetings; duties; quorum (2023)
content:
(a) The board of auditors shall meet annually at the place of meeting of the board
      of supervisors on the day following the day designated by this act for organization
      of the board of supervisors and they shall organize by the election of a chairman
      and secretary.  The board of auditors shall audit, settle and adjust the accounts of all elected
      or appointed officials of the township and its boards or agencies that received or
      disbursed funds of or owing to the township during the immediately preceding calendar
      year.  The board of auditors shall determine the compensations for the current year authorized
      in section 6061for supervisors employed by the township.  Two auditors shall constitute a quorum.  The auditors may also make an audit of the dockets, transcripts and other official
      records of the district justices to determine the amount of fines and costs paid over
      or due the township, and the dockets and records of the district justices shall be
      open to inspection by the auditors for that purpose.  Unless otherwise agreed to by the board of auditors and the officer being audited,
      the audit shall be conducted at the place the records of the officer are normally
      kept.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IX. Auditors; Accountants›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65905. Penalty for failure to perform duty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IX. Auditors; Accountants › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65905. Penalty for failure to perform duty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65905. Penalty for failure to perform duty (2023)
content: Any auditor who fails to comply with this article commits a summary offense.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IX. Auditors; Accountants›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65906. Employment and compensation of attorney
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IX. Auditors; Accountants › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65906. Employment and compensation of attorney
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65906. Employment and compensation of attorney (2023)
content:
If a disagreement occurs with the board of auditors and any official it is required
   to audit, the board of auditors may petition the court of common pleas to appoint
   an attorney to represent or advise the board of auditors on the matter.  The court shall not appoint an attorney unless reasonable effort to reach an agreement
   has been made and only after the board of auditors has given notice to the official
   or the board of supervisors of its intent to petition the court for the appointment.  The board of auditors, with the agreement of the board of supervisors, shall determine
   the compensation of the attorney.  If the dispute results in litigation or if the board of auditors and the board of
   supervisors cannot agree upon the compensation to be paid to the attorney, the court
   shall establish the compensation for the attorney appointed for the board of auditors.  The compensation for the attorney shall be paid out of the general township fund.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IX. Auditors; Accountants›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65908. Collection of surcharge; bond
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IX. Auditors; Accountants › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65908. Collection of surcharge; bond
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65908. Collection of surcharge; bond (2023)
content:
Any auditor, elector or taxpayer of the township may enforce the collection of a judgment
   entered for a surcharge for the benefit of the township, by any appropriate action
   or execution, upon filing in the court of common pleas a bond (in the case of an elector
   or taxpayer), with one or more sureties, conditioned to indemnify the township for
   all costs which may accrue in the proceedings undertaken, subject, however, to all
   rights of appeal from the report of the board of auditors.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IX. Auditors; Accountants›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65904. Completion, filing and publication of annual township report and financial statement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IX. Auditors; Accountants › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65904. Completion, filing and publication of annual township report and financial statement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65904. Completion, filing and publication of annual township report and financial statement (2023)
content:
(a) The board of auditors shall complete their audit, settlement and adjustment before
      the first day of April of each year.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IX. Auditors; Accountants›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65903. Subpoenas; oaths; perjury
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IX. Auditors; Accountants › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65903. Subpoenas; oaths; perjury
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65903. Subpoenas; oaths; perjury (2023)
content:
The board of auditors may issue subpoenas to obtain the attendance of the officers
   whose accounts they are required to audit or adjust, of their executors and administrators
   and of any person whom it may be necessary to examine as a witness and to compel their
   attendance, by attachment, the same as any court of common pleas may in cases pending
   before them and may also compel the production of all books, vouchers and papers relative
   to township accounts.  The subpoena and attachment shall be issued by a district justice.  The board of auditors may administer oaths and affirmations to all persons brought
   or appearing before them, whether accountants, witnesses or otherwise.  All persons swearing or affirming falsely upon examination are guilty of perjury.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IX. Auditors; Accountants›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65909. Appeals from report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IX. Auditors; Accountants › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65909. Appeals from report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65909. Appeals from report (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors or any elector or taxpayer of the township or any officer
   whose account is settled or audited by the board of auditors may appeal from any settlement
   or audit of the board of auditors to the court of common pleas within forty-five days
   after the settlement has been filed in the court of common pleas.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article VIII. Township Secretary›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65802. Secretary's duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article VIII. Township Secretary › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65802. Secretary's duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65802. Secretary's duties (2023)
content: The township secretary is a clerk to the board of supervisors.  The township secretary shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IX. Auditors; Accountants›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65912. Report; prima facie evidence; burden of proof
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IX. Auditors; Accountants › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65912. Report; prima facie evidence; burden of proof
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65912. Report; prima facie evidence; burden of proof (2023)
content:
The accounts of the officer in question may be investigated de novo.  The figures and facts found and stated by the auditors in their report of audit
   shall be taken as prima facie correct as against any officer, and the burden shall
   be upon each officer whose accounts are in question to establish the validity of the
   credits which he claims.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IX. Auditors; Accountants›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65914. Costs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IX. Auditors; Accountants › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65914. Costs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65914. Costs (2023)
content:
In all cases of appeal from the report or audit of the board of auditors to the court
   of common pleas, the costs shall be determined by the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IX. Auditors; Accountants›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65907. Surcharge by auditors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IX. Auditors; Accountants › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65907. Surcharge by auditors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65907. Surcharge by auditors (2023)
content:
(a) The board of auditors shall surcharge any elected or appointed officer for the
      amount of any loss to the township caused in whole or in part by the officer's act
      or omission in violation of law or beyond the scope of the officer's authority.  If the auditors find an absence of intent to violate the law or exceed the scope
      of authority and find the result of the officer's act could have been achieved by
      legal means and authorized procedures, the surcharge imposed shall be limited to the
      difference between the costs actually incurred by the township and the costs that
      would have been incurred had legal means and authorized procedures been employed.  Provisions of this section which limit the amount of surcharge do not apply to cases
      involving fraud or collusion on the part of the officers or to any penalty ensuing
      to the benefit of or payable to the Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IX. Auditors; Accountants›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65910. Taxpayer's appeal; bond
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IX. Auditors; Accountants › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65910. Taxpayer's appeal; bond
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65910. Taxpayer's appeal; bond (2023)
content:
No appeal by an elector, taxpayer or officer shall be allowed unless the appellant
   enters into recognizance to prosecute the appeal with effect, and to pay all costs
   accruing thereon, in case, if the appellant is an elector or taxpayer, he fails to
   obtain a final decision more favorable to the township than that awarded by the board
   of auditors or, if the appellant is an officer, he fails to obtain a final decision
   more favorable to the officer than that awarded by the board of auditors.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IX. Auditors; Accountants›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65913. Findings; judgment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IX. Auditors; Accountants › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65913. Findings; judgment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65913. Findings; judgment (2023)
content:
After hearing, the court shall file findings of fact and law and enter judgment, and
   the judgment so entered may be enforced by appropriate proceedings by any auditor,
   officer, elector or taxpayer of the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IX. Auditors; Accountants›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65911. Consolidation of appeals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IX. Auditors; Accountants › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65911. Consolidation of appeals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65911. Consolidation of appeals (2023)
content:
When more than one appeal from the report of the board of auditors is taken, whether
   by the board of supervisors, by an officer thereof or by an elector or taxpayer, the
   court may direct that the several appeals be consolidated.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IX. Auditors; Accountants›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65917. Appointment of accountant
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IX. Auditors; Accountants › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65917. Appointment of accountant
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65917. Appointment of accountant (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors may contract with a certified or competent public accountant
      or a firm of certified or competent public accountants, either of which shall be registered
      in this Commonwealth, to be appointed by the court of common pleas at least thirty
      days before the close of the fiscal year to audit the accounts of the township and
      the township officers if a petition has been presented to the supervisors by at least
      twenty-five taxpayers of the township asking for the appointment.  The amount paid to the accountant or firm in any year shall not exceed the maximum
      allowed by law to be paid to the board of auditors in any year unless the payment
      of an additional amount is approved by the court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IX. Auditors; Accountants›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65915. Attorney fees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IX. Auditors; Accountants › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65915. Attorney fees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65915. Attorney fees (2023)
content:
Upon final determination of an appeal taken under section 9091from any report, audit or settlement of the account of any township officer, attorney
   fees shall be awarded as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article X. Tax Collector; Assessor›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66001. Tax collector; powers, duties and liabilities
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article X. Tax Collector; Assessor › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66001. Tax collector; powers, duties and liabilities
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66001. Tax collector; powers, duties and liabilities (2023)
content:
The tax collector shall collect all county, township, school, institution district
   and other taxes levied within townships by authorities authorized to levy taxes.  The tax collector may also be designated in the tax-levying ordinance or resolution
   or be employed by the tax-levying authority to collect taxes levied under the act
   of December 31, 1965 (P.L. 1257, No. 511), known as “The Local Tax Enabling Act.”1In addition to the powers, duties and responsibilities under this act, the tax collector
   shall exercise all the powers and perform all the duties and be subject to all the
   obligations and responsibilities for the collection of taxes as are conferred upon
   tax collectors by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article IX. Auditors; Accountants›PA ST 53 P.S. § 65916. Interest in township transactions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article IX. Auditors; Accountants › PA ST 53 P.S. § 65916. Interest in township transactions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 65916. Interest in township transactions (2023)
content:
Any auditor who is financially interested, directly or indirectly, in any township
   transaction commits a summary offense.  The auditor shall forfeit the office and forfeit to the township any financial benefit
   derived from the transaction.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XII. Township Engineer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66201. Township engineer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XII. Township Engineer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66201. Township engineer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66201. Township engineer (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may appoint and determine the compensation of a township
   engineer who shall be a registered professional engineer.  The township engineer serves at the pleasure of the board of supervisors.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XI. Township Solicitor›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66102. Solicitor to have control of legal matters
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XI. Township Solicitor › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66102. Solicitor to have control of legal matters
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66102. Solicitor to have control of legal matters (2023)
content:
The township solicitor shall direct and control the legal matters of the township,
   and no official or official body of the township, except as otherwise provided under
   law, shall employ an additional attorney without the assent or ratification of the
   board of supervisors.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XI. Township Solicitor›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66101. Township solicitor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XI. Township Solicitor › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66101. Township solicitor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66101. Township solicitor (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may appoint and determine the compensation of a township
   solicitor.  The township solicitor shall be licensed to practice law in this Commonwealth and
   may be one person or a law firm, partnership, association or professional corporation.  The township solicitor serves at the pleasure of the board of supervisors.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XII. Township Engineer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66203. Certificate of commencement and of completion of municipal improvements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XII. Township Engineer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66203. Certificate of commencement and of completion of municipal improvements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66203. Certificate of commencement and of completion of municipal improvements (2023)
content:
The township engineer shall certify to the township secretary the date of commencement
   and of completion of all municipal improvements, the cost of which, in whole or in
   part, is to be paid by the owners of the abutting property.  The certification shall be made a part of the permanent records of the township.  The certified time of commencement and completion is conclusive on all parties.  The term“certified time of completion”means the time of the completion of the whole contract for the improvement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XII. Township Engineer›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66202. Engineer's duties; preparation of plans
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XII. Township Engineer › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66202. Engineer's duties; preparation of plans
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66202. Engineer's duties; preparation of plans (2023)
content:
The township engineer shall perform duties as the board of supervisors may direct
   for the construction, reconstruction, maintenance and repair of streets, roads, pavements,
   sanitary sewers, bridges, culverts and other engineering work.  The township engineer shall prepare plans, specifications and estimates of the work
   undertaken by the township and furnish the board of supervisors with reports, information
   or estimates on any township engineering work or on questions submitted by the board
   of supervisors.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66504. Personal property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66504. Personal property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66504. Personal property (2023)
content:
(a) No personal property of the township shall be sold or disposed of without the
      approval of the board of supervisors.  No personal property owned by the township, the estimated fair market value of which
      is two thousand dollars ($2,000) or more, shall be sold except to the highest bidder
      after due notice by advertisement for bids or for public auction in one newspaper
      of general circulation in the township.  The advertisement shall be published once not less than ten days before the date
      set for the opening of bids or public auction, and the date for opening bids or public
      auction shall be announced in the advertisement.  The advertisement for electronic auction sales authorized in subsection (d) shall
      include the Internet address or means of accessing the electronic auction and the
      date, time and duration of the electronic auction.  If after attempting twice to receive bids or if at a public auction no bid was received,
      the board of supervisors may by resolution adopt a procedure by which the personal
      property may be sold without further action of the board of supervisors.  A procedure adopted pursuant to this authorization shall be subject to and shall
      conform with the requirements of any law governing the sale of property by municipal
      corporations generally when no bids have been received.  The award of contracts shall be made only by public announcement at a regular or
      special meeting of the board of supervisors or at the public auction.  Except as provided in subsection (d), all bids shall be accepted on the condition
      that payment of the purchase price in full is made immediately upon acceptance of
      the successful bid.  The board of supervisors may reject any bids received if the bids are believed to
      be less than the fair market value of the property.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XIV. County and State Associations of Townships›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66401. County associations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XIV. County and State Associations of Townships › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66401. County associations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66401. County associations (2023)
content:
(a) County associations of township officials may be formed.  County associations shall hold annual or semi-annual conventions at places determined
      by the association to consider and discuss questions and subjects pertaining to improvement
      of township government, assessment of property, collection of taxes and construction,
      improvement and maintenance of roads.  Associations of two or more adjacent counties may arrange to meet in joint sessions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XIV. County and State Associations of Townships›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66402. State Association of Township Supervisors authorized
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XIV. County and State Associations of Townships › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66402. State Association of Township Supervisors authorized
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66402. State Association of Township Supervisors authorized (2023)
content: (a) The formation of a State Association of Township Supervisors is authorized.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XIII. Township Manager›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66301. Township manager; appointment, removal, powers and duties; compensation; bond
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XIII. Township Manager › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66301. Township manager; appointment, removal, powers and duties; compensation; bond
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66301. Township manager; appointment, removal, powers and duties; compensation; bond (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors may by ordinance at any time create the office of township
      manager and may in like manner abolish the office.  While the office exists, the board of supervisors shall appoint one person to fill
      the office.  The township manager shall serve at the pleasure of the board of supervisors, subject
      to contractual rights that may arise under an employment agreement that may be entered
      into in accordance with subsection (a.1).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XI. Township Solicitor›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66103. Duties of solicitor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XI. Township Solicitor › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66103. Duties of solicitor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66103. Duties of solicitor (2023)
content:
The township solicitor, when directed or requested so to do, shall prepare or approve
   any bonds, obligations, contracts, leases, conveyances, ordinances and assurances
   to which the township may be a party.  The township solicitor shall commence and prosecute all actions brought by the township
   for or on account of any of the estates, rights, trusts, privileges, claims or demands,
   as well as defend the township or any township officer against all actions or suits
   brought against the township or township officer in which any of the estates, rights,
   privileges, trusts, ordinances or accounts of the township may be brought in question
   before any court in this Commonwealth and do every professional act incident to the
   office which the township solicitor may be authorized or required to do by the board
   of supervisors or by any resolution.  The township solicitor shall furnish the board of supervisors, upon request, with
   an opinion in writing upon any question of law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66502. Property; penalty for violation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66502. Property; penalty for violation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66502. Property; penalty for violation (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors may purchase, acquire by gift or otherwise, hold, lease,
      let and convey, by sale or lease, any real and personal property it judges to be to
      the best interest of the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66501. Suits
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66501. Suits
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66501. Suits (2023)
content: Any township may sue and be sued.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66507. Intergovernmental cooperation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66507. Intergovernmental cooperation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66507. Intergovernmental cooperation (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may make agreements with other municipal corporations in
   performing governmental powers, duties and functions and in carrying into effect provisions
   of 53 Pa.C.S. Ch. 23 Subch. A (relating to intergovernmental cooperation).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66508. Capital reserve fund
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66508. Capital reserve fund
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66508. Capital reserve fund (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors may create and maintain a separate capital reserve fund
      for any anticipated capital expenses, which fund shall be designated for a specific
      purpose or purposes when created.  The moneys in the fund shall be used for no other purpose unless the board of supervisors
      declares that conditions in the township make other expenses more urgent than those
      for which the fund was created.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66503. Real property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66503. Real property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66503. Real property (2023)
content:
(a) No real estate owned by the township having a value in excess of six thousand
      dollars ($6,000) may be sold except to the highest bidder after due notice by advertisement
      for bids or advertisement of a public auction in one newspaper of general circulation
      in the township.  The advertisement shall be published once not less than ten days before the date
      set for the opening of bids or public auction, and the date for opening bids or public
      auction shall be announced in the advertisement.  The award of contracts shall be made only by public announcement at a regular or
      special meeting of the board of supervisors or at the public auction.  All bids shall be accepted on the condition that payment of the purchase price in
      full shall be made within sixty days of the acceptance of bids.  Real estate owned by the township may be sold at a consideration of six thousand
      dollars ($6,000) or less without advertisement or competitive bidding only after the
      board of supervisors estimates the value of the real estate upon receipt of an appraisal
      by a qualified real estate appraiser.  Prior to selling real estate valued at six thousand dollars ($6,000) or less without
      advertisement or competitive bidding, the board of supervisors shall make a public
      announcement of the board of supervisors' intention to sell the real estate at a regular
      or special meeting of the board of supervisors at least thirty days prior to the sale.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66508.1. Operating reserve fund
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66508.1. Operating reserve fund
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66508.1. Operating reserve fund (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors shall have the power to create and maintain a separate
      operating reserve fund in order to minimize future revenue shortfalls and deficits,
      provide greater continuity and predictability in the funding of vital government services,
      minimize the need to increase taxes to balance the budget in times of fiscal distress,
      provide the capacity to undertake long-range financial planning and develop fiscal
      resources to meet long-term needs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66511. Township seals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66511. Township seals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66511. Township seals (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may adopt a seal which contains the name of the township
   and the word“seal”and which shall be in the custody of the township secretary or manager.  The official acts of the board of supervisors may be authenticated by use of the
   seal.  The seal has the same effect as the seal of a notary public.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66510. Display of flags
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66510. Display of flags
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66510. Display of flags (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may display the flag of the United States or the Commonwealth,
   the official POW/MIA flag or the flag of any county or municipal corporation on any
   public building or grounds of the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66506. General powers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66506. General powers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66506. General powers (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may make and adopt any ordinances, bylaws, rules and regulations
   not inconsistent with or restrained by the Constitution and laws of this Commonwealth
   necessary for the proper management, care and control of the township and its finances
   and the maintenance of peace, good government, health and welfare of the township
   and its citizens, trade, commerce and manufacturers.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66513. Widening and deepening watercourses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66513. Widening and deepening watercourses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66513. Widening and deepening watercourses (2023)
content:
After permits have been secured from the Department of Environmental Protection and
   the Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission, the board of supervisors or its agents
   or employes may widen and deepen watercourses running through the township and erect
   dikes, retaining walls and embankments along the watercourses as are necessary to
   prevent water from overflowing the banks.  For these purposes, townships may enter and condemn property as may be necessary.  Townships may enter land lying near the watercourses and secure materials as may
   be necessary in connection with the work.  Damages for property taken, injured or destroyed as the result of the work shall
   be determined under this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66505. Boards of supervisors to exercise powers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66505. Boards of supervisors to exercise powers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66505. Boards of supervisors to exercise powers (2023)
content:
The corporate powers of townships shall be exercised by the board of supervisors.  If no specific authority is given for the payment of costs incurred in the exercise
   of any power contained in this act, the expenses may be paid from the general township
   fund.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66509. Indebtedness
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66509. Indebtedness
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66509. Indebtedness (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may incur indebtedness and issues1notes, bonds or other evidence of indebtedness under the act of July 12, 1972 (P.L.
   781, No. 185), known as the “Local Government Unit Debt Act,”2to provide sufficient moneys for any expense of the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66512. Insurance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66512. Insurance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66512. Insurance (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors shall secure workers' compensation insurance for its
      employes, including volunteer firemen and volunteer ambulance and rescue personnel
      of companies duly recognized by the township by resolution, killed or injured in the
      course of their appointed functions or while performing any other duties expressly
      authorized by the board of supervisors.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66514. Airports
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66514. Airports
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66514. Airports (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors may acquire by grant, lease, purchase or, where appropriate,
      eminent domain any property located inside or outside the boundaries of the township
      which in the judgment of the board of supervisors may be necessary to establish and
      maintain municipal airport facilities.  Any township having acquired land for those purposes may establish, equip, condition,
      operate and maintain the property as a municipal airport, may lease all or part of
      the property to any individual or corporation desiring to use the property for aviation
      purposes and may contract in the form of a lease of all or part of the property by
      the Federal Government for aviation purposes upon nominal rental or without consideration.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66523. Surplus foods
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66523. Surplus foods
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66523. Surplus foods (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may appropriate moneys for the handling, storage and distribution
   of surplus foods obtained through a Federal, State or local agency.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66524. Community nursing services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66524. Community nursing services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66524. Community nursing services (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may appropriate moneys to nonprofit associations or corporations
   which provide community nursing services.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66515. Urban common carrier mass transportation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66515. Urban common carrier mass transportation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66515. Urban common carrier mass transportation (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may appropriate funds for urban common carrier mass transportation
   purposes, make contributions to county departments of transportation or urban common
   carrier mass transportation authorities to assist the departments or the authorities
   to meet costs of planning, operation, maintenance, capital improvements and debt service
   and make long-term agreements providing for the payment of contributions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66520. Numbering of buildings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66520. Numbering of buildings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66520. Numbering of buildings (2023)
content: The board of supervisors may by ordinance require and regulate the numbering of buildings.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66516. Land use regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66516. Land use regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66516. Land use regulations (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may plan for the development of the township through zoning,
   subdivision and land development regulations under the act of July 31, 1968 (P.L.
   805, No. 247), known as the “Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code.”1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66521. Insect, pest and vector programs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66521. Insect, pest and vector programs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66521. Insect, pest and vector programs (2023)
content: The board of supervisors may appropriate moneys toward insect, pest and vector programs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66519. Building lines
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66519. Building lines
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66519. Building lines (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may by ordinance establish and maintain uniform building
   lines upon any or all public streets or highways of the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66517. Building and housing regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66517. Building and housing regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66517. Building and housing regulations (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may enact and enforce codes and ordinances to govern and
   regulate the construction, alteration, repair, occupation, maintenance, sanitation,
   lighting, ventilation, water supply, toilet facilities, drainage, use and inspection
   of all buildings and housing constructed, erected, altered, designed or used for any
   use or occupancy and the sanitation and inspection of land in accordance with Article
   XVII-A.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66528. Ambulances and rescue and life saving services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66528. Ambulances and rescue and life saving services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66528. Ambulances and rescue and life saving services (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may acquire, operate and maintain motor vehicles for the
   purposes of conveying persons to and from hospitals, and it may appropriate moneys
   toward ambulance and rescue and life saving services and make contracts relating thereto.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66525. Mental health centers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66525. Mental health centers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66525. Mental health centers (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may appropriate moneys toward any nonprofit association or
   corporation which operates or conducts a mental health center.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66526. Hospitals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66526. Hospitals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66526. Hospitals (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may appropriate not exceeding one dollar ($1) for each township
   resident each year toward the erection, maintenance or support of any medical center
   or hospital building facilities.  If the total cost of the purchase or erection exceeds one hundred thousand dollars
   ($100,000), approval by the appropriate health planning agency is required.  The number of residents is determined from the latest official census.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66529. Nuisances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66529. Nuisances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66529. Nuisances (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may by ordinance prohibit nuisances, including, but not limited
   to, the storage of abandoned or junked automobiles, on private and public property
   and the carrying on of any offensive manufacture or business.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66527. Public safety
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66527. Public safety
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66527. Public safety (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may adopt ordinances to secure the safety of persons or property
   within the township and to define disturbing the peace within the limits of the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66522. Sewage treatment facilities regulations
