title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66522. Sewage treatment facilities regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66522. Sewage treatment facilities regulations (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may by ordinance make regulations respecting the installation
   of individual or community sewage treatment facilities under the act of January 24,
   1966 (1965 P.L. 1535, No. 537), known as the “Pennsylvania Sewage Facilities Act.”1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66531. Animal shelters
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66531. Animal shelters
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66531. Animal shelters (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may appropriate moneys to foster, encourage or assist the
   operation of humane societies, animal shelters or animal control centers or programs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66532. Regulation of business
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66532. Regulation of business
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66532. Regulation of business (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors may license and regulate, by ordinance, the following
      business activities within the township:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66535. Human services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66535. Human services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66535. Human services (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may, under the provisions of the act of December 10, 1974
   (P.L. 865, No. 292),1entitled “An act authorizing municipalities to expend Federal general revenue sharing
   or general funds for social service programs for the poor, the disabled and the aging,
   and to jointly cooperate in the sponsorship, establishment, administration, maintenance
   and operation of such programs,” by ordinance or resolution appropriate moneys for
   social service programs for the poor, the disabled and the aging.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66533. Dangerous structures
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66533. Dangerous structures
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66533. Dangerous structures (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may by ordinance require the owner to remove any nuisance
   or dangerous structure on public or private grounds after notice to the owner to do
   so.  In the owner's default, the board of supervisors may remove the nuisance or structure
   and collect the cost of the removal, together with the penalty imposed by the ordinance,
   from the owner by summary proceedings or under law for the collection of municipal
   liens.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66537. Burial plots of service persons
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66537. Burial plots of service persons
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66537. Burial plots of service persons (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may purchase plots of ground in any cemetery or burial ground
   for the interment of deceased or former service men and women who at the time of their
   death maintained legal residence within the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66534. Fireworks and inflammable articles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66534. Fireworks and inflammable articles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66534. Fireworks and inflammable articles (2023)
content: The board of supervisors may:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66542. Community development
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66542. Community development
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66542. Community development (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may undertake community development programs, including,
   but not limited to, urban renewal, public housing, model cities programs and neighborhood
   development projects.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66545. Nonprofit art corporations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66545. Nonprofit art corporations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66545. Nonprofit art corporations (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may appropriate moneys, not exceeding an amount equal to
   one mill of the real estate tax, to any nonprofit art corporation for the conduct
   of its artistic and cultural activities.  For the purposes of this section, the term“nonprofit art corporation”means a local arts council, commission or coordinating agency or any other nonprofit
   corporation engaged in the production or display of works of art, including the visual,
   written or performing arts and the term“artistic and cultural activities”includes the display or production of theater, music, dance, painting, architecture,
   sculpture, arts and crafts, photography, film, graphic arts and design and creative
   writing.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66539. Libraries
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66539. Libraries
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66539. Libraries (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may, in accordance with the act of June 14, 1961 (P.L. 324,
   No. 188), known as “The Library Code,”1appropriate moneys toward any nonprofit association or corporation which operates
   or conducts a library or contract with or make grants to counties or municipal corporations
   for the furnishing of library service to the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66543. Industrial promotion
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66543. Industrial promotion
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66543. Industrial promotion (2023)
content: The board of supervisors may make appropriations to an industrial development agency.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66548. Municipality authorities
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66548. Municipality authorities
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66548. Municipality authorities (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may by ordinance or resolution individually or in cooperation
   with other municipal corporations form municipality authorities as authorized by the
   act of May 2, 1945 (P.L. 382, No. 164), known as the “Municipality Authorities Act
   of 1945,”1specify the project or projects to be undertaken by the authorities, appoint members
   and establish their compensation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66536. Cemeteries
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66536. Cemeteries
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66536. Cemeteries (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors may by ordinance make rules and regulations regarding
      the location, operation and maintenance of cemeteries in the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66530. Regulation of dogs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66530. Regulation of dogs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66530. Regulation of dogs (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may by ordinance prohibit and regulate the running at large
   of dogs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66540. Observances and celebrations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66540. Observances and celebrations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66540. Observances and celebrations (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may appropriate moneys for the observance of holidays, centennials
   or other anniversaries or for township celebrations or civic projects or programs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66547. Public rewards
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66547. Public rewards
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66547. Public rewards (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may offer rewards for information leading to the arrest and
   conviction of persons who commit capital or other crimes within the township or for
   the violation of any township ordinance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66541. Historical property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66541. Historical property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66541. Historical property (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may acquire by purchase or by gift, repair, supervise, operate
   and maintain ancient landmarks and other property of historical or antiquarian interest
   and make appropriations to nonprofit associations or corporations organized to acquire
   and maintain historical properties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66538. Care of memorials
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66538. Care of memorials
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66538. Care of memorials (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may maintain and repair any soldiers' monument or memorial
   existing or erected within the township and may receive funds from persons or organizations
   for those purposes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66546. Neighborhood crime watch programs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66546. Neighborhood crime watch programs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66546. Neighborhood crime watch programs (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may appropriate moneys toward a neighborhood crime watch
   program.  No township or township official is subject to contractual, tort or other liability
   as a result of making an appropriation under this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66549. Racetracks
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66549. Racetracks
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66549. Racetracks (2023)
content:
(a) In addition to the powers and duties imposed upon the township supervisors by
      this act or any other provision of law, the township supervisors shall have the power
      and duty to secure the health, safety and welfare of persons and property by adopting
      an ordinance prohibiting the conducting of live horse race meets by a licensed corporation
      at a racetrack located within the area of fifty air miles from the center of an existing,
      currently licensed racetrack, notwithstanding the provisions of the act of December
      17, 1981 (P.L. 435, No. 135), known as the “Race Horse Industry Reform Act,”1provided that a majority of electors of the township approve a referendum pursuant
      to subsection (b) prohibiting the conducting of such horse race meets within the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66550. Conservation district
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66550. Conservation district
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66550. Conservation district (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may make appropriations to a conservation district as defined
   in the act of May 15, 1945 (P.L. 547, No. 217), known as the “Conservation District
   Law.”1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66551. Watershed associations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66551. Watershed associations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66551. Watershed associations (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may make appropriations to nonprofit watershed associations
   for watersheds serving the township.  Such appropriations may not be used to undertake litigation against any municipal
   corporation or to seek redress against any individual landowner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66552. Counties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66552. Counties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66552. Counties (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may make appropriations to the county in which the township
   is situated for land acquisition related to community and economic development projects
   located within the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66544. Tourist promotion agencies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66544. Tourist promotion agencies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66544. Tourist promotion agencies (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may appropriate moneys not in excess of ten cents (10¢) for
   each resident of the township, as determined by the latest official census, to any
   tourist promotion agency, as defined in the act of April 28, 1961 (P.L. 111, No. 50),
   known as the “Tourist Promotion Law,”1to assist the agencies in carrying out tourist promotional activities.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XVII. Public Buildings›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66701. Township buildings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XVII. Public Buildings › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66701. Township buildings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66701. Township buildings (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors may procure by purchase, gift, devise or the exercise
      of eminent domain a lot or lots of ground located within the township and erect or
      use buildings thereon for township purposes.  No land or property used for any cemetery, burying ground, public or parochial school,
      educational or charitable institution, seminary or place of public worship shall be
      taken or appropriated under this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XVII. Public Buildings›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66702. Use of public land acquired for other purposes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XVII. Public Buildings › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66702. Use of public land acquired for other purposes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66702. Use of public land acquired for other purposes (2023)
content:
When the board of supervisors desires to take any public lands previously granted
   or dedicated to a use or purpose for which they are no longer used, it shall pass
   an ordinance declaring its intention and shall petition the court of common pleas
   for leave to file the bond of the township to secure any person or persons who may
   be entitled to compensation for the taking.  The court shall direct notice to be given by publication in at least one newspaper
   circulating generally in the township.  The court may increase the amount of the bond, shall hear all exceptions that are
   filed against the petition and the sufficiency of the bond and may grant or deny the
   request of the petition.  Upon the granting of the petition and the approval of the bond, the board of supervisors
   may enter lands for the purposes of erecting public buildings.  The bond, which shall be in the name of the Commonwealth for the use of any person
   or persons who are entitled to damages by reason of the taking of the lands, shall
   remain on file for their use and benefit.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XVII. Public Buildings›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66704. Garages and warehouses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XVII. Public Buildings › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66704. Garages and warehouses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66704. Garages and warehouses (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may purchase or lease land inside or outside the limits of
   the township and erect garages, warehouses or other buildings as may be necessary
   for handling and storing equipment, materials and supplies.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XVII-A. Uniform Construction Code, Property Maintenance Code and Reserved Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66702-A. Primacy of Uniform Construction Code
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XVII-A. Uniform Construction Code, Property Maintenance Code and Reserved Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66702-A. Primacy of Uniform Construction Code
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66702-A. Primacy of Uniform Construction Code (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The Uniform Construction Code shall apply to the construction, alteration, repair
      and occupancy of all buildings and structures within a township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XVII-A. Uniform Construction Code, Property Maintenance Code and Reserved Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66703-A. Public nuisance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XVII-A. Uniform Construction Code, Property Maintenance Code and Reserved Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66703-A. Public nuisance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66703-A. Public nuisance (2023)
content:
A building, housing or property, or part of a building, housing or property erected,
   altered, extended, reconstructed, removed or maintained, contrary to a provision of
   an ordinance passed for a purpose specified in this article may be declared, by a
   court of law, a public nuisance, and may be abatable as such.  However, a violation of the Uniform Construction Code or an ordinance that equals
   or exceeds the Uniform Construction Code shall be subject to the provisions of the
   act of November 10, 1999 (P.L. 491, No. 45),1known as the Pennsylvania Construction Code Act, and the regulations adopted thereunder
   by the Department of Labor and Industry relating to enforcement for noncompliance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XV. Corporate Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66553. Emergency services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XV. Corporate Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66553. Emergency services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66553. Emergency services (2023)
content:
(a) The township shall be responsible for ensuring that fire and emergency medical
      services are provided within the township by the means and to the extent determined
      by the township, including the appropriate financial and administrative assistance
      for these services.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XVII-A. Uniform Construction Code, Property Maintenance Code and Reserved Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66704-A. Property maintenance code
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XVII-A. Uniform Construction Code, Property Maintenance Code and Reserved Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66704-A. Property maintenance code
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66704-A. Property maintenance code (2023)
content:
(a) Property maintenance code.--Notwithstanding the primacy of the Uniform Construction Code, the township supervisors
      may enact a property maintenance ordinance, and they may incorporate a standard or
      nationally recognized property maintenance code, or a variation or change or part
      of the code, published and printed in book form, without incorporating the text of
      the code in the ordinance, or the supervisors may enact a standard or nationally recognized
      property maintenance code or a change or variation or part, as the ordinance.  In either event, the proposed ordinance, or a brief summary of the proposed ordinance,
      shall be published not more than 60 days nor less than seven days before passage at
      least once in one newspaper circulating generally in the township.  The notice shall state the time and place of the meeting and the particular nature
      of the ordinance to be considered.  The notice shall also state where copies of the proposed ordinance and property
      maintenance code can be examined or obtained at cost.  A property maintenance code adopted by reference need not be recorded in or attached
      to the ordinance book, but shall be deemed to have been legally recorded if the ordinance
      by which the code was adopted by reference shall have been recorded, with an accompanying
      notation stating where the full text of the code has been filed.  The ordinance may provide for reasonable property fines and penalties for violations
      of the ordinance.  The procedure under this section relating to the adoption of the ordinance may likewise
      be utilized in amending, supplementing or repealing a provision of the ordinance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XVI. Ordinances›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66601. Ordinances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XVI. Ordinances › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66601. Ordinances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66601. Ordinances (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors may adopt ordinances in which general or specific powers
      of the township may be exercised, and, by the enactment of subsequent ordinances,
      the board of supervisors may amend, repeal or revise existing ordinances.  All proposed ordinances, whether original, amended, repealed, revised, consolidated
      or codified, shall be published not more than sixty days nor less than seven days
      before passage at least once in one newspaper circulating generally in the township.  Public notices shall include either the full text or a brief summary of the proposed
      ordinance which lists the provisions in reasonable detail and a reference to a place
      within the township where copies of the proposed ordinance may be examined.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XVII-A. Uniform Construction Code, Property Maintenance Code and Reserved Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66705-A. Reserved powers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XVII-A. Uniform Construction Code, Property Maintenance Code and Reserved Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66705-A. Reserved powers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66705-A. Reserved powers (2023)
content:
If, as a result of legislative action or final order of court for which the time for
   appeal has expired and no appeal has been taken or from which there is no pending
   appeal, the Uniform Construction Code or a replacement code is no longer applicable
   in townships, the township supervisors may:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XVII-A. Uniform Construction Code, Property Maintenance Code and Reserved Powers›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66701-A. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XVII-A. Uniform Construction Code, Property Maintenance Code and Reserved Powers › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66701-A. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66701-A. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this article shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XVIII. Fire Prevention and Protection›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66801. Authority of board of supervisors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XVIII. Fire Prevention and Protection › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66801. Authority of board of supervisors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66801. Authority of board of supervisors (2023)
content: The board of supervisors may provide for fire protection within the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XVIII. Fire Prevention and Protection›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66802. Fire hydrants and water supply
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XVIII. Fire Prevention and Protection › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66802. Fire hydrants and water supply
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66802. Fire hydrants and water supply (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors may place, replace, operate, maintain and repair or contract
      with water companies or municipal authorities for the placing, replacing, operating,
      maintaining and repairing of fire hydrants to water mains, maintaining pressures approved
      by fire insurance underwriters along highways, streets, roads and alleys within the
      township or provide for or acquire a water supply system equipped to supply sufficient
      water for the protection of property from fire.  The moneys necessary for providing or acquiring these fire protection services may
      be obtained by one of the following methods:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XVII. Public Buildings›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66703. How damages are assessed
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XVII. Public Buildings › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66703. How damages are assessed
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66703. How damages are assessed (2023)
content:
The compensation and damages arising from taking, using and appropriating private
   or public property for township purposes shall be ascertained, determined, awarded
   and paid under this act for eminent domain proceedings.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XVIII. Fire Prevention and Protection›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66803. Fire companies, facilities and training
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XVIII. Fire Prevention and Protection › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66803. Fire companies, facilities and training
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66803. Fire companies, facilities and training (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors may appropriate moneys for the use of the township or
      to fire companies located in the township for the operation and maintenance of fire
      companies, for the purchase and maintenance of fire apparatus, for the construction,
      repair and maintenance of fire company houses, for training of fire company personnel
      and, as set forth in this section, for fire training schools or centers in order to
      secure fire protection for the inhabitants of the township.  The fire companies shall submit to the board of supervisors an annual report of
      the use of the appropriated moneys for each completed year of the township before
      any further payments may be made to the fire companies for the current year.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XVIII. Fire Prevention and Protection›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66804. Ponds, dams or impoundments for fire protection
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XVIII. Fire Prevention and Protection › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66804. Ponds, dams or impoundments for fire protection
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66804. Ponds, dams or impoundments for fire protection (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may construct or contribute moneys for or participate in
   the construction of, ponds, dams or other impoundments to provide water for fire protection
   for the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XVIII. Fire Prevention and Protection›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66805. Fire Prevention code
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XVIII. Fire Prevention and Protection › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66805. Fire Prevention code
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66805. Fire Prevention code (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may adopt any standard fire prevention code published and
   printed in book form as provided under this act for adopting standard codes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XIX. Township Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66901. Creating or disbanding police force
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XIX. Township Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66901. Creating or disbanding police force
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66901. Creating or disbanding police force (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may by resolution create or disband a police force within
   the township or, upon the petition of not less than twenty-five registered electors
   or taxpayers of the township, appoint police officers.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XIX. Township Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66903. Contracts to secure police service
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XIX. Township Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66903. Contracts to secure police service
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66903. Contracts to secure police service (2023)
content:
Any township may contract with any municipal corporation to secure the services within
   the township of the police of the municipal corporation.  When any contract is made, the police officers of the employing municipal corporation
   have all the powers and authority conferred by law on police officers in the township
   which has contracted to secure police service.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XIX. Township Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66906. Shield
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XIX. Township Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66906. Shield
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66906. Shield (2023)
content: Each police officer when on duty, shall wear a shield or badge with the words“township police”and the name of the township inscribed thereon.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XVIII. Fire Prevention and Protection›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66806. Prohibition of fire-producing devices in certain retail stores
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XVIII. Fire Prevention and Protection › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66806. Prohibition of fire-producing devices in certain retail stores
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66806. Prohibition of fire-producing devices in certain retail stores (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may by ordinance prohibit the smoking or carrying of lighted
   cigarettes, cigars, pipes or matches and the use of matches or fire-producing devices
   in retail stores arranged to accommodate one hundred persons or more or which employ
   ten or more employes.  Any ordinance passed under this section may not prohibit smoking in any restaurant
   room, rest room, beauty parlor, executive office or any shopping center area designated
   for smoking.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XIX. Township Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66905. Powers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XIX. Township Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66905. Powers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66905. Powers (2023)
content:
Each township police officer has those powers and abilities as are granted to police
   officers under the laws of this Commonwealth or the rules of the Supreme Court or
   the ordinances of the township for which a fine or penalty is imposed unless otherwise
   excepted in this act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XIX. Township Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66902. Appointment of police
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XIX. Township Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66902. Appointment of police
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66902. Appointment of police (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors shall provide for the organization and supervision and determine
   the number and the compensation of the police officers.  The position of police officer is incompatible with the office of supervisor, auditor,
   tax collector and manager.  The chairman of the board of supervisors may swear in police officers.  The board of supervisors may assign any police officer to undergo a course of training
   at any training school for police officers established or made available by the Federal
   or State Government and provide for payment of the officer's expenses while in attendance
   at the training school.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XIX. Township Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66909. Certain compensation prohibited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XIX. Township Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66909. Certain compensation prohibited
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66909. Certain compensation prohibited (2023)
content:
No police officer may charge or accept any fee or other compensation in addition to
   the salary paid by the township for any service rendered or performed by the police
   officer, except public rewards.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XIX. Township Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66904. Contract to provide police service
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XIX. Township Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66904. Contract to provide police service
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66904. Contract to provide police service (2023)
content:
Any township may contract with any municipal corporation to provide police services
   within the other municipal corporation.  When a contract is made, the township police have all the powers and authority conferred
   by law on police in the municipal corporation which has contracted to secure police
   service.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XIX. Township Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66912. Removal of police officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XIX. Township Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66912. Removal of police officers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66912. Removal of police officers (2023)
content:
No person employed as a regular full-time police officer in any police department,
   except officers appointed for a probationary period of one year or less, shall be
   suspended, removed or reduced in rank except under the act of June 15, 1951 (P.L.
   586, No. 144),1entitled “An act regulating the suspension, removal, furloughing and reinstatement
   of police officers in boroughs and townships of the first class having police forces
   of less than three members, and in townships of the second class.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XIX. Township Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66911. Police protection districts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XIX. Township Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66911. Police protection districts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66911. Police protection districts (2023)
content:
On petition of a majority of the property owners of any territory within the township,
   the board of supervisors may designate the territory as a district for the purpose
   of providing police protection.  The board of supervisors may annually assess the cost of the maintenance of the
   police protection by an equal assessment on all property benefited by the protection
   in proportion to the number of feet the property fronts on the street or highway or
   portion thereof to be protected.  The board of supervisors may provide for an equitable reduction from the frontage
   of lots at intersections or where, due to the irregular shape of lots, an assessment
   of the full frontage would be inequitable.  No assessment shall be made against any farmland, but vacant lots between built-up
   sections, whether tilled or not tilled, are not farmland.  The assessment for each foot front against vacant lots shall be only twenty-five
   percent of the assessment for each foot front against property with improvements.  All assessments for police protection shall be filed with the township tax collector
   under section 3301(a).1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XIX. Township Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66910. Police pension fund
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XIX. Township Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66910. Police pension fund
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66910. Police pension fund (2023)
content:
(a) In those townships maintaining police forces of less than three full-time police
      officers the board of supervisors may by ordinance or resolution establish a police
      pension fund or pension annuity into which each member of the police force may be
      required to pay a member contribution of an equal and proportionate charge which,
      except to the extent that section 607(c) of the act of December 18, 1984 (P.L. 1005,
      No. 205), known as the “Municipal Pension Plan Funding Standard and Recovery Act,”1applies, shall not exceed annually three percent of the pay of the member.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XIX. Township Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66907. Equipment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XIX. Township Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66907. Equipment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66907. Equipment (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may provide each police officer with a uniform, equipment
   and means of transportation and the maintenance thereof.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XIX. Township Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66913. Auxiliary police
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XIX. Township Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66913. Auxiliary police
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66913. Auxiliary police (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may confirm persons to serve as auxiliary police officers
   under the act of January 14, 1952 (1951 P.L. 2016, No. 561),1entitled “An act providing for supplementing the police forces of cities, boroughs,
   towns and townships, for the appointment, powers and control of auxiliary police therein,
   and for the transfer during disasters and emergencies of such auxiliary police, members
   of the regular police forces, and police equipment thereof.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XIX. Township Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66914. Special fire police
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XIX. Township Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66914. Special fire police
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66914. Special fire police (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may confirm any members of a volunteer fire company to serve
   as special fire police under the act of June 18, 1941 (P.L. 137, No. 74),1entitled, as amended, “An act providing for the appointment, powers and control of
   members of volunteer fire companies as special fire police, and conferring powers
   on them at fires attended by their fire companies in any city, borough, town, township
   or home rule municipality.”  The chairman of the board of supervisors may swear in special fire police officers.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XIX. Township Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66908. Lockups
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XIX. Township Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66908. Lockups
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66908. Lockups (2023)
content: The board of supervisors may provide lockup facilities.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XX. Street Lights›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67001. Lighting
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XX. Street Lights › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67001. Lighting
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67001. Lighting (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may light and illuminate the highways, roads and other public
   places of the township and remove, alter or improve lighting as may be appropriate
   and in the best interests of the township and make contracts for securing and maintaining
   a supply of light.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XIX. Township Police›PA ST 53 P.S. § 66915. School crossing guards
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XIX. Township Police › PA ST 53 P.S. § 66915. School crossing guards
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 66915. School crossing guards (2023)
content:
(a) Upon request of the board of school directors of a school district located wholly
      or partially within the township, the board of supervisors by resolution may appoint
      school crossing guards to control and direct traffic at or near schools.  The school crossing guards shall be in uniform and shall be authorized only in the
      management of traffic and pedestrians.  School crossing guards serve at the pleasure of the board of supervisors, except
      as provided in subsection (c), and are not eligible to join any township pension fund.  The board of supervisors shall determine the compensation of school crossing guards,
      to be paid by the township or jointly by the township and the school district in a
      ratio to be determined by the two boards.  If the township and school district cannot determine the ratio of compensation to
      be paid by each board, each board shall pay one-half of the compensation of the school
      crossing guards.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XX. Street Lights›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67002. Street light districts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XX. Street Lights › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67002. Street light districts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67002. Street light districts (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors may provide street lights and make regulations therefor
      within the township or within any district of the township established by the board
      of supervisors for that purpose.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXI. Solid Waste Collection and Disposition›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67103. Disposal
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXI. Solid Waste Collection and Disposition › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67103. Disposal
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67103. Disposal (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may dispose of, by contract or otherwise, ashes, garbage,
   solid waste and other refuse materials.  Any contract with the owner of a private facility for the disposal or incineration
   of ashes, garbage, solid waste and other refuse materials may be made for a period
   not exceeding twenty years.  This limitation does not apply to contracts with any county or municipal corporation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXI. Solid Waste Collection and Disposition›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67102. Collection
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXI. Solid Waste Collection and Disposition › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67102. Collection
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67102. Collection (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may collect and remove, by contract or otherwise, ashes,
   garbage, solid waste and other refuse materials and recyclables and prescribe penalties
   for the enforcement thereof.  Any contract with refuse haulers may be made for a period not exceeding five years.  This limitation does not apply to contracts with any other county or municipal corporation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXI. Solid Waste Collection and Disposition›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67105. Charge for services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXI. Solid Waste Collection and Disposition › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67105. Charge for services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67105. Charge for services (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may establish, alter, charge and collect rates and other
   charges for the collection, removal and disposal of ashes, garbage, solid waste, other
   refuse materials and recyclable materials, and the costs of including the payment
   of any indebtedness incurred for the construction, purchase, improvement, repair,
   maintenance and operation of any facilities therefor, and the amount due under any
   contract with any county or municipal corporation furnishing the services or facilities.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXI. Solid Waste Collection and Disposition›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67108. Exclusion from bidding requirements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXI. Solid Waste Collection and Disposition › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67108. Exclusion from bidding requirements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67108. Exclusion from bidding requirements (2023)
content:
A township shall not be subject to requirements otherwise imposed by law for the sale
   of personal property owned by the township when selling recyclable materials or materials
   separated, collected, recovered or created by recycling, as provided in the act of
   April 9, 1992 (P.L. 70, No. 21),1entitled “An act excluding the sale of recyclable material from political subdivision
   personal property sale restrictions relating to advertising and bidding.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXI. Solid Waste Collection and Disposition›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67104. Acquisition of land
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXI. Solid Waste Collection and Disposition › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67104. Acquisition of land
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67104. Acquisition of land (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may acquire any real property and erect, maintain, improve,
   operate and lease, either as lessor or lessee, facilities for incineration, landfill
   or other methods of disposal, either inside or outside the limits of the township,
   including equipment, either separately or jointly, with any county or municipal corporation
   in order to provide for the destruction, collection, removal and disposal of ashes,
   garbage, solid waste or other refuse materials, for the collection and storage of
   recyclable materials or for the composting of leaf and yard waste.  The board of supervisors may provide for the payment of the cost thereof out of
   the funds of the township.  The board of supervisors may acquire land for landfill purposes, either amicably
   or by exercising the power of eminent domain, and maintain lands and places for the
   dumping of ashes, garbage, solid waste and other refuse materials.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XX. Street Lights›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67003. Costs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XX. Street Lights › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67003. Costs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67003. Costs (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors may pay for the cost of public lighting by any one or
      a combination of the following means, whether the installation of the lighting was
      initiated by action of the board of supervisors or by petition:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXI. Solid Waste Collection and Disposition›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67107. Refuse collection district
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXI. Solid Waste Collection and Disposition › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67107. Refuse collection district
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67107. Refuse collection district (2023)
content:
On petition of a majority of the owners, occupants or tenants of any territory inside
   the township which is definitely defined, set apart and limited by the board of supervisors
   as a refuse collection district, either with township employes and facilities or with
   independent contractors, the board of supervisors may provide for the removal from
   the refuse collection district of ashes, garbage, solid waste or other refuse materials
   and for the disposal thereof, including the collection and marketing of recyclable
   materials.  The board of supervisors may levy an assessment upon all owners, occupants or tenants
   of the district sufficient to defray the cost of the removal, disposal or marketing
   under section 3301(b).1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXII. Parks, Recreation Centers and Forests›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67201. Acquisition of lands and buildings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXII. Parks, Recreation Centers and Forests › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67201. Acquisition of lands and buildings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67201. Acquisition of lands and buildings (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may designate lands or buildings owned, leased or controlled
   by the township for use as parks, playgrounds, playfields, gymnasiums, swimming pools,
   indoor recreation centers, public parks and other recreation areas and facilities
   and acquire lands or buildings by lease, gift, devise, purchase or by the exercise
   of the right of eminent domain for recreational purposes and construct and equip facilities
   for recreational purposes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXII. Parks, Recreation Centers and Forests›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67203. Regulation of parks and public amusements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXII. Parks, Recreation Centers and Forests › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67203. Regulation of parks and public amusements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67203. Regulation of parks and public amusements (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors may by ordinance regulate the use and enjoyment by the
      public of any park or recreation grounds owned and operated by the township or charitable
      organizations for the use of the public.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXII. Parks, Recreation Centers and Forests›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67202. Recreation facilities employes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXII. Parks, Recreation Centers and Forests › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67202. Recreation facilities employes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67202. Recreation facilities employes (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may employ persons to maintain the recreation facilities
   or supervise the use of the recreation facilities.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXII. Parks, Recreation Centers and Forests›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67206. Expenses for maintenance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXII. Parks, Recreation Centers and Forests › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67206. Expenses for maintenance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67206. Expenses for maintenance (2023)
content:
All expenses incurred in the operation of parks, recreation areas and facilities are
   payable from the general township fund or from the treasury of the municipal corporations,
   counties or school districts under the agreement of the corporate authorities.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXI. Solid Waste Collection and Disposition›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67101. Accumulation of ashes, garbage, solid waste and refuse materials
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXI. Solid Waste Collection and Disposition › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67101. Accumulation of ashes, garbage, solid waste and refuse materials
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67101. Accumulation of ashes, garbage, solid waste and refuse materials (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors in the manner authorized by the act of July 7, 1980 (P.L.
   380, No. 97), known as the “Solid Waste Management Act,”1and the act of July 28, 1988 (P.L. 556, No. 101), known as the “Municipal Waste Planning,
   Recycling and Waste Reduction Act,”2may prohibit accumulations of ashes, garbage, solid waste and other refuse materials
   upon private property, including the imposition and collection of reasonable fees
   and charges for the collection, removal and disposal thereof.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXIII. Roads, Streets, Bridges and Highways›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67305. Hearing; report; exceptions thereto; view and notice
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXIII. Roads, Streets, Bridges and Highways › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67305. Hearing; report; exceptions thereto; view and notice
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67305. Hearing; report; exceptions thereto; view and notice (2023)
content:
(a) Before the passage of any ordinance for the laying out, opening, changing or vacating
      of any road or highway or section thereof, the board of supervisors shall give ten
      days' written notice to the owners of property adjacent to the road or portions thereof
      involved of the time and place set for a hearing on the proposed ordinance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXIII. Roads, Streets, Bridges and Highways›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67301. Road and bridge maintenance, repair and construction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXIII. Roads, Streets, Bridges and Highways › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67301. Road and bridge maintenance, repair and construction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67301. Road and bridge maintenance, repair and construction (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors may purchase or hire materials, equipment, machinery
      and implements necessary for the construction, repair and maintenance of roads and
      bridges and make and maintain bridges over streams, gullies, canals and railroads
      where bridges are necessary for the ease and safety of travelers.  The bridges shall be deemed to be a part of the road.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXII. Parks, Recreation Centers and Forests›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67204. Creation of recreation boards
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXII. Parks, Recreation Centers and Forests › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67204. Creation of recreation boards
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67204. Creation of recreation boards (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors may by ordinance create a recreation board to supervise,
      regulate, equip and maintain township-funded recreation programs and facilities.  The recreation board has only those powers specifically delegated to it by the board
      of supervisors.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXIII. Roads, Streets, Bridges and Highways›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67304. Power to lay out, open, widen, vacate, et cetera
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXIII. Roads, Streets, Bridges and Highways › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67304. Power to lay out, open, widen, vacate, et cetera
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67304. Power to lay out, open, widen, vacate, et cetera (2023)
content:
(a) The board of supervisors may by ordinance enact, ordain, survey, lay out, open,
      widen, straighten, vacate and relay all roads and bridges and parts thereof which
      are located wholly or partially within the township.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXII. Parks, Recreation Centers and Forests›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67205. Joint ownership and maintenance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXII. Parks, Recreation Centers and Forests › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67205. Joint ownership and maintenance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67205. Joint ownership and maintenance (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may join with any one or more municipal corporations, counties
   or school districts to acquire, create, equip, maintain and operate any park or recreation
   area to serve residents of the township under the act of July 12, 1972 (P.L. 762,
   No. 180), referred to as the Intergovernmental Cooperation Law.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXI. Solid Waste Collection and Disposition›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67106. Appropriations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXI. Solid Waste Collection and Disposition › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67106. Appropriations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67106. Appropriations (2023)
content:
The board of supervisors may make appropriations to any county or municipal corporation
   for the construction, purchase, improvement, repair, maintenance and operation of
   any facilities for the collection, removal, disposal or marketing of ashes, garbage,
   solid waste, other refuse materials, recyclable materials or composted leaf and yard
   waste.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXII. Parks, Recreation Centers and Forests›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67207. Forest lands
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXII. Parks, Recreation Centers and Forests › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67207. Forest lands
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67207. Forest lands (2023)
content:
(a) Townships may acquire, by purchase, gift or lease, and hold tracts of land covered
      with forest or tree growth, or suitable for the growth of trees, and administer the
      tracts under the direction of the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources.  The tracts may be of any size suitable for the purpose and may be located inside
      or outside the township limits.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXIII. Roads, Streets, Bridges and Highways›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67302. Duties of roadmasters
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXIII. Roads, Streets, Bridges and Highways › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67302. Duties of roadmasters
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67302. Duties of roadmasters (2023)
content: The roadmasters shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXIII. Roads, Streets, Bridges and Highways›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67303. Road complaints
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXIII. Roads, Streets, Bridges and Highways › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67303. Road complaints
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67303. Road complaints (2023)
content:
If any complaint alleges that the public roads and highways of any township are not
   maintained in accordance with law, the court may appoint three persons who shall examine
   the highways and report the findings to the court.  In these cases, the complainants shall first enter security, in a sum as the court
   may fix, to pay all costs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXIII. Roads, Streets, Bridges and Highways›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67306. Width of public roads
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations › Part X. Townships of the Second Class › Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code › Article XXIII. Roads, Streets, Bridges and Highways › PA ST 53 P.S. § 67306. Width of public roads
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 53 P.S. § 67306. Width of public roads (2023)
content:
The width of the right-of-way of a public road in townships shall not be less than
   thirty-three feet or more than one hundred and twenty feet, and the width of the right-of-way
   of alleys opened by the township as public roads shall not be less than fifteen feet.  The minimum required width shall be in addition to any width required for necessary
   slopes in cuts or fills.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 53 P.S. Municipal and Quasi-Municipal Corporations›Part X. Townships of the Second Class›Chapter 141. Second Class Township Code›Article XXIII. Roads, Streets, Bridges and Highways›PA ST 53 P.S. § 67312. Elimination of curves; acquisition of views
